  6. The system account rule. Only deposits may draw from External funding. Without this check, anyone could send a transfer from the bank's own account and create money out of thin air. Asking "what if I use an account I shouldn't control?" is exactly the kind of test a fintech QA is paid to think of.
  7. The balance check runs after the lock, so it sees the real current balance.
  8. The inserts write the transfer record, then two ledger entries: minus from the sender, plus to the receiver.
  9. COMMIT makes all of it permanent at once. If anything above threw an error, catch runs ROLLBACK and nothing is saved.
  10. finally returns the connection to the pool whether the transfer succeeded or failed. Forgetting this leaks connections until the API stops answering.

Two smaller pieces:

  • AppError carries an HTTP status and a stable code such as insufficient_funds. Clients and tests check the code, never the message, so messages can be reworded without breaking anyone.
  • toCents exists because Postgres bigint can hold numbers JavaScript can't represent exactly, so the pg library hands them back as text. Ledgerline's amounts are far below that limit, so it converts them, but refuses loudly if a value ever isn't a safe whole number.

Commit with git add -A && git commit -m "Step 10: Ledger".

Step 11: Routes for accounts, deposits and transfers

About an hour.

What, why and how: JSON Schema and request validation

What it is. JSON Schema is a standard way to describe what valid JSON looks like: which fields are required, what type each one is, and which values are allowed. Fastify checks every request's body against the schema you give each route.

Why we use it. Validation at the door means bad input never reaches your code. A missing field, text where a number belongs, or a negative amount each gets a 400 with a clear message, and your handler can trust whatever it receives.

How we use it. Each route has a schema with a body or params section. required lists mandatory fields, type sets each field's type, minimum and maximum bound numbers, format: "uuid" checks ids, and additionalProperties: false refuses unknown fields. Week 3 uses the same standard for the API's contract.

How it works inside. When the API starts, Fastify hands each route's schema to a library called Ajv, which compiles it into a small JavaScript function that checks exactly those rules. Every request body then goes through that function before the handler runs, so validation costs almost nothing per request. When a rule fails, Ajv reports where and why, like body/amountCents must be integer, and Fastify turns that into a 400.

Routes connect URLs to code. Each route here also gets a JSON Schema: a description of what a valid request looks like. Fastify checks every request against it before your code runs, and rejects anything that doesn't match with a 400.

Create src/routes/schemas.ts:

src/routes/schemas.ts
// JSON Schemas Fastify uses to validate requests before our code runs.
// Anything that doesn't match gets a 400 automatically.

export const idParams = {
  type: "object",
  required: ["id"],
  properties: { id: { type: "string", format: "uuid" } },
} as const;

export const amountCents = {
  type: "integer",
  minimum: 1,
  maximum: 100_000_000, // $1,000,000.00 per transfer
} as const;

Create src/routes/accounts.ts:

src/routes/accounts.ts
import type { FastifyInstance } from "fastify";
import { pool } from "../db";
import { notFound } from "../errors";
import { FUNDING_ACCOUNT_ID, getBalance, moveMoney } from "../ledger";
import { amountCents, idParams } from "./schemas";

interface AccountRow {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  type: string;
  created_at: Date;
}

async function loadAccount(id: string) {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<AccountRow>(
    "SELECT id, name, type, created_at FROM accounts WHERE id = $1",
    [id],
  );
  if (rows.length === 0) throw notFound("account", id);
  const account = rows[0];
  return {
    id: account.id,
    name: account.name,
    type: account.type,
    balanceCents: await getBalance(pool, account.id),
    createdAt: account.created_at.toISOString(),
  };
}

export async function accountRoutes(app: FastifyInstance) {
  app.post<{ Body: { name: string } }>(
    "/accounts",
    {
      schema: {
        body: {
          type: "object",
          required: ["name"],
          additionalProperties: false,
          properties: {
            name: { type: "string", minLength: 1, maxLength: 100 },
          },
        },
      },
    },
    async (request, reply) => {
      const { rows } = await pool.query<{ id: string }>(
        "INSERT INTO accounts (name) VALUES ($1) RETURNING id",
        [request.body.name],
      );
      return reply.code(201).send(await loadAccount(rows[0].id));
    },
  );

  app.get<{ Params: { id: string } }>(
    "/accounts/:id",
    { schema: { params: idParams } },
    async (request) => loadAccount(request.params.id),
  );

  app.post<{ Params: { id: string }; Body: { amountCents: number } }>(
    "/accounts/:id/deposits",
    {
      schema: {
        params: idParams,
        body: {
          type: "object",
          required: ["amountCents"],
          additionalProperties: false,
          properties: { amountCents },
        },
      },
    },
    async (request, reply) => {
      const transfer = await moveMoney({
        kind: "deposit",
        fromAccountId: FUNDING_ACCOUNT_ID,
        toAccountId: request.params.id,
        amountCents: request.body.amountCents,
      });
      return reply.code(201).send(transfer);
    },
  );
}

Create src/routes/transfers.ts:

src/routes/transfers.ts
import type { FastifyInstance } from "fastify";
import { getTransfer, moveMoney } from "../ledger";
import { amountCents, idParams } from "./schemas";

interface CreateTransferBody {
  fromAccountId: string;
  toAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
}

export async function transferRoutes(app: FastifyInstance) {
  app.post<{ Body: CreateTransferBody }>(
    "/transfers",
    {
      schema: {
        body: {
          type: "object",
          required: ["fromAccountId", "toAccountId", "amountCents"],
          additionalProperties: false,
          properties: {
            fromAccountId: { type: "string", format: "uuid" },
            toAccountId: { type: "string", format: "uuid" },
            amountCents,
          },
        },
      },
    },
    async (request, reply) => {
      const transfer = await moveMoney({ kind: "internal", ...request.body });
      return reply.code(201).send(transfer);
    },
  );

  app.get<{ Params: { id: string } }>(
    "/transfers/:id",
    { schema: { params: idParams } },
    async (request) => getTransfer(request.params.id),
  );
}

Replace src/app.ts:

src/app.ts
import Fastify, { type FastifyError } from "fastify";
import { pool } from "./db";
import { AppError } from "./errors";
import { accountRoutes } from "./routes/accounts";
import { transferRoutes } from "./routes/transfers";

export function buildApp() {
  const app = Fastify({
    logger: true,
    ajv: {
      customOptions: {
        // Fastify's defaults quietly turn "2500" into 2500 and drop unknown
        // fields. For money we want strict: wrong types and extra fields fail.
        coerceTypes: false,
        removeAdditional: false,
      },
    },
  });

  app.get("/health", async (request, reply) => {
    try {
      await pool.query("SELECT 1");
      return { status: "ok", database: "up" };
    } catch (error) {
      request.log.error({ err: error }, "database health check failed");
      return reply.code(503).send({ status: "degraded", database: "down" });
    }
  });

  app.register(accountRoutes);
  app.register(transferRoutes);

  // Every error leaves the API in the same shape: { error, message }.
  app.setErrorHandler<FastifyError>((error, request, reply) => {
    if (error instanceof AppError) {
      return reply
        .code(error.statusCode)
        .send({ error: error.code, message: error.message });
    }
    if (error.validation) {
      return reply
        .code(400)
        .send({ error: "validation_error", message: error.message });
    }
    if (error.statusCode && error.statusCode < 500) {
      // Things like malformed JSON, which Fastify rejects before our code runs.
      return reply
        .code(error.statusCode)
        .send({ error: "bad_request", message: error.message });
    }
    request.log.error({ err: error }, "unhandled error");
    return reply
      .code(500)
      .send({ error: "internal_error", message: "Something went wrong" });
  });

  app.setNotFoundHandler((request, reply) => {
    reply.code(404).send({
      error: "route_not_found",
      message: `No route for ${request.method} ${request.url}`,
    });
  });

  return app;
}

npm run typecheck
npm run lint

What the code does

  • The endpoints. POST /accounts opens an account, GET /accounts/:id returns one with its balance, POST /accounts/:id/deposits adds money, POST /transfers moves money, and GET /transfers/:id returns a transfer. :id is a placeholder filled in from the URL.
  • as const tells TypeScript to treat the schema objects as fixed values, which Fastify needs in order to read them precisely.
  • app.post<{ Body: CreateTransferBody }> tells TypeScript what request.body contains, so your editor autocompletes it and catches typos.
  • reply.code(201) means Created. The tests check for it.
  • app.register plugs each group of routes into the app.
  • The error handler gives every error the same shape: { "error": "code", "message": "text" }. An AppError keeps its own status and code, schema failures become validation_error, Fastify's own rejections (like malformed JSON) become bad_request, and anything unexpected becomes a 500 that's logged but doesn't leak internal details.
  • The not-found handler gives unknown URLs the same error shape.

Found while testing this guide

Look at the ajv options near the top of app.ts. Fastify's defaults are friendly, and for a banking API, too friendly. I checked: with the defaults, a transfer body of {"amountCents": "2500", "memo": "extra"} is accepted. The text "2500" is quietly converted into the number 2500, and the unknown memo field is silently thrown away. A client sending the wrong type, or a field it believes does something, deserves to hear about it. coerceTypes: false and removeAdditional: false make the API refuse both, and Step 13 has tests that hold it to that. Framework defaults are a great place to hunt for bugs.

Commit with git add -A && git commit -m "Step 11: Routes".

Step 12: Explore it by hand

About 30 minutes.

What, why and how: curl and jq

What it is. curl sends HTTP requests from the terminal. jq reads JSON, and either pretty-prints it or pulls out one field.

Why we use it. Poking at an API by hand is the fastest way to explore it before automating anything. And a curl command can go straight into a bug report, so anyone can reproduce the problem.

How we use it. In curl, -X POST sets the method, -H 'name: value' adds a header, -d '...' sends a body, -s hides progress output, and -i shows the status line and headers. Piping into jq, as in curl ... | jq, formats the response. jq .balanceCents pulls out one field, and jq -r .id pulls it out without quotes, ready to keep in a shell variable.

How it works inside. curl opens a connection to the server, writes out the request text described in the API primer, and prints whatever comes back. -i just shows the response's status line and headers as well. jq parses JSON into a tree and runs a small query language over it: .balanceCents means "the field called balanceCents at the top level".

Before automating anything, poke at it. Exploratory testing finds the things you didn't know to write tests for, and it tells you what the automated tests should check.

jq pretty-prints JSON and pulls fields out of it. On a Mac you installed it in Step 1; on Windows, install it now: 

sudo apt install jq -y

Start the API with npm run dev. In a second terminal, create two accounts and keep their ids in the shell variables A and B: 

A=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:3000/accounts -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Kali Bakery"}' | jq -r .id)
B=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:3000/accounts -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Flour Supplier"}' | jq -r .id)
echo $A $B

Deposit $100 into the bakery, send the supplier $25, then check both balances: 

curl -s -X POST localhost:3000/accounts/$A/deposits -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"amountCents":10000}' | jq
curl -s -X POST localhost:3000/transfers -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"fromAccountId\":\"$A\",\"toAccountId\":\"$B\",\"amountCents\":2500}" | jq
curl -s localhost:3000/accounts/$A | jq .balanceCents
curl -s localhost:3000/accounts/$B | jq .balanceCents

You should see 7500 and 2500. Now look at the ledger rows those calls wrote: 

docker compose exec postgres psql -U ledgerline -d ledgerline -c "SELECT transfer_id, account_id, amount_cents FROM ledger_entries ORDER BY id;"

Try to break it

Send each of these, building the curl from the ones above, and check you get the result in brackets:

  • Transfer more than the bakery has (422 insufficient_funds, with a message showing the balance).
  • Send "amountCents":"100" as text (400 validation_error).
  • Add an extra field, like "memo":"x" (400 validation_error).
  • Send broken JSON, such as -d '{bad json' (400 bad_request).
  • Get /accounts/not-a-uuid (400), then a well-formed id that doesn't exist (404 account_not_found).
  • Transfer from $A to $A (422 same_account).
  • Transfer from 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001, the funding account (422 account_not_allowed).

Write down anything that surprised you in your dev log, then stop the server with Ctrl+C.

Heads up

From Week 3, the API needs an API key, so curl commands like these will need -H 'x-api-key: local-dev-key' added.

Step 13: API tests for money movement

About two hours.

Now turn what you explored into automated tests. Start with a few helper functions so the tests read clearly. In Week 3 you'll grow these into a proper framework.

Create tests/api/support/api.ts:

tests/api/support/api.ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { expect, type APIRequestContext } from "@playwright/test";

// The shapes our API returns. Week 3 checks these against a formal contract.
export interface Account {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  type: string;
  balanceCents: number;
  createdAt: string;
}

export interface Transfer {
  id: string;
  kind: string;
  fromAccountId: string;
  toAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  status: string;
  createdAt: string;
}

// Each test makes its own accounts with unique names, so tests never share
// data and can run in parallel, in any order.
export async function createAccount(
  request: APIRequestContext,
  name = `Test business ${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`,
): Promise<Account> {
  const response = await request.post("/accounts", { data: { name } });
  expect(response.status(), await response.text()).toBe(201);
  return response.json();
}

export async function getAccount(
  request: APIRequestContext,
  id: string,
): Promise<Account> {
  const response = await request.get(`/accounts/${id}`);
  expect(response.status(), await response.text()).toBe(200);
  return response.json();
}

export async function deposit(
  request: APIRequestContext,
  accountId: string,
  amountCents: number,
): Promise<Transfer> {
  const response = await request.post(`/accounts/${accountId}/deposits`, {
    data: { amountCents },
  });
  expect(response.status(), await response.text()).toBe(201);
  return response.json();
}

export async function createFundedAccount(
  request: APIRequestContext,
  balanceCents: number,
): Promise<Account> {
  const account = await createAccount(request);
  if (balanceCents > 0) await deposit(request, account.id, balanceCents);
  return getAccount(request, account.id);
}

export async function balanceOf(
  request: APIRequestContext,
  accountId: string,
): Promise<number> {
  return (await getAccount(request, accountId)).balanceCents;
}

Create tests/api/accounts.spec.ts:

tests/api/accounts.spec.ts
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { balanceOf, createAccount, deposit, type Account } from "./support/api";

test.describe("accounts", () => {
  test("a new account starts with a zero balance", async ({ request }) => {
    const account = await createAccount(request, "Kali's Bakery");

    expect(account).toMatchObject({
      name: "Kali's Bakery",
      type: "customer",
      balanceCents: 0,
    });
  });

  test("an account can be fetched by id", async ({ request }) => {
    const created = await createAccount(request);

    const response = await request.get(`/accounts/${created.id}`);

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect((await response.json()) as Account).toEqual(created);
  });

  test("deposits increase the balance", async ({ request }) => {
    const account = await createAccount(request);

    await deposit(request, account.id, 5_000);
    await deposit(request, account.id, 1_250);

    expect(await balanceOf(request, account.id)).toBe(6_250);
  });

  test("an unknown account returns 404", async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get(
      "/accounts/7b1f2c3d-0000-4000-8000-000000000000",
    );

    expect(response.status()).toBe(404);
    expect(await response.json()).toMatchObject({ error: "account_not_found" });
  });

  test("a malformed account id returns 400", async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get("/accounts/not-a-uuid");

    expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
    expect(await response.json()).toMatchObject({ error: "validation_error" });
  });

  test("an account needs a name", async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.post("/accounts", { data: {} });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
    expect(await response.json()).toMatchObject({ error: "validation_error" });
  });
});

Create tests/api/transfers.spec.ts:

tests/api/transfers.spec.ts
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import {
  balanceOf,
  createAccount,
  createFundedAccount,
  type Transfer,
} from "./support/api";

const FUNDING_ACCOUNT_ID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001";

test.describe("transfers between accounts", () => {
  test("moves money from one account to another", async ({ request }) => {
    const from = await createFundedAccount(request, 10_000);
    const to = await createAccount(request);

    const response = await request.post("/transfers", {
      data: { fromAccountId: from.id, toAccountId: to.id, amountCents: 2_500 },
    });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(201);
    expect(await response.json()).toMatchObject({
      kind: "internal",
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      status: "completed",
    });
    expect(await balanceOf(request, from.id)).toBe(7_500);
    expect(await balanceOf(request, to.id)).toBe(2_500);
  });

  test("a transfer can be fetched by id", async ({ request }) => {
    const from = await createFundedAccount(request, 1_000);
    const to = await createAccount(request);
    const created = await request.post("/transfers", {
      data: { fromAccountId: from.id, toAccountId: to.id, amountCents: 300 },
    });
    const transfer = (await created.json()) as Transfer;

    const response = await request.get(`/transfers/${transfer.id}`);

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(await response.json()).toEqual(transfer);
  });

  test("allows spending the exact balance", async ({ request }) => {
    const from = await createFundedAccount(request, 1_000);
    const to = await createAccount(request);

    const response = await request.post("/transfers", {
      data: { fromAccountId: from.id, toAccountId: to.id, amountCents: 1_000 },
    });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(201);
    expect(await balanceOf(request, from.id)).toBe(0);
  });

  test("rejects a transfer one cent over the balance and changes nothing", async ({
    request,
  }) => {
    const from = await createFundedAccount(request, 1_000);
    const to = await createAccount(request);

    const response = await request.post("/transfers", {
      data: { fromAccountId: from.id, toAccountId: to.id, amountCents: 1_001 },
    });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(422);
    expect(await response.json()).toMatchObject({
      error: "insufficient_funds",
    });
    expect(await balanceOf(request, from.id)).toBe(1_000);
    expect(await balanceOf(request, to.id)).toBe(0);
  });

  test("rejects sending money to the same account", async ({ request }) => {
    const account = await createFundedAccount(request, 1_000);

    const response = await request.post("/transfers", {
      data: {
        fromAccountId: account.id,
        toAccountId: account.id,
        amountCents: 100,
      },
    });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(422);
    expect(await response.json()).toMatchObject({ error: "same_account" });
  });

  test("won't let anyone spend from the system funding account", async ({
    request,
  }) => {
    const to = await createAccount(request);

    const response = await request.post("/transfers", {
      data: {
        fromAccountId: FUNDING_ACCOUNT_ID,
        toAccountId: to.id,
        amountCents: 1_000_000,
      },
    });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(422);
    expect(await response.json()).toMatchObject({
      error: "account_not_allowed",
    });
    expect(await balanceOf(request, to.id)).toBe(0);
  });

  test("returns 404 when an account doesn't exist", async ({ request }) => {
    const from = await createFundedAccount(request, 1_000);

    const response = await request.post("/transfers", {
      data: {
        fromAccountId: from.id,
        toAccountId: "7b1f2c3d-0000-4000-8000-000000000000",
        amountCents: 100,
      },
    });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(404);
    expect(await response.json()).toMatchObject({ error: "account_not_found" });
  });

  const invalidAmounts = [
    { label: "zero", amountCents: 0 },
    { label: "negative", amountCents: -500 },
    { label: "fractional cents", amountCents: 10.5 },
    { label: "a string", amountCents: "1000" },
    { label: "over the limit", amountCents: 100_000_001 },
  ];

  for (const { label, amountCents } of invalidAmounts) {
    test(`rejects an amount that is ${label}`, async ({ request }) => {
      const from = await createFundedAccount(request, 1_000);
      const to = await createAccount(request);

      const response = await request.post("/transfers", {
        data: { fromAccountId: from.id, toAccountId: to.id, amountCents },
      });

      expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
      expect(await response.json()).toMatchObject({
        error: "validation_error",
      });
      expect(await balanceOf(request, from.id)).toBe(1_000);
    });
  }

  test("rejects unknown fields instead of ignoring them", async ({
    request,
  }) => {
    const from = await createFundedAccount(request, 1_000);
    const to = await createAccount(request);

    const response = await request.post("/transfers", {
      data: {
        fromAccountId: from.id,
        toAccountId: to.id,
        amountCents: 100,
        memo: "not part of the API",
      },
    });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
  });

  test("rejects malformed JSON", async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.post("/transfers", {
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      // A Buffer is sent byte-for-byte. A plain string would be JSON-encoded
      // by Playwright into a valid JSON string, and the test would lie to us.
      data: Buffer.from("{not valid json"),
    });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
    expect(await response.json()).toMatchObject({ error: "bad_request" });
  });

  test("parallel transfers can't overdraw an account", async ({ request }) => {
    const from = await createFundedAccount(request, 10_000);
    const to = await createAccount(request);

    // Five $30 transfers fired at the same moment from a $100 account.
    const responses = await Promise.all(
      Array.from({ length: 5 }, () =>
        request.post("/transfers", {
          data: {
            fromAccountId: from.id,
            toAccountId: to.id,
            amountCents: 3_000,
          },
        }),
      ),
    );

    const statuses = responses.map((response) => response.status()).sort();
    expect(statuses).toEqual([201, 201, 201, 422, 422]);
    expect(await balanceOf(request, from.id)).toBe(1_000);
    expect(await balanceOf(request, to.id)).toBe(9_000);
  });
});

npm run test:api

You should see 23 passed: 2 health tests, 6 account tests and 15 transfer tests.

The edges these tests aim at, to nudge a cent at a time:

What makes these good payments tests

  • Unique data per test. Every test creates its own accounts with random names, so tests can run in parallel and in any order without stepping on each other.
  • expect(response.status(), await response.text()). The second argument is a message shown when the assertion fails. Here it's the response body, so a failure tells you why, not just "expected 201, received 400".
  • Boundaries in pairs. Spending the exact balance succeeds; one cent more fails. Bugs cluster at edges, so test both sides of each one.
  • "And changes nothing". Every rejected request checks that balances didn't move. In payments, a refusal that leaves partial damage behind is worse than no validation at all.
  • Table-driven negatives. Five invalid amounts, one loop, five separately named tests.
  • The funding account test turns Step 10's security rule into a permanent guarantee.

Found while testing this guide

My first version of the malformed-JSON test sent the broken text as a plain string, and it failed. Playwright had JSON-encoded my string into a perfectly valid JSON string, so the API received valid JSON and complained about something else. The fix is Buffer.from(...), which sends bytes exactly as written. The lesson is worth more than the fix: when a test fails in a way you didn't expect, check what the test actually sent before blaming the system.

Commit with git add -A && git commit -m "Step 13: Money movement tests".

Step 14: Concurrency and ledger integrity

About 90 minutes.

Two kinds of test finish the week. The parallel transfer test at the end of transfers.spec.ts proves the row lock works. Integrity tests check rules that must hold for every row in the database, no matter which test, or which bug, created it.

Create tests/api/support/db.ts:

tests/api/support/db.ts
import { Client } from "pg";

const DATABASE_URL =
  process.env.DATABASE_URL ??
  "postgres://ledgerline:ledgerline@localhost:5432/ledgerline";

// Opens a database connection, hands it to your code, and always closes it.
export async function withDb<T>(work: (db: Client) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  const db = new Client({ connectionString: DATABASE_URL });
  await db.connect();
  try {
    return await work(db);
  } finally {
    await db.end();
  }
}

Create tests/api/ledger.spec.ts:

tests/api/ledger.spec.ts
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { withDb } from "./support/db";

// These tests don't call the API. They check rules that must hold for every
// row in the database, including data created by every other test.

test.describe("ledger integrity", () => {
  test("every transfer has exactly two entries that sum to zero", async () => {
    await withDb(async (db) => {
      const { rows } = await db.query(`
        SELECT t.id, COUNT(e.id) AS entries, COALESCE(SUM(e.amount_cents), 0) AS total
        FROM transfers t
        LEFT JOIN ledger_entries e ON e.transfer_id = t.id
        GROUP BY t.id
        HAVING COUNT(e.id) <> 2 OR COALESCE(SUM(e.amount_cents), 0) <> 0
      `);
      expect(rows).toEqual([]);
    });
  });

  test("the whole ledger sums to zero", async () => {
    await withDb(async (db) => {
      const { rows } = await db.query(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents), 0)::text AS total FROM ledger_entries",
      );
      expect(rows[0].total).toBe("0");
    });
  });

  test("no customer account has a negative balance", async () => {
    await withDb(async (db) => {
      const { rows } = await db.query(`
        SELECT a.id, SUM(e.amount_cents) AS balance
        FROM accounts a
        JOIN ledger_entries e ON e.account_id = a.id
        WHERE a.type = 'customer'
        GROUP BY a.id
        HAVING SUM(e.amount_cents) < 0
      `);
      expect(rows).toEqual([]);
    });
  });
});

npm run test:api

26 passed.

The experiment: watch the race happen

Open src/ledger.ts and delete FOR UPDATE from the SELECT near the top of moveMoney, keeping ORDER BY id. Save, then run only the parallel test, ten times: 

npx playwright test -g "parallel transfers" --repeat-each 10

When I did this, all ten runs failed. Without the lock, several of the five $30 transfers read the same $100 balance, and they all got through. Now run the integrity tests: 

npx playwright test tests/api/ledger.spec.ts

"no customer account has a negative balance" fails too. The race really did overdraw accounts, and the damaged rows are still in your database. No test was written for those particular accounts, but the invariant caught the damage anyway. That's what integrity tests are for.

Put FOR UPDATE back, then:

npx playwright test -g "parallel transfers" --repeat-each 20
npm run db:reset
npm run test:api

You should see 20 passes, a clean database, then all 26 tests passing. --repeat-each is also how you'll hunt flaky tests in Week 9.

What the integrity queries check

  • Unbalanced transfers. LEFT JOIN keeps transfers even when they have no entries, and HAVING keeps only the ones with anything other than two entries summing to zero. The test expects none.
  • The whole ledger. The sum of every entry ever written must be zero.
  • Negative customer balances. Any customer account below zero is a bug.

withDb opens a connection, hands it to your code, and always closes it, even when an assertion fails. You'll replace it with something better in Week 3.

Update CI

The pipeline needs the tables too. Replace .github/workflows/ci.yml:

.github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: ledgerline
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ledgerline
          POSTGRES_DB: ledgerline
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U ledgerline -d ledgerline"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm

      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run format:check
      - run: npm run test:unit
      - run: npm run db:migrate
      - run: npm run test:api

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: always()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 14

The only change is the npm run db:migrate step before the API tests. Push, and check that the run goes green: 

git add -A
git commit -m "Step 14: Concurrency and ledger integrity"
git push
gh run watch

Verify on your machine

Pass: a green run, where the npm run db:migrate step prints "Applied 001_create_accounts.sql" and "Applied 002_create_transfers_and_ledger.sql".

Fail: the API tests fail in CI but pass on your machine. Download the playwright-report artifact from the run, open it, and send me the first failure.

Week 2 wrap-up

  • Teach it back. Draw the ledger rows for a deposit and a transfer, then explain to an imaginary developer why removing FOR UPDATE breaks the parallel test.
  • Dev log. Write up the race experiment. It's one of your strongest interview stories.
  • The interview line. "I built a double-entry ledger and proved it holds under concurrency. I reproduced a race condition by removing a row lock, showed that it overdrew accounts, and added invariant tests that catch that whole class of damage."

Week 3: From tests to a framework

Your tests work, but they're a pile: URLs repeated in every file, response shapes only checked for the fields someone remembered, and a new database connection for every integrity test. This week turns them into a framework a developer could pick up without you, with layers, fixtures, a contract, authentication and a manual collection. Designing frameworks is the first thing Relay's posting asks for.

Step 15: The shape of a framework, and an API key

About an hour.

What, why and how: Authentication and API keys

What it is. Authentication answers the question "who is calling?". An API key is the simplest answer: a secret string the client sends in a header with every request, which the server compares with the one it expects.

Why we use it. No real banking API is open to anyone. Testing that the wrong key, or no key, is refused, and that a refused request changes nothing, is standard security testing.

How we use it. The API checks the x-api-key header in a hook that runs before every route except /health, and answers 401 if it doesn't match. The expected key comes from the API_KEY environment variable, and defaults to local-dev-key. Playwright sends it on every request through extraHTTPHeaders, and curl sends it with -H 'x-api-key: local-dev-key'. Real systems use stronger schemes, like OAuth tokens, but the testing questions are the same.

How it works inside. HTTP remembers nothing between requests, so the key travels in a header with every single one. The server checks it before any route runs. A plain comparison stops at the first character that differs, so in principle an attacker could time responses to guess a key one character at a time. That's why production systems compare secrets in constant time, as the webhook code does in Week 6, and store only a hash of each key, never the key itself.

Each layer solves one of those problems:

specs      what should happen, in plain words
fixtures   hand each test what it needs, and clean up after it
builders   create test data in one readable line
client     one method per endpoint, contract checked on every call
contract   openapi.yaml: what every response must look like
db helper  integrity questions asked of the database directly

Specs sit on top and only talk to the layers below them. When an endpoint changes, you fix the client once instead of every test.

Tap a layer to see its file and its one job:

Real APIs require authentication, and testing it is part of the job, so the API gets a simple API key first. Replace src/app.ts:

src/app.ts
import Fastify, { type FastifyError } from "fastify";
import { pool } from "./db";
import { AppError } from "./errors";
import { accountRoutes } from "./routes/accounts";
import { transferRoutes } from "./routes/transfers";

const API_KEY = process.env.API_KEY ?? "local-dev-key";

export function buildApp() {
  const app = Fastify({
    logger: true,
    ajv: {
      customOptions: {
        // Fastify's defaults quietly turn "2500" into 2500 and drop unknown
        // fields. For money we want strict: wrong types and extra fields fail.
        coerceTypes: false,
        removeAdditional: false,
      },
    },
  });

  // Every route except the health check needs the right x-api-key header.
  app.addHook("onRequest", async (request, reply) => {
    if (request.routeOptions.url === "/health") return;
    if (request.headers["x-api-key"] !== API_KEY) {
      return reply
        .code(401)
        .send({ error: "unauthorized", message: "Missing or invalid API key" });
    }
  });

  app.get("/health", async (request, reply) => {
    try {
      await pool.query("SELECT 1");
      return { status: "ok", database: "up" };
    } catch (error) {
      request.log.error({ err: error }, "database health check failed");
      return reply.code(503).send({ status: "degraded", database: "down" });
    }
  });

  app.register(accountRoutes);
  app.register(transferRoutes);

  // Every error leaves the API in the same shape: { error, message }.
  app.setErrorHandler<FastifyError>((error, request, reply) => {
    if (error instanceof AppError) {
      return reply
        .code(error.statusCode)
        .send({ error: error.code, message: error.message });
    }
    if (error.validation) {
      return reply
        .code(400)
        .send({ error: "validation_error", message: error.message });
    }
    if (error.statusCode && error.statusCode < 500) {
      // Things like malformed JSON, which Fastify rejects before our code runs.
      return reply
        .code(error.statusCode)
        .send({ error: "bad_request", message: error.message });
    }
    request.log.error({ err: error }, "unhandled error");
    return reply
      .code(500)
      .send({ error: "internal_error", message: "Something went wrong" });
  });

  app.setNotFoundHandler((request, reply) => {
    reply.code(404).send({
      error: "route_not_found",
      message: `No route for ${request.method} ${request.url}`,
    });
  });

  return app;
}

Replace playwright.config.ts. It now sends the key with every test request:

playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "@playwright/test";

const port = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000);
const baseURL = process.env.API_URL ?? `http://localhost:${port}`;

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: "tests/api",
  fullyParallel: true,
  forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI,
  retries: 0,
  reporter: [["list"], ["html", { open: "never" }]],
  use: {
    baseURL,
    // Sent with every request made through the request fixture.
    extraHTTPHeaders: { "x-api-key": process.env.API_KEY ?? "local-dev-key" },
  },
  webServer: {
    command: "npm run start",
    url: `${baseURL}/health`,
    reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
    timeout: 30_000,
  },
});

npm run test:api

All 26 still pass, because extraHTTPHeaders adds the key to every request the tests make. Now try without it. With npm run dev running: 

curl -s localhost:3000/accounts/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001
curl -s -H 'x-api-key: local-dev-key' localhost:3000/accounts/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001

The first returns {"error":"unauthorized",...}, and the second returns the funding account.

What the code does

  • An onRequest hook runs before every route. If the route isn't /health and the x-api-key header doesn't match, it answers 401 and the route never runs.
  • request.routeOptions.url is the matched route pattern, so /health?anything is still recognised as the health check.
  • process.env.API_KEY ?? "local-dev-key" means CI or production can set a real key without changing any code.

Heads up

A production API would store only hashed keys and compare them in constant time. For a local test project, a plain comparison keeps the focus on testing.

Commit with git add -A && git commit -m "Step 15: API key".

In a company

Keys and secrets never live in the code. local-dev-key is a default for your laptop only. A real service reads its secrets from a secrets manager when it starts, and each environment has different ones.

Step 16: Write the contract

About an hour.

What, why and how: OpenAPI

What it is. OpenAPI is a standard file format, written in YAML or JSON, that describes a REST API: every endpoint, what it accepts and what it returns, with data shapes written in JSON Schema. It's the REST equivalent of a SOAP WSDL.

Why we use it. It's the promise the API makes to everyone who calls it. Tools read it to generate documentation, client code and tests, and your framework uses it to check every response automatically.

How we use it. openapi.yaml sits in the project folder. paths lists the endpoints, and components/schemas defines each shape once, with $ref pointing back to it. Whenever the API's shape changes on purpose, the contract changes first. Paste the file into editor.swagger.io to see it as interactive documentation.

How it works inside. An OpenAPI file is just structured data. Nothing runs it; tools read it. Documentation sites turn it into pages, generators turn it into client code, and your framework feeds its schemas to a validator. A $ref is a pointer within the file, like #/components/schemas/Account, which is how one schema is shared by every endpoint that returns an account.

OpenAPI is a standard format for describing a REST API: every endpoint, what it accepts, and what it returns. It's the REST equivalent of the WSDL you asked about for SOAP. The contract lives separately from the code on purpose: if the code and the contract ever disagree, a test should fail, because mobile apps and partners build against the contract.

Create openapi.yaml in the project folder:

openapi.yaml
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Ledgerline API
  version: 0.3.0
  description: >
    Accounts, deposits and transfers for small businesses.
    All amounts are whole cents: 2500 means $25.00.

servers:
  - url: http://localhost:3000

security:
  - apiKey: []

paths:
  /health:
    get:
      summary: Check the API and its database
      security: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Everything is up
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/HealthStatus"
        "503":
          description: The database can't be reached
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/HealthStatus"

  /accounts:
    post:
      summary: Open an account
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [name]
              additionalProperties: false
              properties:
                name:
                  type: string
                  minLength: 1
                  maxLength: 100
      responses:
        "201":
          description: The new account
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Account"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"

  /accounts/{id}:
    get:
      summary: Get an account and its balance
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Id"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The account
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Account"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"

  /accounts/{id}/deposits:
    post:
      summary: Deposit money into an account
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Id"
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [amountCents]
              additionalProperties: false
              properties:
                amountCents:
                  $ref: "#/components/schemas/AmountCents"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: The deposit, recorded as a transfer
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Transfer"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "422":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"

  /transfers:
    post:
      summary: Move money between two customer accounts
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [fromAccountId, toAccountId, amountCents]
              additionalProperties: false
              properties:
                fromAccountId:
                  type: string
                  format: uuid
                toAccountId:
                  type: string
                  format: uuid
                amountCents:
                  $ref: "#/components/schemas/AmountCents"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: The completed transfer
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Transfer"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "422":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"

  /transfers/{id}:
    get:
      summary: Get a transfer
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Id"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The transfer
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Transfer"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"

components:
  securitySchemes:
    apiKey:
      type: apiKey
      in: header
      name: x-api-key

  parameters:
    Id:
      name: id
      in: path
      required: true
      schema:
        type: string
        format: uuid

  responses:
    Error:
      description: The request failed. `error` says why in a stable code.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"

  schemas:
    AmountCents:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100000000

    HealthStatus:
      type: object
      required: [status, database]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [ok, degraded]
        database:
          type: string
          enum: [up, down]

    Account:
      type: object
      required: [id, name, type, balanceCents, createdAt]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        name:
          type: string
        type:
          type: string
          enum: [customer, system]
        balanceCents:
          type: integer
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time

    Transfer:
      type: object
      required:
        [id, kind, fromAccountId, toAccountId, amountCents, status, createdAt]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        kind:
          type: string
          enum: [deposit, internal]
        fromAccountId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        toAccountId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        amountCents:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/AmountCents"
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [completed]
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time

    Error:
      type: object
      required: [error, message]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        error:
          type: string
          description: Stable code such as insufficient_funds
        message:
          type: string
          description: Human-readable explanation

To see it as interactive documentation, paste it into editor.swagger.io.

How to read it

  • paths lists each URL, then each method under it, with its requestBody and its possible responses by status code.
  • components/schemas defines each shape once (Account, Transfer, Error and HealthStatus), and $ref points at them. Change Account in one place and every endpoint that returns an account follows.
  • additionalProperties: false on response schemas means the API may not add undocumented fields without updating the contract first.
  • enum lists the only allowed values, and format: uuid and format: date-time describe the shape of ids and timestamps.
  • security requires the API key everywhere, and /health opts out with security: [].

Commit with git add -A && git commit -m "Step 16: OpenAPI contract".

Step 17: The contract validator and the API client

About 90 minutes.

What, why and how: Ajv, the validator

What it is. Ajv is a JavaScript library that takes a JSON Schema and checks data against it, listing every rule the data breaks.

Why we use it. It turns openapi.yaml from documentation into something that can fail a test. Every response the framework receives gets checked against it.

How we use it. contract.ts loads openapi.yaml into Ajv once. assertMatchesContract("Account", body, ...) finds the Account schema inside the file and throws a readable error if the body breaks it. The API client calls it for you on every response. Chapter 11 of the field guide has a live validator to experiment with.

How it works inside. Ajv compiles a schema into JavaScript code once, then runs that code for every check, which makes it one of the fastest validators available. The contract helper loads the whole OpenAPI file into Ajv under the name openapi, so a reference like openapi#/components/schemas/Account finds one schema inside it, and every $ref within that schema is followed automatically. With allErrors: true, Ajv keeps checking after the first problem, so a contract failure lists everything that's wrong at once. Try it: 

npm install -D ajv@8 ajv-formats@3 yaml@2
mkdir -p tests/framework

yaml reads the contract file, ajv is a JSON Schema validator, and ajv-formats teaches it formats like uuid and date-time.

Create tests/framework/types.ts:

tests/framework/types.ts
// TypeScript shapes for what the API returns. openapi.yaml is the source of
// truth; these just give your editor autocomplete.

export interface HealthStatus {
  status: "ok" | "degraded";
  database: "up" | "down";
}

export interface Account {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  type: "customer" | "system";
  balanceCents: number;
  createdAt: string;
}

export interface Transfer {
  id: string;
  kind: "deposit" | "internal";
  fromAccountId: string;
  toAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  status: "completed";
  createdAt: string;
}

export interface ApiErrorBody {
  error: string;
  message: string;
}

Create tests/framework/test-data.ts:

tests/framework/test-data.ts
// Fixed values tests share. Keep magic strings here, not scattered in specs.

export const FUNDING_ACCOUNT_ID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001";

// A valid UUID that will never exist in the database.

Create tests/framework/contract.ts:

tests/framework/contract.ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import Ajv2020 from "ajv/dist/2020";
import addFormats from "ajv-formats";
import { parse } from "yaml";

// Load openapi.yaml once and teach Ajv (a JSON Schema validator) about it.
const specPath = path.join(__dirname, "..", "..", "openapi.yaml");
const spec = parse(readFileSync(specPath, "utf8"));

// strict: false lets Ajv ignore OpenAPI-only keys like "paths" and "info".
const ajv = new Ajv2020({ allErrors: true, strict: false });
addFormats(ajv);
ajv.addSchema(spec, "openapi");

export type SchemaName = "Account" | "Transfer" | "Error" | "HealthStatus";

/** Throws a readable error if body doesn't match the named schema. */
export function assertMatchesContract(
  schemaName: SchemaName,
  body: unknown,
  context: string,
): void {
  const validate = ajv.getSchema(`openapi#/components/schemas/${schemaName}`);
  if (!validate) {
    throw new Error(`openapi.yaml has no schema called ${schemaName}`);
  }
  if (!validate(body)) {
    throw new Error(
      [
        `Contract violation: ${context}`,
        `Expected ${schemaName}: ${ajv.errorsText(validate.errors)}`,
        `Body: ${JSON.stringify(body, null, 2)}`,
      ].join("\n"),
    );
  }
}

Create tests/framework/ledgerline-client.ts:

tests/framework/ledgerline-client.ts
import type { APIRequestContext, APIResponse } from "@playwright/test";
import { assertMatchesContract, type SchemaName } from "./contract";
import type { Account, HealthStatus, Transfer } from "./types";

export interface ApiResult<T> {
  status: number;
  body: T;
}

// One method per endpoint. Tests talk to this class, never to raw URLs, so
// when an endpoint changes you fix it here once instead of in every test.
export class LedgerlineClient {
  constructor(private readonly request: APIRequestContext) {}

  health() {
    return this.send<HealthStatus>(
      this.request.get("/health"),
      "HealthStatus",
      "HealthStatus",
    );
  }

  createAccount(name: string) {
    return this.send<Account>(
      this.request.post("/accounts", { data: { name } }),
      "Account",
    );
  }

  getAccount(id: string) {
    return this.send<Account>(this.request.get(`/accounts/${id}`), "Account");
  }

  deposit(accountId: string, amountCents: unknown) {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.post(`/accounts/${accountId}/deposits`, {
        data: { amountCents },
      }),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  // Takes a loose object on purpose, so negative tests can send bad input.
  createTransfer(data: Record<string, unknown>) {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.post("/transfers", { data }),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  getTransfer(id: string) {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.get(`/transfers/${id}`),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  async balanceOf(accountId: string): Promise<number> {
    const { status, body } = await this.getAccount(accountId);
    if (status !== 200) {
      throw new Error(`Couldn't read balance of ${accountId}: HTTP ${status}`);
    }
    return body.balanceCents;
  }

  // Every response is checked against openapi.yaml before a test sees it:
  // successes against their resource schema, failures against Error.
  private async send<T>(
    pending: Promise<APIResponse>,
    successSchema: SchemaName,
    errorSchema: SchemaName = "Error",
  ): Promise<ApiResult<T>> {
    const response = await pending;
    const status = response.status();
    const body = await response.json();
    const context = `${response.url()} returned ${status}`;
    assertMatchesContract(
      response.ok() ? successSchema : errorSchema,
      body,
      context,
    );
    return { status, body };
  }
}

What the code does

  • Ajv2020 is the version of JSON Schema that OpenAPI 3.1 uses. strict: false lets Ajv ignore OpenAPI-only sections like paths and info.
  • ajv.addSchema(spec, "openapi") loads the whole file under the name openapi, so openapi#/components/schemas/Account points at one schema inside it.
  • assertMatchesContract throws an error that lists exactly what's wrong, plus the full body, so a failure is readable without a debugger.
  • The client has one method per endpoint. Every call goes through send(), which parses the JSON and checks it against the contract before the test ever sees it: success bodies against their own schema, everything else against Error. Every test now checks the contract, without anyone writing contract assertions.
  • Loose inputs, on purpose. deposit accepts amountCents: unknown and createTransfer accepts any object, so negative tests can still send text amounts and extra fields.

Run npm run typecheck, then commit.

Step 18: Builders, the database helper, assertions and fixtures

About 90 minutes.

What, why and how: Fixtures and builders

What it is. A fixture is something Playwright prepares for a test and cleans up afterwards, like an API client, a database connection or a fake bank. A builder is a helper that creates test data in one readable line, with sensible defaults for everything you don't mention.

Why we use it. Setup and cleanup are written once, in one place, instead of being repeated in every test. Tests shrink to what they're actually checking, and a change to setup is a one-file edit.

How we use it. fixtures.ts defines them. A test asks for what it needs by name, in its arguments: async ({ api, newAccount }) => .... Inside a fixture, code before use() is setup and code after it is cleanup. Worker-scoped fixtures are made once per worker process, and test-scoped ones are made fresh for every test. Chapter 12 of the field guide steps through that lifecycle.

How it works inside. Playwright reads the names in each test's braces, { api, newAccount }, and works out every fixture it needs, including the ones those depend on: newAccount needs api and db, and api needs request. It sets them up in dependency order, runs the test, then tears them down in reverse order, running the code after each use(). A worker-scoped fixture is built the first time a worker needs it, and kept until that worker exits. Step through one worker running two tests:

Create tests/framework/account-builder.ts:

tests/framework/account-builder.ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import type { LedgerlineClient } from "./ledgerline-client";
import type { Account } from "./types";

// Reads like a sentence in tests:
//   const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
// Defaults (a unique name, zero balance) cover everything you don't mention.
export class AccountBuilder {
  private name = `Test business ${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`;
  private balanceCents = 0;

  constructor(private readonly api: LedgerlineClient) {}

  named(name: string): this {
    this.name = name;
    return this;
  }

  withBalance(cents: number): this {
    this.balanceCents = cents;
    return this;
  }

  async create(): Promise<Account> {
    const created = await this.api.createAccount(this.name);
    if (created.status !== 201) {
      throw new Error(
        `Test setup failed creating an account: ${created.status}`,
      );
    }
    if (this.balanceCents > 0) {
      const deposit = await this.api.deposit(
        created.body.id,
        this.balanceCents,
      );
      if (deposit.status !== 201) {
        throw new Error(
          `Test setup failed funding an account: ${deposit.status}`,
        );
      }
    }
    return (await this.api.getAccount(created.body.id)).body;
  }
}

Create tests/framework/db-helper.ts:

tests/framework/db-helper.ts
import { Pool } from "pg";

// Read-only questions tests ask the database directly. One instance per
// Playwright worker (see fixtures.ts), closed when the worker finishes.
export class DbHelper {
  private readonly pool = new Pool({
    connectionString:
      process.env.DATABASE_URL ??
      "postgres://ledgerline:ledgerline@localhost:5432/ledgerline",
    max: 2,
  });

  /** Transfers that don't have exactly two ledger entries summing to zero. */
  async unbalancedTransfers() {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(`
      SELECT t.id, COUNT(e.id) AS entries, COALESCE(SUM(e.amount_cents), 0) AS total
      FROM transfers t
      LEFT JOIN ledger_entries e ON e.transfer_id = t.id
      GROUP BY t.id
      HAVING COUNT(e.id) <> 2 OR COALESCE(SUM(e.amount_cents), 0) <> 0
    `);
    return rows;
  }

  /** Sum of every ledger entry ever written. Should always be "0". */
  async ledgerTotal(): Promise<string> {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(
      "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents), 0)::text AS total FROM ledger_entries",
    );
    return rows[0].total;
  }

  /** Customer accounts whose balance has gone below zero. */
  async negativeCustomerBalances() {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(`
      SELECT a.id, SUM(e.amount_cents) AS balance
      FROM accounts a
      JOIN ledger_entries e ON e.account_id = a.id
      WHERE a.type = 'customer'
      GROUP BY a.id
      HAVING SUM(e.amount_cents) < 0
    `);
    return rows;
  }

  async countAccountsNamed(name: string): Promise<number> {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(
      "SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS count FROM accounts WHERE name = $1",
      [name],
    );
    return rows[0].count;
  }

  async close() {
    await this.pool.end();
  }
}

Create tests/framework/assertions.ts:

tests/framework/assertions.ts
import { expect } from "@playwright/test";
import type { ApiResult } from "./ledgerline-client";
import type { ApiErrorBody } from "./types";

/** Asserts the API refused a request with this status and error code. */
export function expectApiError(
  result: ApiResult<unknown>,
  status: number,
  code: string,
): void {
  expect(result.status, JSON.stringify(result.body)).toBe(status);
  expect((result.body as ApiErrorBody).error).toBe(code);
}

Create tests/framework/fixtures.ts:

tests/framework/fixtures.ts
import { test as base, type APIRequestContext } from "@playwright/test";
import { AccountBuilder } from "./account-builder";
import { DbHelper } from "./db-helper";
import { LedgerlineClient } from "./ledgerline-client";

interface TestFixtures {
  api: LedgerlineClient;
  newAccount: () => AccountBuilder;
  apiWithKey: (apiKey?: string) => Promise<LedgerlineClient>;
}

interface WorkerFixtures {
  db: DbHelper;
}

// Specs import { test, expect } from here instead of @playwright/test, and
// get these fixtures handed to them, already set up and cleaned up.
export const test = base.extend<TestFixtures, WorkerFixtures>({
  // A client that sends the normal API key (from playwright.config.ts).
  api: async ({ request }, use) => {
    await use(new LedgerlineClient(request));
  },

  // Call newAccount() for a fresh builder: newAccount().withBalance(500).create()
  newAccount: async ({ api }, use) => {
    await use(() => new AccountBuilder(api));
  },

  // A client with a different API key, or none, for authentication tests.
  apiWithKey: async ({ playwright, baseURL }, use) => {
    const contexts: APIRequestContext[] = [];
    await use(async (apiKey) => {
      const context = await playwright.request.newContext({
        baseURL,
        extraHTTPHeaders: apiKey ? { "x-api-key": apiKey } : {},
      });
      contexts.push(context);
      return new LedgerlineClient(context);
    });
    // Everything after use() runs when the test finishes: clean up.
    for (const context of contexts) await context.dispose();
  },

  db: [
    // Playwright requires the {} here even though this fixture needs nothing.
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
    async ({}, use) => {
      const db = new DbHelper();
      await use(db);
      await db.close();
    },
    { scope: "worker" },
  ],
});

export { expect } from "@playwright/test";

What the code does

  • The builder gives you readable setup, newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create(), with sensible defaults for everything you don't mention. Each method returns this, which is what lets the calls chain.
  • Fixtures are how Playwright hands tests what they need. A test lists what it wants in its arguments, like async ({ api, newAccount }) => ..., and Playwright builds exactly those.
  • await use(...) is the moment the test runs. Code before it is setup, and code after it is cleanup. The apiWithKey fixture uses this to close every extra connection it opened.
  • scope: "worker" creates the db fixture once per worker process instead of once per test. Week 2's withDb opened a new connection for every integrity test; this shares one small pool and closes it when the worker finishes.
  • expectApiError checks the status and the error code in one line, and shows the body when it fails.
  • The eslint-disable comment is needed because Playwright requires an empty {} argument in that spot, and ESLint normally flags empty patterns as a mistake.

Run npm run typecheck, then commit.

import { expectApiError } from "../framework/assertions";
import { expect, test } from "../framework/fixtures";
import { UNKNOWN_ID } from "../framework/test-data";

test.describe("accounts", () => {
  test("a new account starts with a zero balance", async ({ api }) => {
    const { status, body } = await api.createAccount("Kali's Bakery");

    expect(status).toBe(201);
    expect(body).toMatchObject({
      name: "Kali's Bakery",
      type: "customer",
      balanceCents: 0,
    });
  });

  test("an account can be fetched by id", async ({ api, newAccount }) => {
    const account = await newAccount().create();

    const { status, body } = await api.getAccount(account.id);

    expect(status).toBe(200);
    expect(body).toEqual(account);
  });

  test("deposits increase the balance", async ({ api, newAccount }) => {
    const account = await newAccount().create();

    await api.deposit(account.id, 5_000);
    await api.deposit(account.id, 1_250);

    expect(await api.balanceOf(account.id)).toBe(6_250);
  });

  test("an unknown account returns 404", async ({ api }) => {
    expectApiError(await api.getAccount(UNKNOWN_ID), 404, "account_not_found");
  });

  test("a malformed account id returns 400", async ({ api }) => {
    expectApiError(await api.getAccount("not-a-uuid"), 400, "validation_error");
  });

  test("a name of 100 characters is accepted", async ({ api }) => {
    const { status } = await api.createAccount("a".repeat(100));

    expect(status).toBe(201);
  });

  for (const [label, name] of [
    ["empty", ""],
    ["101 characters", "a".repeat(101)],
  ]) {
    test(`a name that is ${label} is rejected`, async ({ api }) => {
      expectApiError(await api.createAccount(name), 400, "validation_error");
    });
  }
});

Replace tests/api/transfers.spec.ts:

tests/api/transfers.spec.ts
import { expectApiError } from "../framework/assertions";
import { expect, test } from "../framework/fixtures";
import { FUNDING_ACCOUNT_ID, UNKNOWN_ID } from "../framework/test-data";

test.describe("transfers between accounts", () => {
  test("moves money from one account to another", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();

    const { status, body } = await api.createTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
    });

    expect(status).toBe(201);
    expect(body).toMatchObject({
      kind: "internal",
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      status: "completed",
    });
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(7_500);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(to.id)).toBe(2_500);
  });

  test("a transfer can be fetched by id", async ({ api, newAccount }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();
    const created = await api.createTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 300,
    });

    const { status, body } = await api.getTransfer(created.body.id);

    expect(status).toBe(200);
    expect(body).toEqual(created.body);
  });

  test("allows spending the exact balance", async ({ api, newAccount }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();

    const { status } = await api.createTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 1_000,
    });

    expect(status).toBe(201);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(0);
  });

  test("rejects a transfer one cent over the balance and changes nothing", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();

    const result = await api.createTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 1_001,
    });

    expectApiError(result, 422, "insufficient_funds");
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(1_000);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(to.id)).toBe(0);
  });

  test("rejects sending money to the same account", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
  }) => {
    const account = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();

    const result = await api.createTransfer({
      fromAccountId: account.id,
      toAccountId: account.id,
      amountCents: 100,
    });

    expectApiError(result, 422, "same_account");
  });

  test("won't let anyone spend from the system funding account", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
  }) => {
    const to = await newAccount().create();

    const result = await api.createTransfer({
      fromAccountId: FUNDING_ACCOUNT_ID,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 1_000_000,
    });

    expectApiError(result, 422, "account_not_allowed");
    expect(await api.balanceOf(to.id)).toBe(0);
  });

  test("returns 404 when an account doesn't exist", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();

    const result = await api.createTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: UNKNOWN_ID,
      amountCents: 100,
    });

    expectApiError(result, 404, "account_not_found");
  });

  const invalidAmounts = [
    { label: "zero", amountCents: 0 },
    { label: "negative", amountCents: -500 },
    { label: "fractional cents", amountCents: 10.5 },
    { label: "a string", amountCents: "1000" },
    { label: "over the limit", amountCents: 100_000_001 },
  ];

  for (const { label, amountCents } of invalidAmounts) {
    test(`rejects an amount that is ${label}`, async ({ api, newAccount }) => {
      const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();
      const to = await newAccount().create();

      const result = await api.createTransfer({
        fromAccountId: from.id,
        toAccountId: to.id,
        amountCents,
      });

      expectApiError(result, 400, "validation_error");
      expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(1_000);
    });
  }

  test("rejects unknown fields instead of ignoring them", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();

    const result = await api.createTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 100,
      memo: "not part of the API",
    });

    expectApiError(result, 400, "validation_error");
  });

  test("rejects malformed JSON", async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.post("/transfers", {
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      // A Buffer is sent byte-for-byte. A plain string would be JSON-encoded
      // by Playwright into a valid JSON string, and the test would lie to us.
      data: Buffer.from("{not valid json"),
    });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
    expect(await response.json()).toMatchObject({ error: "bad_request" });
  });

  test("parallel transfers can't overdraw an account", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();

    // Five $30 transfers fired at the same moment from a $100 account.
    const results = await Promise.all(
      Array.from({ length: 5 }, () =>
        api.createTransfer({
          fromAccountId: from.id,
          toAccountId: to.id,
          amountCents: 3_000,
        }),
      ),
    );

    const statuses = results.map((result) => result.status).sort();
    expect(statuses).toEqual([201, 201, 201, 422, 422]);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(1_000);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(to.id)).toBe(9_000);
  });
});

import { formatCents } from "../../src/domain/money";
import { expect, test } from "../framework/fixtures";
import { MAX_AMOUNT_CENTS, UNKNOWN_ID } from "../framework/test-data";
import { expectApiError } from "../framework/assertions";

test.describe("deposit amount boundaries", () => {
  // Boundary value analysis: test just below, on, and just above each edge.
  const cases = [
    { amountCents: 0, expected: 400 },
    { amountCents: 1, expected: 201 },
    { amountCents: MAX_AMOUNT_CENTS, expected: 201 },
    { amountCents: MAX_AMOUNT_CENTS + 1, expected: 400 },
  ];

  for (const { amountCents, expected } of cases) {
    test(`a deposit of ${formatCents(amountCents)} returns ${expected}`, async ({
      api,
      newAccount,
    }) => {
      const account = await newAccount().create();

      const { status } = await api.deposit(account.id, amountCents);

      expect(status).toBe(expected);
      expect(await api.balanceOf(account.id)).toBe(
        expected === 201 ? amountCents : 0,
      );
    });
  }

  test("a deposit to an unknown account returns 404", async ({ api }) => {
    expectApiError(
      await api.deposit(UNKNOWN_ID, 100),
      404,
      "account_not_found",
    );
  });
});

New tests in this step:

  • Boundary value analysis in deposits.spec.ts: just below, on, and just above each edge of the allowed amount. The titles use formatCents, so the report reads "a deposit of $0.01 returns 201".
  • Account name boundaries: 100 characters accepted; empty and 101 characters rejected.

Try this

Break the contract on purpose. In src/routes/accounts.ts, inside loadAccount, rename balanceCents: to balance:, then run npm run test:api: 

Error: Contract violation: http://localhost:3000/accounts returned 201
