Replace src/ledger.ts. The new parts are at the bottom: findTransferStatus and recordPartnerOutcome:

src/ledger.ts
import type { PoolClient } from "pg";
import { pool } from "./db";
import { formatCents } from "./domain/money";
import { AppError, notFound } from "./errors";

export const FUNDING_ACCOUNT_ID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001";
export const CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002";

export type TransferKind = "deposit" | "internal" | "external" | "reversal";
export type TransferStatus =
  "completed" | "pending" | "submitted" | "rejected" | "failed";

// Where a payment to another bank is going.
export interface Counterparty {
  name: string;
  routingNumber: string;
  accountNumber: string;
}

// What a transfers row looks like coming out of Postgres.
interface TransferRow {
  id: string;
  kind: TransferKind;
  from_account_id: string;
  to_account_id: string;
  amount_cents: string; // bigint arrives as a string, see toCents()
  status: TransferStatus;
  counterparty_name: string | null;
  counterparty_routing: string | null;
  counterparty_account: string | null;
  reverses_transfer_id: string | null;
  partner_reference: string | null;
  status_reason: string | null;
  created_at: Date;
}

// What we send back to API clients.
export interface Transfer {
  id: string;
  kind: TransferKind;
  fromAccountId: string;
  toAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  status: TransferStatus;
  createdAt: string;
  // Only the last four digits ever leave the API.
  counterparty?: { name: string; routingNumber: string; accountLast4: string };
  partnerReference?: string;
  statusReason?: string;
  reversesTransferId?: string;
}

// Postgres bigint can hold numbers JavaScript can't represent exactly, so pg
// returns them as strings. Our amounts are far below that limit, so we convert,
// but refuse loudly if a value ever isn't a safe whole number.
export function toCents(value: string | number): number {
  const cents = Number(value);
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(cents)) {
    throw new Error(`Not a safe whole number of cents: ${value}`);
  }
  return cents;
}

export function toTransfer(row: TransferRow): Transfer {
  const transfer: Transfer = {
    id: row.id,
    kind: row.kind,
    fromAccountId: row.from_account_id,
    toAccountId: row.to_account_id,
    amountCents: toCents(row.amount_cents),
    status: row.status,
    createdAt: row.created_at.toISOString(),
  };
  if (row.counterparty_account) {
    transfer.counterparty = {
      name: row.counterparty_name ?? "",
      routingNumber: row.counterparty_routing ?? "",
      accountLast4: row.counterparty_account.slice(-4),
    };
  }
  if (row.partner_reference) transfer.partnerReference = row.partner_reference;
  if (row.status_reason) transfer.statusReason = row.status_reason;
  if (row.reverses_transfer_id) {
    transfer.reversesTransferId = row.reverses_transfer_id;
  }
  return transfer;
}

type Queryable = Pick<PoolClient, "query">;

export async function getBalance(db: Queryable, accountId: string) {
  const { rows } = await db.query<{ balance: string }>(
    "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents), 0) AS balance FROM ledger_entries WHERE account_id = $1",
    [accountId],
  );
  return toCents(rows[0].balance);
}

export async function getTransfer(id: string): Promise<Transfer> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<TransferRow>(
    "SELECT * FROM transfers WHERE id = $1",
    [id],
  );
  if (rows.length === 0) throw notFound("transfer", id);
  return toTransfer(rows[0]);
}

interface MoveMoneyInput {
  kind: TransferKind;
  fromAccountId: string;
  toAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  status?: TransferStatus;
  counterparty?: Counterparty;
  // Runs inside the transaction, after everything is written but before
  // COMMIT. If it throws, the whole transfer is rolled back.
  beforeCommit?: (transfer: Transfer) => Promise<void>;
}

// The one place money moves. Everything happens inside a database transaction:
// either the transfer and both ledger entries are saved, or nothing is.
export async function moveMoney(input: MoveMoneyInput): Promise<Transfer> {
  if (input.fromAccountId === input.toAccountId) {
    throw new AppError(
      422,
      "same_account",
      "Can't transfer to the same account",
    );
  }

  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query("BEGIN");

    // Lock both account rows until COMMIT, always in the same order (by id).
    // Two transfers touching the same account now take turns instead of both
    // reading the old balance, and opposite transfers can't deadlock.
    const { rows: accounts } = await client.query<{ id: string; type: string }>(
      "SELECT id, type FROM accounts WHERE id = ANY($1::uuid[]) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE",
      [[input.fromAccountId, input.toAccountId]],
    );
    const from = accounts.find((account) => account.id === input.fromAccountId);
    const to = accounts.find((account) => account.id === input.toAccountId);
    if (!from) throw notFound("account", input.fromAccountId);
    if (!to) throw notFound("account", input.toAccountId);

    // Only deposits may draw on a system account.
    if (
      input.kind === "internal" &&
      (from.type !== "customer" || to.type !== "customer")
    ) {
      throw new AppError(
        422,
        "account_not_allowed",
        "Transfers must be between customer accounts",
      );
    }
    if (input.kind === "external" && from.type !== "customer") {
      throw new AppError(
        422,
        "account_not_allowed",
        "Only customer accounts can pay other banks",
      );
    }

    if (from.type === "customer") {
      const balance = await getBalance(client, from.id);
      if (balance < input.amountCents) {
        throw new AppError(
          422,
          "insufficient_funds",
          `Balance is ${formatCents(balance)} but the transfer needs ${formatCents(input.amountCents)}`,
        );
      }
    }

    const { rows } = await client.query<TransferRow>(
      `INSERT INTO transfers (kind, from_account_id, to_account_id, amount_cents, status,
         counterparty_name, counterparty_routing, counterparty_account)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)
       RETURNING *`,
      [
        input.kind,
        input.fromAccountId,
        input.toAccountId,
        input.amountCents,
        input.status ?? "completed",
        input.counterparty?.name ?? null,
        input.counterparty?.routingNumber ?? null,
        input.counterparty?.accountNumber ?? null,
      ],
    );
    const transfer = toTransfer(rows[0]);

    // Double entry: money leaves one account and arrives in the other.
    await client.query(
      "INSERT INTO ledger_entries (account_id, transfer_id, amount_cents) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)",
      [input.fromAccountId, transfer.id, -input.amountCents],
    );
    await client.query(
      "INSERT INTO ledger_entries (account_id, transfer_id, amount_cents) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)",
      [input.toAccountId, transfer.id, input.amountCents],
    );

    if (input.beforeCommit) await input.beforeCommit(transfer);

    await client.query("COMMIT");
    return transfer;
  } catch (error) {
    await client.query("ROLLBACK");
    throw error;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

export type PartnerOutcome =
  | { status: "submitted"; partnerReference: string }
  | { status: "rejected" | "failed"; reason: string };

/** The transfer's current status, or null if it doesn't exist. */
export async function findTransferStatus(
  id: string,
): Promise<TransferStatus | null> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<{ status: TransferStatus }>(
    "SELECT status FROM transfers WHERE id = $1",
    [id],
  );
  return rows[0]?.status ?? null;
}

// Records what the partner bank said about a pending payment. Safe to call
// twice: only a pending transfer can change, so a duplicate message changes
// nothing. A rejected or failed payment sends the money back with a reversal.
export async function recordPartnerOutcome(
  transferId: string,
  outcome: PartnerOutcome,
): Promise<"updated" | "unchanged"> {
  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query("BEGIN");
    const { rows } = await client.query<TransferRow>(
      "SELECT * FROM transfers WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE",
      [transferId],
    );
    const transfer = rows[0];
    if (!transfer || transfer.status !== "pending") {
      await client.query("ROLLBACK");
      return "unchanged";
    }

    if (outcome.status === "submitted") {
      await client.query(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = 'submitted', partner_reference = $2 WHERE id = $1",
        [transferId, outcome.partnerReference],
      );
    } else {
      await client.query(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = $2, status_reason = $3 WHERE id = $1",
        [transferId, outcome.status, outcome.reason],
      );
      // Money goes back from clearing to the customer: a new transfer.
      const amount = toCents(transfer.amount_cents);
      const { rows: reversal } = await client.query<{ id: string }>(
        `INSERT INTO transfers (kind, from_account_id, to_account_id, amount_cents, status, reverses_transfer_id)
         VALUES ('reversal', $1, $2, $3, 'completed', $4)
         RETURNING id`,
        [transfer.to_account_id, transfer.from_account_id, amount, transfer.id],
      );
      await client.query(
        "INSERT INTO ledger_entries (account_id, transfer_id, amount_cents) VALUES ($1, $2, $3), ($4, $2, $5)",
        [
          transfer.to_account_id,
          reversal[0].id,
          -amount,
          transfer.from_account_id,
          amount,
        ],
      );
    }

    await client.query("COMMIT");
    return "updated";
  } catch (error) {
    await client.query("ROLLBACK");
    throw error;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

Create src/processor/partner.ts:

src/processor/partner.ts
import type { TransferRequestedMessage } from "../queue";

// The partner bank's API. In tests and locally it's WireMock.
export const PARTNER_URL = process.env.PARTNER_URL ?? "http://localhost:8080";
const TIMEOUT_MS = Number(process.env.PARTNER_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 2000);

export type PartnerResult =
  | { kind: "accepted"; reference: string }
  | { kind: "rejected"; reason: string }
  | { kind: "retryable"; reason: string };

export async function originatePayment(
  message: TransferRequestedMessage,
): Promise<PartnerResult> {
  let response: Response;
  try {
    response = await fetch(`${PARTNER_URL}/ach/originate`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "content-type": "application/json",
        // The partner can use this to spot a payment it has already seen.
        "idempotency-key": message.transferId,
        "x-correlation-id": message.correlationId,
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        transferId: message.transferId,
        amountCents: message.amountCents,
        counterparty: message.counterparty,
      }),
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(TIMEOUT_MS),
    });
  } catch (error) {
    const timedOut = error instanceof Error && error.name === "TimeoutError";
    return {
      kind: "retryable",
      reason: timedOut
        ? `no answer within ${TIMEOUT_MS} ms`
        : "partner unreachable",
    };
  }

  const body = (await response.json().catch(() => ({}))) as {
    reference?: string;
    error?: string;
  };
  if (response.ok) {
    return { kind: "accepted", reference: body.reference ?? "unknown" };
  }
  // 5xx and 429 mean "try again later". Any other 4xx means the request
  // itself is wrong, and sending it again would get the same answer.
  if (response.status >= 500 || response.status === 429) {
    return { kind: "retryable", reason: `partner answered ${response.status}` };
  }
  return {
    kind: "rejected",
    reason: body.error ?? `partner answered ${response.status}`,
  };
}

Create src/processor/handler.ts:

src/processor/handler.ts
import { ChangeMessageVisibilityCommand } from "@aws-sdk/client-sqs";
import type { SQSBatchResponse, SQSEvent, SQSRecord } from "aws-lambda";
import { findTransferStatus, recordPartnerOutcome } from "../ledger";
import { sqs, TRANSFERS_QUEUE, type TransferRequestedMessage } from "../queue";
import { originatePayment } from "./partner";

// Must match maxReceiveCount in scripts/aws-setup.ts.
const MAX_ATTEMPTS = Number(process.env.MAX_ATTEMPTS ?? 3);
const RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS = Number(process.env.RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS ?? 2);

function log(level: string, msg: string, fields: Record<string, unknown>) {
  console.log(
    JSON.stringify({ level, time: new Date().toISOString(), msg, ...fields }),
  );
}

// The Lambda entry point. AWS calls it with a batch of SQS messages and reads
// back which ones failed, so only those are retried.
export async function handler(event: SQSEvent): Promise<SQSBatchResponse> {
  const batchItemFailures: { itemIdentifier: string }[] = [];
  for (const record of event.Records) {
    const succeeded = await processRecord(record);
    if (!succeeded)
      batchItemFailures.push({ itemIdentifier: record.messageId });
  }
  return { batchItemFailures };
}

function parse(body: string): TransferRequestedMessage | null {
  try {
    const message = JSON.parse(body);
    const valid =
      message?.version === 1 &&
      message.type === "transfer.requested" &&
      typeof message.transferId === "string" &&
      Number.isInteger(message.amountCents) &&
      typeof message.counterparty?.accountNumber === "string";
    return valid ? message : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

async function processRecord(record: SQSRecord): Promise<boolean> {
  const attempt = Number(record.attributes.ApproximateReceiveCount ?? "1");
  const message = parse(record.body);
  if (!message) {
    // It will never parse, however often it's retried. Let it fail its way
    // to the dead-letter queue, where a person can look at it.
    log("error", "unreadable message", {
      messageId: record.messageId,
      attempt,
    });
    await retryLater(record, attempt);
    return false;
  }

  const context = {
    transferId: message.transferId,
    correlationId: message.correlationId,
    attempt,
  };

  // At-least-once delivery means duplicates. Only pending payments are sent.
  const status = await findTransferStatus(message.transferId);
  if (status !== "pending") {
    log("info", "nothing to do", { ...context, status });
    return true;
  }

  const result = await originatePayment(message);

  if (result.kind === "accepted") {
    await recordPartnerOutcome(message.transferId, {
      status: "submitted",
      partnerReference: result.reference,
    });
    log("info", "payment submitted", {
      ...context,
      reference: result.reference,
    });
    return true;
  }

  if (result.kind === "rejected") {
    await recordPartnerOutcome(message.transferId, {
      status: "rejected",
      reason: result.reason,
    });
    log("warn", "payment rejected, money returned", {
      ...context,
      reason: result.reason,
    });
    return true;
  }

  if (attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
    await recordPartnerOutcome(message.transferId, {
      status: "failed",
      reason: result.reason,
    });
    log("error", "payment failed, money returned", {
      ...context,
      reason: result.reason,
    });
    // Fail once more with no delay, so SQS moves it to the dead-letter queue.
    await retryLater(record, 0);
    return false;
  }

  log("warn", "partner problem, will retry", {
    ...context,
    reason: result.reason,
  });
  await retryLater(record, attempt);
  return false;
}

// Hide the message for a while before its next try: 2s, then 4s.
async function retryLater(record: SQSRecord, attempt: number) {
  const queueUrl = record.eventSourceARN
    ? await queueUrlFromArn(record.eventSourceARN)
    : undefined;
  if (!queueUrl) return;
  await sqs.send(
    new ChangeMessageVisibilityCommand({
      QueueUrl: queueUrl,
      ReceiptHandle: record.receiptHandle,
      VisibilityTimeout: RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS * attempt,
    }),
  );
}

async function queueUrlFromArn(arn: string): Promise<string> {
  // arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:000000000000:ledgerline-transfers
  const [, , , region, account, name] = arn.split(":");
  const endpoint =
    process.env.AWS_ENDPOINT_URL ?? `https://sqs.${region}.amazonaws.com`;
  return `${endpoint}/${account}/${name ?? TRANSFERS_QUEUE}`;
}

Create scripts/processor.ts, the local runner:

scripts/processor.ts
import http from "node:http";
import {
  DeleteMessageCommand,
  GetQueueAttributesCommand,
  GetQueueUrlCommand,
  ReceiveMessageCommand,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-sqs";
import type { SQSEvent } from "aws-lambda";
import { handler } from "../src/processor/handler";
import { sqs, TRANSFERS_QUEUE } from "../src/queue";

// Runs the Lambda handler on your machine the way AWS's SQS trigger would:
// fetch a batch, call the handler, delete what succeeded, and leave the
// failures on the queue so they're retried.
async function main() {
  const { QueueUrl } = await sqs.send(
    new GetQueueUrlCommand({ QueueName: TRANSFERS_QUEUE }),
  );
  const { Attributes } = await sqs.send(
    new GetQueueAttributesCommand({ QueueUrl, AttributeNames: ["QueueArn"] }),
  );
  const queueArn = Attributes?.QueueArn ?? "";

  // A tiny health endpoint so Playwright knows when the processor is ready.
  const port = Number(process.env.PROCESSOR_PORT ?? 3002);
  http.createServer((_, res) => res.end("ok")).listen(port);
  console.log(`Processor polling ${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}, health on port ${port}`);

  for (;;) {
    try {
      const { Messages = [] } = await sqs.send(
        new ReceiveMessageCommand({
          QueueUrl,
          MaxNumberOfMessages: 10,
          WaitTimeSeconds: 5,
          AttributeNames: ["All"],
        }),
      );
      if (Messages.length === 0) continue;

      const event: SQSEvent = {
        Records: Messages.map((m) => ({
          messageId: m.MessageId ?? "",
          receiptHandle: m.ReceiptHandle ?? "",
          body: m.Body ?? "",
          attributes: {
            ApproximateReceiveCount:
              m.Attributes?.ApproximateReceiveCount ?? "1",
            SentTimestamp: m.Attributes?.SentTimestamp ?? "",
            SenderId: m.Attributes?.SenderId ?? "",
            ApproximateFirstReceiveTimestamp:
              m.Attributes?.ApproximateFirstReceiveTimestamp ?? "",
          },
          messageAttributes: {},
          md5OfBody: m.MD5OfBody ?? "",
          eventSource: "aws:sqs",
          eventSourceARN: queueArn,
          awsRegion: process.env.AWS_REGION ?? "us-east-1",
        })),
      };

      const { batchItemFailures } = await handler(event);
      const failed = new Set(batchItemFailures.map((f) => f.itemIdentifier));
      await Promise.all(
        Messages.filter((m) => !failed.has(m.MessageId ?? "")).map((m) =>
          sqs.send(
            new DeleteMessageCommand({
              QueueUrl,
              ReceiptHandle: m.ReceiptHandle,
            }),
          ),
        ),
      );
    } catch (error) {
      console.error("Processor loop error, retrying in 1s:", error);
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
    }
  }
}

main().catch((error) => {
  console.error("Processor failed to start:", error);
  process.exit(1);
});

Replace scripts/aws-setup.ts. It adds a third queue that Step 28's tests need:

scripts/aws-setup.ts
import {
  CreateQueueCommand,
  GetQueueAttributesCommand,
  ListQueuesCommand,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-sqs";
import { sqs, TRANSFERS_QUEUE } from "../src/queue";

const DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE = `${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}-dlq`;
const INSPECT_QUEUE = `${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}-inspect`;

// MiniStack can take a few seconds to start, especially in CI.
async function waitForMiniStack() {
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 30; attempt++) {
    try {
      await sqs.send(new ListQueuesCommand({}));
      return;
    } catch {
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
    }
  }
  throw new Error("MiniStack didn't answer on port 4566. Is it running?");
}

async function setup() {
  await waitForMiniStack();

  // The dead-letter queue first, because the main queue points at it.
  const dlq = await sqs.send(
    new CreateQueueCommand({ QueueName: DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE }),
  );
  const { Attributes } = await sqs.send(
    new GetQueueAttributesCommand({
      QueueUrl: dlq.QueueUrl,
      AttributeNames: ["QueueArn"],
    }),
  );

  // After 3 failed receives, SQS moves a message to the dead-letter queue.
  await sqs.send(
    new CreateQueueCommand({
      QueueName: TRANSFERS_QUEUE,
      Attributes: {
        VisibilityTimeout: "30",
        RedrivePolicy: JSON.stringify({
          deadLetterTargetArn: Attributes?.QueueArn,
          maxReceiveCount: 3,
        }),
      },
    }),
  );

  // A queue nobody reads from. Tests point a copy of the API at it, so they
  // can inspect messages before the processor takes them.
  await sqs.send(new CreateQueueCommand({ QueueName: INSPECT_QUEUE }));

  console.log(
    `Queues ready: ${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}, ${DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE} and ${INSPECT_QUEUE}`,
  );
}

setup().catch((error) => {
  console.error("AWS setup failed:", error);
  process.exitCode = 1;
});

npm pkg set scripts.processor="tsx scripts/processor.ts"
npm run aws:setup

Queues ready: ledgerline-transfers, ledgerline-transfers-dlq and ledgerline-transfers-inspect

Watch it work

Use three terminals: npm run dev in the first, npm run processor in the second. In the third, send a payment with the curl from Step 23, wait two seconds, then look at it: 

curl -s -H 'x-api-key: local-dev-key' localhost:3000/transfers/PASTE-THE-TRANSFER-ID | jq

The status is now "submitted", with "partnerReference": "ACH-DEFAULT", and the processor's terminal printed a JSON line saying "payment submitted".

What the code does

  • handler is the Lambda entry point. It processes each record and returns batchItemFailures: the ids of the messages that failed. That's the partial batch response from chapter 14 of the field guide, so only failed messages are retried.
  • parse checks the message's shape. Unreadable messages are logged and failed, never crashed on.
  • findTransferStatus is the first defence against duplicates: anything that isn't pending is skipped.
  • originatePayment sorts every answer into three kinds. 2xx is accepted. 5xx and 429 are worth retrying. Any other 4xx is a rejection. A timeout, set with AbortSignal.timeout, also counts as retryable.
  • recordPartnerOutcome locks the transfer row and only changes a pending transfer. It's the second defence against duplicates: if two copies of a message race, the second finds the transfer already handled.
  • ApproximateReceiveCount is how many times SQS has delivered this message. On the third failure, the processor marks the payment failed, returns the money, and fails the message once more, so SQS moves it to the dead-letter queue.
  • retryLater hides the message for a few seconds with ChangeMessageVisibility, instead of the queue's default 30, so retries are quick.
  • The runner gives the handler exactly the event shape Lambda would, and deletes only the messages that succeeded. Its small health server on port 3002 lets Playwright know it's ready.

Heads up

A rare race condition is hiding in this handler. It only shows up when the suite runs many times over, and Week 10's repeat runs find and fix it. If a processor test fails once in a long while before then, that's why.

Commit with git add -A && git commit -m "Step 27: Processor".

Step 28: Test the processor end to end

About two hours.

Now the processor is running, it takes every message off the main queue, so Week 4's queue-reading tests would race it. They move to a third copy of the API that publishes to the inspect queue, which nobody reads. Every other test now watches outcomes: a transfer's status, the bank's requests, balances, and the dead-letter queue.

Each test gets its own fake bank, with a unique counterparty name, and its stubs only match that name. That's why tests can run in parallel without seeing each other's stubs.

                  $ref: "#/components/schemas/AmountCents"
                counterparty:
                  $ref: "#/components/schemas/CounterpartyDetails"
      responses:
        "202":
          description: Accepted and waiting to be sent
          headers:
            x-correlation-id:
              description: One id that follows this payment through every log
              schema:
                type: string
                format: uuid
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Transfer"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "422":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "503":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"

  /transfers/{id}:
    get:
      summary: Get a transfer
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Id"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The transfer
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Transfer"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"

components:
  securitySchemes:
    apiKey:
      type: apiKey
      in: header
      name: x-api-key

  parameters:
    Id:
      name: id
      in: path
      required: true
      schema:
        type: string
        format: uuid

  responses:
    Error:
      description: The request failed. `error` says why in a stable code.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"

  schemas:
    AmountCents:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100000000

    HealthStatus:
      type: object
      required: [status, database]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [ok, degraded]
        database:
          type: string
          enum: [up, down]

    Account:
      type: object
      required: [id, name, type, balanceCents, createdAt]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        name:
          type: string
        type:
          type: string
          enum: [customer, system]
        balanceCents:
          type: integer
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time

    Transfer:
      type: object
      required:
        [id, kind, fromAccountId, toAccountId, amountCents, status, createdAt]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        kind:
          type: string
          enum: [deposit, internal, external, reversal]
        fromAccountId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        toAccountId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        amountCents:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/AmountCents"
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [completed, pending, submitted, rejected, failed]
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        counterparty:
          type: object
          description: Only on external transfers. Never the full account number.
          required: [name, routingNumber, accountLast4]
          additionalProperties: false
          properties:
            name:
              type: string
            routingNumber:
              type: string
              pattern: "^[0-9]{9}$"
            accountLast4:
              type: string
              pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
        partnerReference:
          type: string
          description: The partner bank's id for a submitted payment
        statusReason:
          type: string
          description: Why a payment was rejected or failed
        reversesTransferId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
          description: On a reversal, the payment it sends money back for

    CounterpartyDetails:
      type: object
      required: [name, routingNumber, accountNumber]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 100
        routingNumber:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{9}$"
        accountNumber:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4,17}$"

    TransferRequestedMessage:
      description: What the API puts on the transfers queue. Not an HTTP response.
      type: object
      required:
        [version, type, transferId, correlationId, amountCents, counterparty]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        version:
          const: 1
        type:
          const: transfer.requested
        transferId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        correlationId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        amountCents:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/AmountCents"
        counterparty:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/CounterpartyDetails"

    Error:
      type: object
      required: [error, message]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        error:
          type: string
          description: Stable code such as insufficient_funds
        message:
          type: string
          description: Human-readable explanation

tests/framework/queue-helper.ts
import {
  DeleteMessageCommand,
  GetQueueAttributesCommand,
  GetQueueUrlCommand,
  ReceiveMessageCommand,
  SendMessageCommand,
  SQSClient,
  type Message,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-sqs";

export interface ReceivedMessage {
  raw: string;
  body: Record<string, unknown>;
  correlationId: string | undefined;
}

// Reads and writes one queue in MiniStack.
export class QueueHelper {
  private readonly sqs = new SQSClient({
    region: process.env.AWS_REGION ?? "us-east-1",
    endpoint: process.env.AWS_ENDPOINT_URL ?? "http://localhost:4566",
    credentials: { accessKeyId: "test", secretAccessKey: "test" },
  });
  private url: string | undefined;

  constructor(private readonly queueName: string) {}

  /** Deletes every message waiting on the queue, so a test starts clean. */
  async drain(): Promise<void> {
    for (;;) {
      const messages = await this.receive(0, 30);
      if (messages.length === 0) return;
      await Promise.all(messages.map((message) => this.delete(message)));
    }
  }

  /** Waits for a message that passes the check, deletes it, and returns it. */
  async takeMessage(
    matches: (raw: string) => boolean,
    timeoutMs = 5_000,
  ): Promise<ReceivedMessage> {
    const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
    while (Date.now() < deadline) {
      // Visibility 0: look without hiding other tests' messages.
      for (const message of await this.receive(1, 0)) {
        const raw = message.Body ?? "";
        if (!matches(raw)) continue;
        await this.delete(message);
        let body: Record<string, unknown> = {};
        try {
          body = JSON.parse(raw);
        } catch {
          // Not JSON. The raw text is still returned.
        }
        return {
          raw,
          body,
          correlationId: message.MessageAttributes?.correlationId?.StringValue,
        };
      }
    }
    throw new Error(
      `No matching message on ${this.queueName} within ${timeoutMs} ms`,
    );
  }

  /** Waits for the message about one transfer. */
  takeMessageFor(transferId: string, timeoutMs = 5_000) {
    return this.takeMessage((raw) => raw.includes(transferId), timeoutMs);
  }

  /** True when nothing is waiting. Looks without hiding anything. */
  async isEmpty(): Promise<boolean> {
    return (await this.receive(1, 0)).length === 0;
  }

  /** True when nothing is waiting and nothing is being worked on. */
  async isIdle(): Promise<boolean> {
    const { Attributes } = await this.sqs.send(
      new GetQueueAttributesCommand({
        QueueUrl: await this.queueUrl(),
        AttributeNames: [
          "ApproximateNumberOfMessages",
          "ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible",
        ],
      }),
    );
    return (
      Attributes?.ApproximateNumberOfMessages === "0" &&
      Attributes?.ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible === "0"
    );
  }

  /** Puts a message on the queue directly, bypassing the API. */
  async send(body: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.sqs.send(
      new SendMessageCommand({
        QueueUrl: await this.queueUrl(),
        MessageBody: body,
      }),
    );
  }

  private async receive(waitSeconds: number, visibilityTimeout: number) {
    const result = await this.sqs.send(
      new ReceiveMessageCommand({
        QueueUrl: await this.queueUrl(),
        MaxNumberOfMessages: 10,
        WaitTimeSeconds: waitSeconds,
        VisibilityTimeout: visibilityTimeout,
        MessageAttributeNames: ["All"],
      }),
    );
    return result.Messages ?? [];
  }

  private async delete(message: Message) {
    await this.sqs.send(
      new DeleteMessageCommand({
        QueueUrl: await this.queueUrl(),
        ReceiptHandle: message.ReceiptHandle,
      }),
    );
  }

  private async queueUrl(): Promise<string> {
    if (!this.url) {
      const result = await this.sqs.send(
        new GetQueueUrlCommand({ QueueName: this.queueName }),
      );
      if (!result.QueueUrl) throw new Error(`No queue ${this.queueName}`);
      this.url = result.QueueUrl;
    }
    return this.url;
  }
}

tests/framework/fake-partner.ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";

const WIREMOCK_URL = process.env.WIREMOCK_URL ?? "http://localhost:8080";

export interface PartnerRequest {
  body: Record<string, unknown>;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
}

// Programs WireMock to behave like the partner bank, for one test's payments.
// Every stub matches this partner's unique counterparty name, so tests
// running in parallel never see each other's stubs.
export class FakePartner {
  readonly counterparty = {
    name: `Supplier ${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`,
    routingNumber: "021000021",
    accountNumber: "123456789",
  };
  private readonly stubIds: string[] = [];

  /** The partner accepts every payment. */
  accepts() {
    return this.stub({ status: 200, jsonBody: { reference: "ACH-7F3A2B" } });
  }

  /** The partner refuses: a 400 that's not worth retrying. */
  rejects(error = "invalid_account") {
    return this.stub({ status: 400, jsonBody: { error } });
  }

  /** The partner answers with a server error every time. */
  failsWith(status = 500) {
    return this.stub({ status });
  }

  /** The first call fails with a 500; every call after that works. */
  async failsOnceThenAccepts() {
    const scenarioName = `flaky ${this.counterparty.name}`;
    await this.stub(
      { status: 500 },
      {
        scenarioName,
        requiredScenarioState: "Started",
        newScenarioState: "recovered",
      },
    );
    await this.stub(
      { status: 200, jsonBody: { reference: "ACH-SECOND-TRY" } },
      { scenarioName, requiredScenarioState: "recovered" },
    );
  }

  /** Every request the partner received for this test's payments. */
  async requests(): Promise<PartnerRequest[]> {
    const response = await fetch(`${WIREMOCK_URL}/__admin/requests/find`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ ...this.matcher() }),
    });
    const { requests } = (await response.json()) as {
      requests: { body: string; headers: Record<string, string> }[];
    };
    return requests.map((r) => ({
      body: JSON.parse(r.body),
      headers: Object.fromEntries(
        Object.entries(r.headers).map(([k, v]) => [k.toLowerCase(), v]),
      ),
    }));
  }

  async cleanup() {
    await Promise.all(
      this.stubIds.map((id) =>
        fetch(`${WIREMOCK_URL}/__admin/mappings/${id}`, { method: "DELETE" }),
      ),
    );
  }

  private matcher() {
    return {
      method: "POST",
      urlPath: "/ach/originate",
      bodyPatterns: [
        {
          matchesJsonPath: `$.counterparty[?(@.name == '${this.counterparty.name}')]`,
        },
      ],
    };
  }

  private async stub(
    response: Record<string, unknown>,
    extra: Record<string, unknown> = {},
  ) {
    const result = await fetch(`${WIREMOCK_URL}/__admin/mappings`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        priority: 1,
        ...extra,
        request: this.matcher(),
        response: {
          headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
          ...response,
        },
      }),
    });
    const { id } = (await result.json()) as { id: string };
    this.stubIds.push(id);
  }
}

tests/framework/fixtures.ts
import { test as base, type APIRequestContext } from "@playwright/test";
import { AccountBuilder } from "./account-builder";
import { DbHelper } from "./db-helper";
import { LedgerlineClient } from "./ledgerline-client";
import { FakePartner } from "./fake-partner";
import { QueueHelper } from "./queue-helper";
import {
  API_KEY,
  BROKEN_QUEUE_API_URL,
  DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE,
  INSPECT_API_URL,
  INSPECT_QUEUE,
  TRANSFERS_QUEUE,
} from "./test-data";

interface TestFixtures {
  api: LedgerlineClient;
  newAccount: () => AccountBuilder;
  apiWithKey: (apiKey?: string) => Promise<LedgerlineClient>;
  brokenQueueApi: LedgerlineClient;
  inspectApi: LedgerlineClient;
  partner: FakePartner;
}

interface WorkerFixtures {
  db: DbHelper;
  inspectQueue: QueueHelper;
  transfersQueue: QueueHelper;
  deadLetterQueue: QueueHelper;
}

// Specs import { test, expect } from here instead of @playwright/test, and
// get these fixtures handed to them, already set up and cleaned up.
export const test = base.extend<TestFixtures, WorkerFixtures>({
  // A client that sends the normal API key (from playwright.config.ts).
  api: async ({ request }, use) => {
    await use(new LedgerlineClient(request));
  },

  // Call newAccount() for a fresh builder: newAccount().withBalance(500).create()
  newAccount: async ({ api }, use) => {
    await use(() => new AccountBuilder(api));
  },

  // A client with a different API key, or none, for authentication tests.
  apiWithKey: async ({ playwright, baseURL }, use) => {
    const contexts: APIRequestContext[] = [];
    await use(async (apiKey) => {
      const context = await playwright.request.newContext({
        baseURL,
        extraHTTPHeaders: apiKey ? { "x-api-key": apiKey } : {},
      });
      contexts.push(context);
      return new LedgerlineClient(context);
    });
    // Everything after use() runs when the test finishes: clean up.
    for (const context of contexts) await context.dispose();
  },

  // A client for the second API, the one whose queue doesn't exist.
  brokenQueueApi: async ({ playwright }, use) => {
    const context = await playwright.request.newContext({
      baseURL: BROKEN_QUEUE_API_URL,
      extraHTTPHeaders: { "x-api-key": API_KEY },
    });
    await use(new LedgerlineClient(context));
    await context.dispose();
  },

  // A client for the third API, which publishes to the inspect queue.
  inspectApi: async ({ playwright }, use) => {
    const context = await playwright.request.newContext({
      baseURL: INSPECT_API_URL,
      extraHTTPHeaders: { "x-api-key": API_KEY },
    });
    await use(new LedgerlineClient(context));
    await context.dispose();
  },

  // A fake partner bank with its own counterparty, so its stubs only match
  // this test's payments. Its stubs are removed when the test ends.
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
  partner: async ({}, use) => {
    const partner = new FakePartner();
    await use(partner);
    await partner.cleanup();
  },

  // The queues in MiniStack, one helper each per worker.
  inspectQueue: [
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
    async ({}, use) => {
      await use(new QueueHelper(INSPECT_QUEUE));
    },
    { scope: "worker" },
  ],
  transfersQueue: [
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
    async ({}, use) => {
      await use(new QueueHelper(TRANSFERS_QUEUE));
    },
    { scope: "worker" },
  ],
  deadLetterQueue: [
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
    async ({}, use) => {
      await use(new QueueHelper(DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE));
    },
    { scope: "worker" },
  ],

  db: [
    // Playwright requires the {} here even though this fixture needs nothing.
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
    async ({}, use) => {
      const db = new DbHelper();
      await use(db);
      await db.close();
    },
    { scope: "worker" },
  ],
});

import { defineConfig } from "@playwright/test";

const port = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000);
const baseURL = process.env.API_URL ?? `http://localhost:${port}`;

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: "tests/api",
  fullyParallel: true,
  forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI,
  retries: 0,
  reporter: [["list"], ["html", { open: "never" }]],
  use: {
    baseURL,
    // Sent with every request made through the request fixture.
    extraHTTPHeaders: { "x-api-key": process.env.API_KEY ?? "local-dev-key" },
  },
  webServer: [
    {
      command: "npm run start",
      url: `${baseURL}/health`,
      reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
      timeout: 30_000,
    },
    {
      // A second API whose queue doesn't exist: fault injection by config.
      command: "npm run start",
      url: "http://localhost:3001/health",
      reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
      timeout: 30_000,
      env: {
        PORT: "3001",
        TRANSFERS_QUEUE_NAME: "ledgerline-queue-that-does-not-exist",
      },
    },
    {
      // A third API that publishes to a queue nobody reads.
      command: "npm run start",
      url: "http://localhost:3003/health",
      reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
      timeout: 30_000,
      env: {
        PORT: "3003",
        TRANSFERS_QUEUE_NAME: "ledgerline-transfers-inspect",
      },
    },
    {
      // The processor, doing locally what the Lambda does in AWS.
      command: "npm run processor",
      url: "http://localhost:3002/health",
      reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
      timeout: 30_000,
    },
  ],
});

Replace tests/api/external-transfers.spec.ts:

tests/api/external-transfers.spec.ts
import { expectApiError } from "../framework/assertions";
import { assertMatchesContract } from "../framework/contract";
import { expect, test } from "../framework/fixtures";
import { CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID, SUPPLIER_BANK } from "../framework/test-data";

// The queue tests use the inspect API, whose queue nobody reads, so messages
// stay put. They share that queue, so they take turns and start by emptying it.
test.describe.configure({ mode: "serial" });

test.describe("payments to other banks", () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ inspectQueue }) => {
    await inspectQueue.drain();
  });

  test("are accepted with 202 and wait as pending", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();

    const { status, body } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: SUPPLIER_BANK,
    });

    expect(status).toBe(202);
    expect(body).toMatchObject({
      kind: "external",
      status: "pending",
      amountCents: 2_500,
      toAccountId: CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID,
      counterparty: {
        name: SUPPLIER_BANK.name,
        routingNumber: SUPPLIER_BANK.routingNumber,
        accountLast4: "6789",
      },
    });
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(7_500);
  });

  test("put a message on the queue that matches the contract", async ({
    inspectApi,
    newAccount,
    inspectQueue,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
    const { body: transfer } = await inspectApi.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: SUPPLIER_BANK,
    });

    const message = await inspectQueue.takeMessageFor(transfer.id);

    assertMatchesContract(
      "TransferRequestedMessage",
      message.body,
      "the transfers queue",
    );
    expect(message.body).toMatchObject({
      transferId: transfer.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: SUPPLIER_BANK,
    });
    expect(message.correlationId).toBe(message.body.correlationId);
  });

  test("never return the full account number", async ({ api, newAccount }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();

    const { body } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 100,
      counterparty: SUPPLIER_BANK,
    });

    expect(JSON.stringify(body)).not.toContain(SUPPLIER_BANK.accountNumber);
  });

  test("refuse a payment over the balance and send nothing", async ({
    inspectApi,
    newAccount,
    inspectQueue,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();

    const result = await inspectApi.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 1_001,
      counterparty: SUPPLIER_BANK,
    });

    expectApiError(result, 422, "insufficient_funds");
    expect(await inspectQueue.isEmpty()).toBe(true);
  });

  const badDetails = [
    {
      label: "an 8-digit routing number",
      change: { routingNumber: "02100002" },
    },
    {
      label: "letters in the account number",
      change: { accountNumber: "12AB5678" },
    },
    { label: "an empty name", change: { name: "" } },
  ];

  for (const { label, change } of badDetails) {
    test(`reject ${label}`, async ({ api, newAccount }) => {
      const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();

      const result = await api.createExternalTransfer({
        fromAccountId: from.id,
        amountCents: 100,
        counterparty: { ...SUPPLIER_BANK, ...change },
      });

      expectApiError(result, 400, "validation_error");
    });
  }

  test("roll back completely when the queue is down", async ({
    api,
    brokenQueueApi,
    newAccount,
    db,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();

    const result = await brokenQueueApi.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: SUPPLIER_BANK,
    });

    expectApiError(result, 503, "queue_unavailable");
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(10_000);
    expect(await db.countTransfersFrom(from.id)).toBe(0);
  });
});

Create tests/api/processor.spec.ts:

tests/api/processor.spec.ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { expect, test } from "../framework/fixtures";

// Each test waits for the processor to act, then checks the result.
// They run one at a time so the failure tests' retries don't slow the others.
test.describe.configure({ mode: "serial" });

test.describe("the payment processor", () => {
  test("sends a payment to the partner and marks it submitted", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
  }) => {
    await partner.accepts();
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();

    const { body: transfer } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });

    await expect
      .poll(async () => (await api.getTransfer(transfer.id)).body.status)
      .toBe("submitted");
    const requests = await partner.requests();
    expect(requests).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(requests[0].body).toEqual({
      transferId: transfer.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });
    expect(requests[0].headers["idempotency-key"]).toBe(transfer.id);
    expect((await api.getTransfer(transfer.id)).body.partnerReference).toBe(
      "ACH-7F3A2B",
    );
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(7_500);
  });

  test("retries after a server error, then succeeds", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
  }) => {
    await partner.failsOnceThenAccepts();
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();

    const { body: transfer } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });

    await expect
      .poll(async () => (await api.getTransfer(transfer.id)).body.status, {
        timeout: 15_000,
      })
      .toBe("submitted");
    expect(await partner.requests()).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  test("gives up after three failures, returns the money, and parks the message", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    deadLetterQueue,
  }) => {
    await partner.failsWith(500);
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();

    const { body: transfer } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });

    await expect
      .poll(async () => (await api.getTransfer(transfer.id)).body.status, {
        timeout: 20_000,
      })
      .toBe("failed");
    expect(await partner.requests()).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(10_000);
    const parked = await deadLetterQueue.takeMessageFor(transfer.id, 15_000);
    expect(parked.body.transferId).toBe(transfer.id);
  });

  test("doesn't retry a rejection, and returns the money", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
  }) => {
    await partner.rejects("invalid_account");
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();

    const { body: transfer } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });

    await expect
      .poll(async () => (await api.getTransfer(transfer.id)).body.status)
      .toBe("rejected");
    const { body } = await api.getTransfer(transfer.id);
    expect(body.statusReason).toBe("invalid_account");
    expect(await partner.requests()).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(10_000);
  });

  test("sends a payment only once, even when the message arrives twice", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    transfersQueue,
  }) => {
    await partner.accepts();
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
    const { body: transfer } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });
    await expect
      .poll(async () => (await api.getTransfer(transfer.id)).body.status)
      .toBe("submitted");

    // At-least-once delivery: the same message shows up again.
    await transfersQueue.send(
      JSON.stringify({
        version: 1,
        type: "transfer.requested",
        transferId: transfer.id,
        correlationId: randomUUID(),
        amountCents: 2_500,
        counterparty: partner.counterparty,
      }),
    );
    await expect
      .poll(() => transfersQueue.isIdle(), { timeout: 15_000 })
      .toBe(true);

    expect(await partner.requests()).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(7_500);
  });

  test("parks an unreadable message in the dead-letter queue", async ({
    transfersQueue,
    deadLetterQueue,
  }) => {
    const garbage = `not a transfer ${randomUUID()}`;

    await transfersQueue.send(garbage);

    const parked = await deadLetterQueue.takeMessage(
      (raw) => raw === garbage,
      20_000,
    );
    expect(parked.raw).toBe(garbage);
  });
});

npm run format
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run test:api

50 passed. The run takes about 30 seconds, because the failure tests wait through real retries.

What the tests prove

  • Submitted: the bank received exactly one request, with exactly the right body and an idempotency-key equal to the transfer id.
  • Fails once, then works: the processor retried, and the bank saw two requests.
  • Fails every time: three requests, then failed, the money back in the account, and the message in the dead-letter queue.
  • Rejected: one request only, no retries, statusReason from the bank, and the money back.
  • Arrives twice: the test puts a copy of the message straight onto the queue, waits until the queue is idle, and checks the bank still saw only one request.
  • Unreadable: garbage on the queue ends up in the dead-letter queue instead of crashing the processor.
  • The ledger integrity tests from Week 2 now also check every reversal, and they still pass.

A few techniques are new: - expect.poll re-runs its function until the value matches or the timeout passes. It's how you test something asynchronous without fixed sleeps. - partner.requests() asks WireMock's request journal what arrived, filtered to this test's payments. - failsOnceThenAccepts uses a WireMock scenario: a stub that changes state after its first match. - isIdle() checks both visible and in-flight counts, so the test knows the duplicate has been fully handled before it asserts.

Try this

Break the first defence against duplicates. In src/processor/handler.ts, comment out the four lines starting at if (status !== "pending"), and run: 

npx playwright test -g "arrives twice"

It fails: the bank received 2 requests. The database stayed correct, thanks to the row lock in recordPartnerOutcome, but the bank was asked to pay twice. That's exactly why the processor also sends the bank an idempotency key. Put the lines back.

Step 29: Deploy it as a real Lambda, and CI

About an hour.

What, why and how: Bundling and deployment packages

What it is. A bundler, esbuild here, follows every import from one starting file and combines that code, and every package it uses, into a single JavaScript file. A deployment package is that file zipped, ready to upload.

Why we use it. Lambda runs what you upload and nothing else: no npm install, and no TypeScript. Bundling turns the processor and everything it uses, including the AWS SDK and the Postgres driver, into one plain JavaScript file that runs anywhere Node does.

How we use it. npm run lambda:deploy bundles src/processor/handler.ts into dist/processor/index.js, zips it, and uploads it to MiniStack. The dist/ folder is build output, so Git ignores it.

How it works inside. esbuild starts at the entry file and follows every import to build a graph of all the code that can be reached. It strips the TypeScript types and writes everything into one file, ordered so each module is defined before it's used. Files nothing imports never make it in. It's written in Go and does all of this in a fraction of a second, which is why it's a popular way to build Lambdas.

The tests run the handler through the local runner. Deploying it into MiniStack as a real Lambda proves the packaging works too: the bundle, the handler name, the environment variables and the SQS trigger. This is a smoke test: one quick end-to-end check that the deployed thing works at all. 

npm install -D esbuild@0
npm install @aws-sdk/client-lambda@3
echo "dist/" >> .gitignore

The bundle goes in dist/, which the linter would otherwise try to check, with hundreds of errors. Replace eslint.config.mjs so it skips that folder:

eslint.config.mjs
import eslint from "@eslint/js";
import { defineConfig } from "eslint/config";
import prettier from "eslint-config-prettier";
import tseslint from "typescript-eslint";

export default defineConfig(
  {
    ignores: ["node_modules/", "playwright-report/", "test-results/", "dist/"],
  },
  eslint.configs.recommended,

);

Create scripts/lambda-deploy.ts:

scripts/lambda-deploy.ts
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import {
  CreateEventSourceMappingCommand,
  CreateFunctionCommand,
  GetFunctionCommand,
  LambdaClient,
  ListEventSourceMappingsCommand,
  UpdateFunctionCodeCommand,
  UpdateFunctionConfigurationCommand,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-lambda";
import {
  GetQueueAttributesCommand,
  GetQueueUrlCommand,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-sqs";
import { build } from "esbuild";
import { sqs, TRANSFERS_QUEUE } from "../src/queue";

const FUNCTION_NAME = "ledgerline-processor";
const OUT_DIR = "dist/processor";

const lambda = new LambdaClient({
  region: process.env.AWS_REGION ?? "us-east-1",
  endpoint: process.env.AWS_ENDPOINT_URL ?? "http://localhost:4566",
  credentials: { accessKeyId: "test", secretAccessKey: "test" },
});

// Where the Lambda finds everything, from wherever it runs. See the handbook:
// inside Docker, "localhost" means the container, not your machine.
const environment = {
  DATABASE_URL:
    process.env.LAMBDA_DATABASE_URL ??
    "postgres://ledgerline:ledgerline@localhost:5432/ledgerline",
  PARTNER_URL: process.env.LAMBDA_PARTNER_URL ?? "http://localhost:8080",
  AWS_ENDPOINT_URL:
    process.env.LAMBDA_AWS_ENDPOINT_URL ?? "http://localhost:4566",
};

async function deploy() {
  // 1. Bundle the handler and everything it imports into one file, and zip it.
  mkdirSync(OUT_DIR, { recursive: true });
  await build({
    entryPoints: ["src/processor/handler.ts"],
    outfile: `${OUT_DIR}/index.js`,
    bundle: true,
    platform: "node",
    target: "node22",
    format: "cjs",
  });
  execFileSync("zip", [
    "-q",
    "-j",
    `${OUT_DIR}/function.zip`,
    `${OUT_DIR}/index.js`,
  ]);
  const zip = readFileSync(`${OUT_DIR}/function.zip`);

  // 2. Create the function, or update it if it already exists.
  const exists = await lambda
    .send(new GetFunctionCommand({ FunctionName: FUNCTION_NAME }))
    .then(() => true)
    .catch(() => false);
  if (exists) {
    await lambda.send(
      new UpdateFunctionCodeCommand({
        FunctionName: FUNCTION_NAME,
        ZipFile: zip,
      }),
    );
    await lambda.send(
      new UpdateFunctionConfigurationCommand({
        FunctionName: FUNCTION_NAME,
        Environment: { Variables: environment },
      }),
    );
  } else {
    await lambda.send(
      new CreateFunctionCommand({
        FunctionName: FUNCTION_NAME,
        Runtime: "nodejs22.x",
        Handler: "index.handler",
        Role: "arn:aws:iam::000000000000:role/ledgerline-processor",
        Code: { ZipFile: zip },
        Timeout: 30,
        Environment: { Variables: environment },
      }),
    );
  }

  // 3. Connect it to the queue, reporting partial batch failures.
  const { QueueUrl } = await sqs.send(
    new GetQueueUrlCommand({ QueueName: TRANSFERS_QUEUE }),
  );
  const { Attributes } = await sqs.send(
    new GetQueueAttributesCommand({ QueueUrl, AttributeNames: ["QueueArn"] }),
  );
  const { EventSourceMappings = [] } = await lambda.send(
    new ListEventSourceMappingsCommand({ FunctionName: FUNCTION_NAME }),
  );
  if (EventSourceMappings.length === 0) {
    await lambda.send(
      new CreateEventSourceMappingCommand({
        FunctionName: FUNCTION_NAME,
        EventSourceArn: Attributes?.QueueArn,
        BatchSize: 10,
        FunctionResponseTypes: ["ReportBatchItemFailures"],
      }),
    );
  }

  console.log(`Deployed ${FUNCTION_NAME}, triggered by ${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}`);
}

deploy().catch((error) => {
  console.error("Deploy failed:", error);
  process.exitCode = 1;
});

Create scripts/lambda-remove.ts:

scripts/lambda-remove.ts
import {
  DeleteEventSourceMappingCommand,
  DeleteFunctionCommand,
  LambdaClient,
  ListEventSourceMappingsCommand,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-lambda";

const FUNCTION_NAME = "ledgerline-processor";

const lambda = new LambdaClient({
  region: process.env.AWS_REGION ?? "us-east-1",
  endpoint: process.env.AWS_ENDPOINT_URL ?? "http://localhost:4566",
  credentials: { accessKeyId: "test", secretAccessKey: "test" },
});

// Removes the deployed Lambda, so the local processor is the only consumer
// of the queue again. Run this before npm run test:api.
async function remove() {
  const { EventSourceMappings = [] } = await lambda.send(
    new ListEventSourceMappingsCommand({ FunctionName: FUNCTION_NAME }),
  );
  for (const mapping of EventSourceMappings) {
    await lambda.send(
      new DeleteEventSourceMappingCommand({ UUID: mapping.UUID }),
    );
  }
  await lambda
    .send(new DeleteFunctionCommand({ FunctionName: FUNCTION_NAME }))
    .catch(() => undefined);
  console.log(`Removed ${FUNCTION_NAME}`);
}

remove().catch((error) => {
  console.error("Remove failed:", error);
  process.exitCode = 1;
});

npm pkg set scripts.lambda:deploy="tsx scripts/lambda-deploy.ts" scripts.lambda:remove="tsx scripts/lambda-remove.ts"

The smoke test

Stop the local processor if it's running (Ctrl+C in its terminal), so the Lambda is the only thing reading the queue. Then: 

npm run lambda:deploy

Deployed ledgerline-processor, triggered by ledgerline-transfers

With npm run dev running, send a payment with the curl from Step 23, wait a few seconds, and check its status as in Step 27. It should be "submitted". Then remove the Lambda, so tests go back to using the local processor: 

npm run lambda:remove

What the deploy script does

  • esbuild bundles the handler and everything it imports, including the AWS SDK and the Postgres driver, into one file. Lambda runs that single file.
  • zip packages it, because Lambda takes code as a zip. It's built into macOS; on Ubuntu, sudo apt install zip.
  • CreateFunctionCommand registers the function: runtime nodejs22.x, handler index.handler (the file, then the exported function), a 30-second timeout, and environment variables. MiniStack doesn't check the role, but real AWS would.
  • CreateEventSourceMappingCommand connects the queue to the function, with ReportBatchItemFailures so partial batch responses work.
  • Running it twice updates the code instead of failing.

Verify on your machine

I ran this smoke test with MiniStack installed directly on the machine, where it runs Lambdas as local processes, and the payment was submitted within 3 seconds. Your MiniStack runs in Docker, where Lambdas can behave differently, so this step is yours to verify.

Pass: npm run lambda:deploy prints the line above, the payment becomes "submitted" within about 10 seconds, and docker compose logs ministack | grep -i lambda shows the function being started and processing a message.

Fail: the status stays pending, and the logs mention Docker or a runtime that can't be found. MiniStack in Docker may need to start containers of its own to run Lambdas. In docker-compose.yml, add a volumes entry to the ministack service, - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock, then run docker compose up -d and deploy again.

Fail: the logs show ECONNREFUSED to port 5432, 8080 or 4566. The Lambda is running inside a container, where localhost means the container itself. Deploy again, pointing it at your machine: 

LAMBDA_DATABASE_URL=postgres://ledgerline:ledgerline@host.docker.internal:5432/ledgerline LAMBDA_PARTNER_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8080 LAMBDA_AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=http://host.docker.internal:4566 npm run lambda:deploy

Either way, always run npm run lambda:remove before npm run test:api. If the Lambda and the local processor both read the queue, the processor tests become flaky.

README.md
# Ledgerline

A small business-banking backend, and the automated test framework around it.
Built to practise how fintech teams test money movement: ledgers, contracts,
concurrency and CI.

## Run it

You need Docker Desktop and Node 24.

```bash
npm install
npm run db:up        # start Postgres, MiniStack and WireMock in Docker
npm run db:migrate   # create the tables
npm run aws:setup    # create the queues in MiniStack
npm test             # unit tests, then API tests (the API starts automatically)
```

Run the API on its own with `npm run dev`, then try `curl localhost:3000/health`.

## How the tests are organised

```
tests/
  unit/        Vitest. Pure functions, no network or database.
  api/         Playwright specs. Each file covers one feature.
  framework/   The plumbing specs are built on:
    fixtures.ts           api, newAccount, apiWithKey, db
    ledgerline-client.ts  one method per endpoint
    contract.ts           checks every response against openapi.yaml
    account-builder.ts    newAccount().withBalance(5000).create()
    db-helper.ts          ledger integrity queries
    queue-helper.ts       reads and writes queues in MiniStack
    fake-partner.ts       programs WireMock to act as the partner bank
    assertions.ts         expectApiError(result, 422, "insufficient_funds")
bruno/         Bruno collection for exploring the API by hand
infra/wiremock/  the fake partner bank's default stubs
src/processor/   the Lambda that sends payments to the partner bank
openapi.yaml   The API contract
```

## Add a test

1. Pick the spec file for the feature, or create `tests/api/<feature>.spec.ts`.
2. Import `{ test, expect }` from `../framework/fixtures`.
3. Set up data with `newAccount()`, act with `api`, assert on the result.

```ts
test("rejects a transfer over the balance", async ({ api, newAccount }) => {
  const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();
  const to = await newAccount().create();

  const result = await api.createTransfer({
    fromAccountId: from.id,
    toAccountId: to.id,
    amountCents: 1_001,
  });

  expectApiError(result, 422, "insufficient_funds");
});
```

Every test creates its own accounts, so tests run in parallel and in any order.
