Week 6: Duplicates, webhooks and returns

Phase 2 ends with the three things that break payment systems in real life: requests that arrive twice, news that arrives days later, and messages from someone pretending to be the bank. You'll add idempotency keys to the API, signed webhooks from the partner bank, and settlement and returns in the ledger. Chapters 15, 16 and 17 of the field guide cover the ideas.

Step 30: Idempotency keys with DynamoDB

About two hours.

What, why and how: DynamoDB

What it is. DynamoDB is AWS's key-value database. Each item is a set of attributes found by its key, like a very large, very fast dictionary. There are no tables joined together and no SQL: you put, get, update and delete items by their key.

Why we use it. Idempotency keys need three things: fast lookup by one exact key, automatic expiry, and a guarantee that two requests can't both claim the same key. DynamoDB does all three. It's also in Relay's stack.

How we use it. The table ledgerline-idempotency-keys lives in MiniStack, and npm run aws:setup creates it. Three features matter here:

  • Conditional writes: ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(pk)" means "only save this if no item with this key exists yet". If ten requests try at once, one succeeds and nine get a ConditionalCheckFailedException.
  • TTL (time to live): DynamoDB deletes an item on its own once the time in its expiresAt attribute has passed.
  • The document client, from @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb, lets you pass ordinary JavaScript objects instead of DynamoDB's own typed format.

How it works inside. DynamoDB spreads a table across many storage partitions, using a hash of each item's key to pick the partition that holds it. That's how it stays fast at any size: getting an item by its key is a direct lookup, never a search. A conditional write is checked and applied by the partition that owns the item, as one step, so two writes racing for the same key are strictly ordered, and exactly one of them sees "no item yet". TTL deletion runs in the background, usually within a few days of the expiry time, not to the second, so code must never depend on an expired item being gone. Ledgerline doesn't: an old key simply stops mattering.

A client sends a payment, the connection drops, and it can't tell whether the payment happened. If it simply retries, the customer may pay twice. With an idempotency key, the client sends a unique key in a header, and Ledgerline remembers the first response for that key. A retry with the same key gets that response back, and no second transfer is made. The idempotency primer in Step 27 explains the idea; this step builds it into the API.

Here's how the wrapper handles a request with a key:

  1. Claim the key in DynamoDB with a conditional write. Only one request can ever win that claim.
  2. If this request won, it does the work, stores the response, and sends it. A refusal, like insufficient funds, is stored too: the same request gets the same answer. A server error isn't stored, so the client can retry.
  3. If the key was already claimed, the wrapper compares fingerprints. A different request with the same key gets a 422. A request still being processed gets a 409, so the client should try again shortly. Otherwise, the stored response is sent again, with an idempotent-replayed: true header. 
npm install @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb@3 @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb@3

Create src/aws.ts, which holds the settings every AWS client shares:

src/aws.ts
// Settings shared by every AWS client. Locally and in CI they point at
// MiniStack, which accepts any credentials. For real AWS, leave the endpoint
// unset and provide real credentials through environment variables.
export const awsConfig = {
  region: process.env.AWS_REGION ?? "us-east-1",
  endpoint: process.env.AWS_ENDPOINT_URL ?? "http://localhost:4566",
  credentials: {
    accessKeyId: process.env.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID ?? "test",
    secretAccessKey: process.env.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY ?? "test",
  },
};

Replace src/queue.ts, which now uses those shared settings:

src/queue.ts
import {
  GetQueueUrlCommand,
  SendMessageCommand,
  SQSClient,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-sqs";
import { awsConfig } from "./aws";

export const sqs = new SQSClient(awsConfig);

export const TRANSFERS_QUEUE =
  process.env.TRANSFERS_QUEUE_NAME ?? "ledgerline-transfers";

// The message the API sends when a customer pays another bank. The "version"
// field lets the format change later without breaking older processors.
export interface TransferRequestedMessage {
  version: 1;
  type: "transfer.requested";
  transferId: string;
  correlationId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  counterparty: { name: string; routingNumber: string; accountNumber: string };
}

let queueUrl: string | undefined;

async function transfersQueueUrl(): Promise<string> {
  if (!queueUrl) {
    const result = await sqs.send(
      new GetQueueUrlCommand({ QueueName: TRANSFERS_QUEUE }),
    );
    if (!result.QueueUrl) throw new Error(`No URL for ${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}`);
    queueUrl = result.QueueUrl;
  }
  return queueUrl;
}

export async function publishTransferRequested(
  message: TransferRequestedMessage,
): Promise<void> {
  await sqs.send(
    new SendMessageCommand({
      QueueUrl: await transfersQueueUrl(),
      MessageBody: JSON.stringify(message),
      MessageAttributes: {
        correlationId: {
          DataType: "String",
          StringValue: message.correlationId,
        },
      },
    }),
  );
}

Create src/idempotency.ts:

src/idempotency.ts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { DynamoDBClient } from "@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb";
import {
  DeleteCommand,
  DynamoDBDocumentClient,
  GetCommand,
  PutCommand,
} from "@aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb";
import type { FastifyReply, FastifyRequest } from "fastify";
import { awsConfig } from "./aws";
import { AppError } from "./errors";

export const IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE =
  process.env.IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE ?? "ledgerline-idempotency-keys";
const KEEP_FOR_SECONDS = 24 * 60 * 60;

const dynamo = DynamoDBDocumentClient.from(new DynamoDBClient(awsConfig), {
  marshallOptions: { removeUndefinedValues: true },
});

export interface Outcome {
  statusCode: number;
  body: unknown;
}

// Wraps a route so that repeating a request with the same Idempotency-Key
// header returns the first response instead of doing the work again.
export async function idempotent(
  request: FastifyRequest,
  reply: FastifyReply,
  work: () => Promise<Outcome>,
) {
  const key = request.headers["idempotency-key"];
  if (key === undefined) return send(reply, await work());
  if (typeof key !== "string" || key.length === 0 || key.length > 255) {
    throw new AppError(
      400,
      "validation_error",
      "Idempotency-Key must be 1 to 255 characters",
    );
  }

  // A fingerprint of the request, so the same key can't be reused for a
  // different request by mistake.
  const fingerprint = createHash("sha256")
    .update(`${request.method} ${request.url} ${JSON.stringify(request.body)}`)
    .digest("hex");
  const expiresAt = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + KEEP_FOR_SECONDS;

  // Claim the key. The condition makes this atomic: if ten requests arrive at
  // once with the same key, exactly one of them gets past this line.
  try {
    await dynamo.send(
      new PutCommand({
        TableName: IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE,
        Item: { pk: key, fingerprint, state: "in_progress", expiresAt },
        ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(pk)",
      }),
    );
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as Error).name !== "ConditionalCheckFailedException")
      throw error;
    return replay(reply, key, fingerprint);
  }

  let outcome: Outcome;
  try {
    outcome = await work();
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof AppError && error.statusCode < 500) {
      // A refusal is an answer too: the same request gets the same refusal.
      await remember(key, fingerprint, expiresAt, {
        statusCode: error.statusCode,
        body: { error: error.code, message: error.message },
      });
    } else {
      // Our fault, not the client's: free the key so a retry can succeed.
      await dynamo.send(
        new DeleteCommand({ TableName: IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE, Key: { pk: key } }),
      );
    }
    throw error;
  }

  await remember(key, fingerprint, expiresAt, outcome);
  return send(reply, outcome);
}

async function replay(reply: FastifyReply, key: string, fingerprint: string) {
  const { Item } = await dynamo.send(
    new GetCommand({ TableName: IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE, Key: { pk: key } }),
  );
  if (Item && Item.fingerprint !== fingerprint) {
    throw new AppError(
      422,
      "idempotency_key_reused",
      "This Idempotency-Key was already used for a different request",
    );
  }
  if (!Item || Item.state !== "completed") {
    throw new AppError(
      409,
      "request_in_progress",
      "A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed",
    );
  }
  reply.header("idempotent-replayed", "true");
  return send(reply, { statusCode: Item.statusCode, body: Item.body });
}

async function remember(
  key: string,
  fingerprint: string,
  expiresAt: number,
  outcome: Outcome,
) {
  await dynamo.send(
    new PutCommand({
      TableName: IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE,
      Item: {
        pk: key,
        fingerprint,
        state: "completed",
        statusCode: outcome.statusCode,
        body: outcome.body,
        expiresAt,
      },
    }),
  );
}

function send(reply: FastifyReply, outcome: Outcome) {
  return reply.code(outcome.statusCode).send(outcome.body);
}

Replace scripts/aws-setup.ts, which now also creates the DynamoDB table:

scripts/aws-setup.ts
import {
  CreateQueueCommand,
  GetQueueAttributesCommand,
  ListQueuesCommand,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-sqs";
import {
  CreateTableCommand,
  DynamoDBClient,
  UpdateTimeToLiveCommand,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb";
import { awsConfig } from "../src/aws";
import { IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE } from "../src/idempotency";
import { sqs, TRANSFERS_QUEUE } from "../src/queue";

const dynamo = new DynamoDBClient(awsConfig);

const DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE = `${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}-dlq`;
const INSPECT_QUEUE = `${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}-inspect`;

// MiniStack can take a few seconds to start, especially in CI.
async function waitForMiniStack() {
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 30; attempt++) {
    try {
      await sqs.send(new ListQueuesCommand({}));
      return;
    } catch {
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
    }
  }
  throw new Error("MiniStack didn't answer on port 4566. Is it running?");
}

async function setup() {
  await waitForMiniStack();

  // The dead-letter queue first, because the main queue points at it.
  const dlq = await sqs.send(
    new CreateQueueCommand({ QueueName: DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE }),
  );
  const { Attributes } = await sqs.send(
    new GetQueueAttributesCommand({
      QueueUrl: dlq.QueueUrl,
      AttributeNames: ["QueueArn"],
    }),
  );

  // After 3 failed receives, SQS moves a message to the dead-letter queue.
  await sqs.send(
    new CreateQueueCommand({
      QueueName: TRANSFERS_QUEUE,
      Attributes: {
        VisibilityTimeout: "30",
        RedrivePolicy: JSON.stringify({
          deadLetterTargetArn: Attributes?.QueueArn,
          maxReceiveCount: 3,
        }),
      },
    }),
  );

  // A queue nobody reads from. Tests point a copy of the API at it, so they
  // can inspect messages before the processor takes them.
  await sqs.send(new CreateQueueCommand({ QueueName: INSPECT_QUEUE }));

  console.log(
    `Queues ready: ${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}, ${DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE} and ${INSPECT_QUEUE}`,
  );

  // The idempotency table: one item per key, found by its "pk" attribute.
  try {
    await dynamo.send(
      new CreateTableCommand({
        TableName: IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE,
        AttributeDefinitions: [{ AttributeName: "pk", AttributeType: "S" }],
        KeySchema: [{ AttributeName: "pk", KeyType: "HASH" }],
        BillingMode: "PAY_PER_REQUEST",
      }),
    );
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as Error).name !== "ResourceInUseException") throw error;
  }
  // Items delete themselves once their expiresAt time has passed.
  try {
    await dynamo.send(
      new UpdateTimeToLiveCommand({
        TableName: IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE,
        TimeToLiveSpecification: { Enabled: true, AttributeName: "expiresAt" },
      }),
    );
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as Error).name !== "ValidationException") throw error;
  }
  console.log(`Table ready: ${IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE}`);
}

setup().catch((error) => {
  console.error("AWS setup failed:", error);
  process.exitCode = 1;
});

Replace src/routes/transfers.ts and src/routes/external-transfers.ts, which wrap their work in idempotent:

src/routes/transfers.ts
import type { FastifyInstance } from "fastify";
import { idempotent } from "../idempotency";
import { getTransfer, moveMoney } from "../ledger";
import { amountCents, idParams } from "./schemas";

interface CreateTransferBody {
  fromAccountId: string;
  toAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
}

export async function transferRoutes(app: FastifyInstance) {
  app.post<{ Body: CreateTransferBody }>(
    "/transfers",
    {
      schema: {
        body: {
          type: "object",
          required: ["fromAccountId", "toAccountId", "amountCents"],
          additionalProperties: false,
          properties: {
            fromAccountId: { type: "string", format: "uuid" },
            toAccountId: { type: "string", format: "uuid" },
            amountCents,
          },
        },
      },
    },
    async (request, reply) =>
      idempotent(request, reply, async () => {
        const transfer = await moveMoney({ kind: "internal", ...request.body });
        return { statusCode: 201, body: transfer };
      }),
  );

  app.get<{ Params: { id: string } }>(
    "/transfers/:id",
    { schema: { params: idParams } },
    async (request) => getTransfer(request.params.id),
  );
}
src/routes/external-transfers.ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import type { FastifyInstance } from "fastify";
import { AppError } from "../errors";
import { idempotent } from "../idempotency";
import { CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID, moveMoney, type Counterparty } from "../ledger";
import { publishTransferRequested } from "../queue";
import { amountCents } from "./schemas";

interface ExternalTransferBody {
  fromAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  counterparty: Counterparty;
}

export async function externalTransferRoutes(app: FastifyInstance) {
  app.post<{ Body: ExternalTransferBody }>(
    "/transfers/external",
    {
      schema: {
        body: {
          type: "object",
          required: ["fromAccountId", "amountCents", "counterparty"],
          additionalProperties: false,
          properties: {
            fromAccountId: { type: "string", format: "uuid" },
            amountCents,
            counterparty: {
              type: "object",
              required: ["name", "routingNumber", "accountNumber"],
              additionalProperties: false,
              properties: {
                name: { type: "string", minLength: 1, maxLength: 100 },
                routingNumber: { type: "string", pattern: "^[0-9]{9}$" },
                accountNumber: { type: "string", pattern: "^[0-9]{4,17}$" },
              },
            },
          },
        },
      },
    },
    async (request, reply) =>
      idempotent(request, reply, async () => {
        // One id that follows this payment through every log and message.
        const correlationId = randomUUID();
        const { fromAccountId, counterparty } = request.body;

        const transfer = await moveMoney({
          kind: "external",
          fromAccountId,
          toAccountId: CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID,
          amountCents: request.body.amountCents,
          status: "pending",
          counterparty,
          // Publish before COMMIT. If the queue is down, the transfer rolls
          // back, so there's never a pending payment nobody will process.
          beforeCommit: async (saved) => {
            try {
              await publishTransferRequested({
                version: 1,
                type: "transfer.requested",
                transferId: saved.id,
                correlationId,
                amountCents: saved.amountCents,
                counterparty,
              });
            } catch (error) {
              request.log.error(
                { err: error, correlationId },
                "could not publish the transfer message",
              );
              throw new AppError(
                503,
                "queue_unavailable",
                "Payments to other banks are unavailable right now. Nothing was sent.",
              );
            }
          },
        });

        request.log.info(
          { transferId: transfer.id, correlationId },
          "external transfer accepted",
        );
        reply.header("x-correlation-id", correlationId);
        return { statusCode: 202, body: transfer };
      }),
  );
}

Queues ready: ledgerline-transfers, ledgerline-transfers-dlq and ledgerline-transfers-inspect
Table ready: ledgerline-idempotency-keys

What the code does

  • attribute_not_exists(pk) is the heart of it. DynamoDB checks and writes in one atomic step, so ten requests arriving at once with the same key can't all claim it.
  • The fingerprint is a SHA-256 hash of the method, URL and body. Reusing a key for a different request is a client bug, and it's refused rather than quietly answered with the wrong response.
  • expiresAt makes DynamoDB delete each key after 24 hours, so the table doesn't grow forever.
  • removeUndefinedValues stops the document client from failing on optional fields that happen to be missing.
  • The routes now return { statusCode, body } instead of sending the reply themselves, so the wrapper can store exactly what was sent.
  • Requests without a key behave exactly as before. Keys are optional, the way Stripe does it.

Verify on your machine

Step 31: Webhooks, settlement and returns

About two hours.

What, why and how: Webhooks

What it is. A webhook is a partner calling your API when something happens on their side, so you don't have to keep asking them. Here, the partner bank sends Ledgerline an HTTP request when a payment settles or comes back.

Why we use it. Settlement and returns happen hours or days after a payment is sent, on the bank's schedule, and webhooks are how the news arrives. They're also a classic source of bugs: they can arrive twice, out of order, late, or from someone pretending to be the bank.

How we use it. The bank posts events to /webhooks/partner, like {"id":"evt_…","type":"transfer.returned","transferId":"…","returnCode":"R03"}. Ledgerline checks the signature, records the event's id so a resent event changes nothing, checks the change is allowed, and then updates the payment and the ledger. Once the signature checks out, it always answers 200, because any other answer makes the bank send the event again.

How it works inside. A sender like the partner bank treats any answer other than a 2xx, or no answer within a few seconds, as a failure, and sends the event again later, often with growing gaps over hours or days. So a receiver has to answer quickly, has to be safe to receive the same event twice, and can't rely on events arriving in order, because a retried older event can overtake a newer one. Ledgerline answers 200 as soon as it has recorded the event, records each event id only once, and checks every status change against its state machine.

What, why and how: Signatures with HMAC

What it is. An HMAC is a fingerprint of a message, made with a secret key. The sender and the receiver share the secret. The sender computes the fingerprint and sends it along with the message, and the receiver computes it again. If even one character of the message changed, or the wrong secret was used, the two fingerprints don't match.

Why we use it. Anyone on the internet can send a request to your webhook URL. A valid signature proves the event came from someone holding the secret, and that nothing was changed on the way.

How we use it. The partner signs timestamp.body with HMAC-SHA256 and sends the result in the x-partner-signature header, with the timestamp in x-partner-timestamp. Ledgerline refuses events more than five minutes old, so a captured event can't be replayed later. It compares signatures with timingSafeEqual, so response times can't reveal how close a forgery came. Chapter 16 of the field guide computes real signatures you can tamper with.

How it works inside. A hash function like SHA-256 turns any input into a fixed-size fingerprint. Change a single bit of the input and about half the fingerprint changes, and there's no practical way to work backwards from a fingerprint to its input. HMAC mixes the secret key into the hashing twice, in a specific way, so that without the key nobody can produce a valid fingerprint for any message, even after seeing many valid ones. Signing the timestamp together with the body, as timestamp.body, stops replays: an old event's timestamp is too old, and changing the timestamp breaks the signature. Compute real signatures and try to fool the check:

What, why and how: The ACH lifecycle and returns

What it is. ACH is the US network most business payments travel on. A payment is sent in a batch and settles one or two business days later, but it can still come back afterwards as a return, with a code saying why: R01 for insufficient funds, R02 for a closed account, R03 for an account that can't be found.

Why we use it. Settled isn't final. A fintech that treats settlement as the end loses money the day a return arrives for a payment it has already forgotten about. Relay's QA role covers ACH and wire payments specifically.

How we use it. In Ledgerline, a payment goes from pending, to submitted (the bank accepted it), to settled (the money arrived), and possibly to returned. Each change after submitted arrives as a webhook. A settlement moves the money from clearing into a "settled outgoing payments" account. A return moves it back to the customer, from wherever it is at that point. Chapter 17 of the field guide has a timeline you can scrub through.

How it works inside. ACH isn't instant because it works in batches. Ledgerline's bank, called the originating bank, collects payments into files and sends them to an ACH operator, either the Federal Reserve or The Clearing House, at set times through the day. The operator sorts the payments and passes each one to the receiving bank, and the money settles between the banks at fixed settlement times. The receiving bank then has a short window to send a return back along the same path: for most return codes, two banking days after settlement. Nacha's rules set all of those times and codes. Scrub through a payment's days:

What, why and how: State machines

What it is. A state machine lists the states something can be in, and the moves allowed between them. Any move not on the list is refused.

Why we use it. Events arrive out of order. Without explicit rules, a late "settled" event could overwrite a payment that was already returned, and hide the fact that the money came back.

How we use it. ALLOWED_FROM in ledger.ts says a settled event may only move a submitted payment, and a returned event may move a submitted or a settled one. Anything else is recorded, logged and ignored. The tests send events out of order on purpose to prove it.

How it works inside. The whole machine is one lookup table: for each event, the statuses it's allowed to move a payment out of. applyPartnerEvent consults it while holding a row lock on the payment, so two events arriving at once are handled one after the other, and the second is judged against whatever status the first one left behind.

A payment's life now continues after submitted. The bank sends a webhook when it settles, and another if it's returned. Money follows it through the ledger:

Event Status Money moves
Payment accepted by the API pending customer → clearing
Bank accepts it submitted (stays in clearing)
Settled webhook settled clearing → settled outgoing
Returned webhook returned back to the customer, from wherever it is

Create db/migrations/005_settlement_and_returns.sql, then run it:

db/migrations/005_settlement_and_returns.sql 
-- After a payment is submitted, the partner bank reports what happened to it
-- in a webhook: settled (the money arrived) or returned (it came back).
ALTER TABLE transfers DROP CONSTRAINT transfers_status_check;
ALTER TABLE transfers ADD CONSTRAINT transfers_status_check
  CHECK (status IN ('completed', 'pending', 'submitted', 'rejected', 'failed', 'settled', 'returned'));

-- A settlement moves the money out of clearing, because it has now left
-- Ledgerline for good.
ALTER TABLE transfers DROP CONSTRAINT transfers_kind_check;
ALTER TABLE transfers ADD CONSTRAINT transfers_kind_check
  CHECK (kind IN ('deposit', 'internal', 'external', 'reversal', 'settlement'));

ALTER TABLE transfers ADD COLUMN settles_transfer_id uuid REFERENCES transfers (id);

INSERT INTO accounts (id, name, type)
VALUES ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003', 'Settled outgoing payments', 'system');

-- Every webhook event already handled, so a resent event changes nothing.
CREATE TABLE webhook_events (
  id text PRIMARY KEY,
  type text NOT NULL,
  transfer_id uuid NOT NULL,
  received_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

Replace src/ledger.ts. New at the bottom: insertMovement, ALLOWED_FROM and applyPartnerEvent:

src/ledger.ts
import type { PoolClient } from "pg";
import { pool } from "./db";
import { formatCents } from "./domain/money";
import { AppError, notFound } from "./errors";

export const FUNDING_ACCOUNT_ID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001";
export const CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002";
export const SETTLED_ACCOUNT_ID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003";

export type TransferKind =
  "deposit" | "internal" | "external" | "reversal" | "settlement";
export type TransferStatus =
  | "completed"
  | "pending"
  | "submitted"
  | "rejected"
  | "failed"
  | "settled"
  | "returned";

// Where a payment to another bank is going.
export interface Counterparty {
  name: string;
  routingNumber: string;
  accountNumber: string;
}

// What a transfers row looks like coming out of Postgres.
interface TransferRow {
  id: string;
  kind: TransferKind;
  from_account_id: string;
  to_account_id: string;
  amount_cents: string; // bigint arrives as a string, see toCents()
  status: TransferStatus;
  counterparty_name: string | null;
  counterparty_routing: string | null;
  counterparty_account: string | null;
  reverses_transfer_id: string | null;
  settles_transfer_id: string | null;
  partner_reference: string | null;
  status_reason: string | null;
  created_at: Date;
}

// What we send back to API clients.
export interface Transfer {
  id: string;
  kind: TransferKind;
  fromAccountId: string;
  toAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  status: TransferStatus;
  createdAt: string;
  // Only the last four digits ever leave the API.
  counterparty?: { name: string; routingNumber: string; accountLast4: string };
  partnerReference?: string;
  statusReason?: string;
  reversesTransferId?: string;
}

// Postgres bigint can hold numbers JavaScript can't represent exactly, so pg
// returns them as strings. Our amounts are far below that limit, so we convert,
// but refuse loudly if a value ever isn't a safe whole number.
export function toCents(value: string | number): number {
  const cents = Number(value);
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(cents)) {
    throw new Error(`Not a safe whole number of cents: ${value}`);
  }
  return cents;
}

export function toTransfer(row: TransferRow): Transfer {
  const transfer: Transfer = {
    id: row.id,
    kind: row.kind,
    fromAccountId: row.from_account_id,
    toAccountId: row.to_account_id,
    amountCents: toCents(row.amount_cents),
    status: row.status,
    createdAt: row.created_at.toISOString(),
  };
  if (row.counterparty_account) {
    transfer.counterparty = {
      name: row.counterparty_name ?? "",
      routingNumber: row.counterparty_routing ?? "",
      accountLast4: row.counterparty_account.slice(-4),
    };
  }
  if (row.partner_reference) transfer.partnerReference = row.partner_reference;
  if (row.status_reason) transfer.statusReason = row.status_reason;
  if (row.reverses_transfer_id) {
    transfer.reversesTransferId = row.reverses_transfer_id;
  }
  return transfer;
}

type Queryable = Pick<PoolClient, "query">;

export async function getBalance(db: Queryable, accountId: string) {
  const { rows } = await db.query<{ balance: string }>(
    "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents), 0) AS balance FROM ledger_entries WHERE account_id = $1",
    [accountId],
  );
  return toCents(rows[0].balance);
}

export async function getTransfer(id: string): Promise<Transfer> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<TransferRow>(
    "SELECT * FROM transfers WHERE id = $1",
    [id],
  );
  if (rows.length === 0) throw notFound("transfer", id);
  return toTransfer(rows[0]);
}

interface MoveMoneyInput {
  kind: TransferKind;
  fromAccountId: string;
  toAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  status?: TransferStatus;
  counterparty?: Counterparty;
  // Runs inside the transaction, after everything is written but before
  // COMMIT. If it throws, the whole transfer is rolled back.
  beforeCommit?: (transfer: Transfer) => Promise<void>;
}

// The one place money moves. Everything happens inside a database transaction:
// either the transfer and both ledger entries are saved, or nothing is.
export async function moveMoney(input: MoveMoneyInput): Promise<Transfer> {
  if (input.fromAccountId === input.toAccountId) {
    throw new AppError(
      422,
      "same_account",
      "Can't transfer to the same account",
    );
  }

  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query("BEGIN");

    // Lock both account rows until COMMIT, always in the same order (by id).
    // Two transfers touching the same account now take turns instead of both
    // reading the old balance, and opposite transfers can't deadlock.
    const { rows: accounts } = await client.query<{ id: string; type: string }>(
      "SELECT id, type FROM accounts WHERE id = ANY($1::uuid[]) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE",
      [[input.fromAccountId, input.toAccountId]],
    );
    const from = accounts.find((account) => account.id === input.fromAccountId);
    const to = accounts.find((account) => account.id === input.toAccountId);
    if (!from) throw notFound("account", input.fromAccountId);
    if (!to) throw notFound("account", input.toAccountId);

    // Only deposits may draw on a system account.
    if (
      input.kind === "internal" &&
      (from.type !== "customer" || to.type !== "customer")
    ) {
      throw new AppError(
        422,
        "account_not_allowed",
        "Transfers must be between customer accounts",
      );
    }
    if (input.kind === "external" && from.type !== "customer") {
      throw new AppError(
        422,
        "account_not_allowed",
        "Only customer accounts can pay other banks",
      );
    }

    if (from.type === "customer") {
      const balance = await getBalance(client, from.id);
      if (balance < input.amountCents) {
        throw new AppError(
          422,
          "insufficient_funds",
          `Balance is ${formatCents(balance)} but the transfer needs ${formatCents(input.amountCents)}`,
        );
      }
    }

    const { rows } = await client.query<TransferRow>(
      `INSERT INTO transfers (kind, from_account_id, to_account_id, amount_cents, status,
         counterparty_name, counterparty_routing, counterparty_account)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)
       RETURNING *`,
      [
        input.kind,
        input.fromAccountId,
        input.toAccountId,
        input.amountCents,
        input.status ?? "completed",
        input.counterparty?.name ?? null,
        input.counterparty?.routingNumber ?? null,
        input.counterparty?.accountNumber ?? null,
      ],
    );
    const transfer = toTransfer(rows[0]);

    // Double entry: money leaves one account and arrives in the other.
    await client.query(
      "INSERT INTO ledger_entries (account_id, transfer_id, amount_cents) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)",
      [input.fromAccountId, transfer.id, -input.amountCents],
    );
    await client.query(
      "INSERT INTO ledger_entries (account_id, transfer_id, amount_cents) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)",
      [input.toAccountId, transfer.id, input.amountCents],
    );

    if (input.beforeCommit) await input.beforeCommit(transfer);

    await client.query("COMMIT");
    return transfer;
  } catch (error) {
    await client.query("ROLLBACK");
    throw error;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

export type PartnerOutcome =
  | { status: "submitted"; partnerReference: string }
  | { status: "rejected" | "failed"; reason: string };

/** The transfer's current status, or null if it doesn't exist. */
export async function findTransferStatus(
  id: string,
): Promise<TransferStatus | null> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<{ status: TransferStatus }>(
    "SELECT status FROM transfers WHERE id = $1",
    [id],
  );
  return rows[0]?.status ?? null;
}

// Records what the partner bank said about a pending payment. Safe to call
// twice: only a pending transfer can change, so a duplicate message changes
// nothing. A rejected or failed payment sends the money back with a reversal.
export async function recordPartnerOutcome(
  transferId: string,
  outcome: PartnerOutcome,
): Promise<"updated" | "unchanged"> {
  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query("BEGIN");
    const { rows } = await client.query<TransferRow>(
      "SELECT * FROM transfers WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE",
      [transferId],
    );
    const transfer = rows[0];
    if (!transfer || transfer.status !== "pending") {
      await client.query("ROLLBACK");
      return "unchanged";
    }

    if (outcome.status === "submitted") {
      await client.query(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = 'submitted', partner_reference = $2 WHERE id = $1",
        [transferId, outcome.partnerReference],
      );
    } else {
      await client.query(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = $2, status_reason = $3 WHERE id = $1",
        [transferId, outcome.status, outcome.reason],
      );
      // Money goes back from clearing to the customer: a new transfer.
      await insertMovement(client, {
        kind: "reversal",
        fromAccountId: transfer.to_account_id,
        toAccountId: transfer.from_account_id,
        amountCents: toCents(transfer.amount_cents),
        reversesTransferId: transfer.id,
      });
    }

    await client.query("COMMIT");
    return "updated";
  } catch (error) {
    await client.query("ROLLBACK");
    throw error;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

// Writes a completed transfer and its two ledger entries, inside a
// transaction the caller has already started.
async function insertMovement(
  client: PoolClient,
  movement: {
    kind: "reversal" | "settlement";
    fromAccountId: string;
    toAccountId: string;
    amountCents: number;
    reversesTransferId?: string;
    settlesTransferId?: string;
  },
): Promise<void> {
  const { rows } = await client.query<{ id: string }>(
    `INSERT INTO transfers (kind, from_account_id, to_account_id, amount_cents, status,
       reverses_transfer_id, settles_transfer_id)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, 'completed', $5, $6)
     RETURNING id`,
    [
      movement.kind,
      movement.fromAccountId,
      movement.toAccountId,
      movement.amountCents,
      movement.reversesTransferId ?? null,
      movement.settlesTransferId ?? null,
    ],
  );
  await client.query(
    "INSERT INTO ledger_entries (account_id, transfer_id, amount_cents) VALUES ($1, $2, $3), ($4, $2, $5)",
    [
      movement.fromAccountId,
      rows[0].id,
      -movement.amountCents,
      movement.toAccountId,
      movement.amountCents,
    ],
  );
}

export type PartnerEvent =
  | { id: string; type: "transfer.settled"; transferId: string }
  | {
      id: string;
      type: "transfer.returned";
      transferId: string;
      returnCode: string;
    };

export type EventResult = "processed" | "duplicate" | "ignored";

// Which statuses each event may move a payment out of. Anything else is an
// event arriving out of order, and it's ignored.
const ALLOWED_FROM: Record<PartnerEvent["type"], TransferStatus[]> = {
  "transfer.settled": ["submitted"],
  "transfer.returned": ["submitted", "settled"],
};

// Applies one webhook event from the partner bank, exactly once.
export async function applyPartnerEvent(
  event: PartnerEvent,
): Promise<{ result: EventResult; reason?: string }> {
  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query("BEGIN");

    // Record the event first. A resent event hits the primary key, inserts
    // nothing, and is reported as a duplicate.
    const inserted = await client.query(
      "INSERT INTO webhook_events (id, type, transfer_id) VALUES ($1, $2, $3) ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING",
      [event.id, event.type, event.transferId],
    );
    if (inserted.rowCount === 0) {
      await client.query("ROLLBACK");
      return { result: "duplicate" };
    }

    const { rows } = await client.query<TransferRow>(
      "SELECT * FROM transfers WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE",
      [event.transferId],
    );
    const transfer = rows[0];
    if (!transfer || transfer.kind !== "external") {
      await client.query("COMMIT");
      return { result: "ignored", reason: "no such payment" };
    }
    if (!ALLOWED_FROM[event.type].includes(transfer.status)) {
      await client.query("COMMIT");
      return {
        result: "ignored",
        reason: `${event.type} can't follow ${transfer.status}`,
      };
    }

    const amountCents = toCents(transfer.amount_cents);
    if (event.type === "transfer.settled") {
      await client.query(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = 'settled' WHERE id = $1",
        [transfer.id],
      );
      await insertMovement(client, {
        kind: "settlement",
        fromAccountId: CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID,
        toAccountId: SETTLED_ACCOUNT_ID,
        amountCents,
        settlesTransferId: transfer.id,
      });
    } else {
      await client.query(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = 'returned', status_reason = $2 WHERE id = $1",
        [transfer.id, event.returnCode],
      );
      // The money comes back from wherever it is now.
      await insertMovement(client, {
        kind: "reversal",
        fromAccountId:
          transfer.status === "settled"
            ? SETTLED_ACCOUNT_ID
            : CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID,
        toAccountId: transfer.from_account_id,
        amountCents,
        reversesTransferId: transfer.id,
      });
    }

    await client.query("COMMIT");
    return { result: "processed" };
  } catch (error) {
    await client.query("ROLLBACK");
    throw error;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

Create src/routes/webhooks.ts:

src/routes/webhooks.ts
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";
import type { FastifyInstance } from "fastify";
import { AppError } from "../errors";
import { applyPartnerEvent, type PartnerEvent } from "../ledger";

export const WEBHOOK_SECRET =
  process.env.PARTNER_WEBHOOK_SECRET ?? "whsec_local_test";
const MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 300;

declare module "fastify" {
  interface FastifyRequest {
    rawBody?: string;
  }
}

// The partner signs "<timestamp>.<body>" with the shared secret. Signing the
// timestamp too means an old event can't be replayed later.
export function signPayload(secret: string, timestamp: string, body: string) {
  const hmac = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${timestamp}.${body}`);
  return `sha256=${hmac.digest("hex")}`;
}

// Compares in constant time, so the response time never leaks how much of a
// forged signature was right.
function sameSignature(received: string, expected: string) {
  const a = Buffer.from(received);
  const b = Buffer.from(expected);
  return a.length === b.length && timingSafeEqual(a, b);
}

export async function webhookRoutes(app: FastifyInstance) {
  // Keep the exact bytes that arrived: the signature covers the body as sent,
  // not as JSON.parse and JSON.stringify would rebuild it. This parser only
  // applies to the routes in this file.
  app.addContentTypeParser(
    "application/json",
    { parseAs: "string" },
    (request, body, done) => {
      request.rawBody = body as string;
      try {
        done(null, JSON.parse(body as string));
      } catch {
        done(
          new AppError(400, "bad_request", "Body is not valid JSON"),
          undefined,
        );
      }
    },
  );

  // Check the signature before anything else looks at the event.
  app.addHook("preValidation", async (request) => {
    const timestamp = String(request.headers["x-partner-timestamp"] ?? "");
    const signature = String(request.headers["x-partner-signature"] ?? "");
    const age = Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(timestamp));
    if (!timestamp || !Number.isFinite(age) || age > MAX_AGE_SECONDS) {
      throw new AppError(
        401,
        "invalid_signature",
        "Missing or stale timestamp",
      );
    }
    const expected = signPayload(
      WEBHOOK_SECRET,
      timestamp,
      request.rawBody ?? "",
    );
    if (!sameSignature(signature, expected)) {
      throw new AppError(401, "invalid_signature", "Signature doesn't match");
    }
  });

  app.post<{ Body: PartnerEvent }>(
    "/webhooks/partner",
    {
      schema: {
        body: {
          type: "object",
          required: ["id", "type", "transferId"],
          additionalProperties: false,
          properties: {
            id: { type: "string", minLength: 1, maxLength: 100 },
            type: { enum: ["transfer.settled", "transfer.returned"] },
            transferId: { type: "string", format: "uuid" },
            returnCode: { type: "string", pattern: "^R[0-9]{2}$" },
          },
          // A return must say why it came back.
          if: { properties: { type: { const: "transfer.returned" } } },
          then: { required: ["returnCode"] },
        },
      },
    },
    async (request) => {
      const { result, reason } = await applyPartnerEvent(request.body);
      request.log.info(
        {
          eventId: request.body.id,
          transferId: request.body.transferId,
          result,
          reason,
        },
        "partner event handled",
      );
      // Always 200 once the signature checks out, even for ignored events:
      // any other answer makes the partner resend the same event.
      return { result };
    },
  );
}

Replace src/app.ts. Webhooks skip the API key check, because they prove who sent them with a signature instead:

src/app.ts
import Fastify, { type FastifyError } from "fastify";
import { pool } from "./db";
import { AppError } from "./errors";
import { accountRoutes } from "./routes/accounts";
import { externalTransferRoutes } from "./routes/external-transfers";
import { transferRoutes } from "./routes/transfers";
import { webhookRoutes } from "./routes/webhooks";

const API_KEY = process.env.API_KEY ?? "local-dev-key";

export function buildApp() {
  const app = Fastify({
    logger: true,
    ajv: {
      customOptions: {
        // Fastify's defaults quietly turn "2500" into 2500 and drop unknown
        // fields. For money we want strict: wrong types and extra fields fail.
        coerceTypes: false,
        removeAdditional: false,
      },
    },
  });

  // Every route needs the right x-api-key header, except the health check and
  // the partner's webhooks, which prove who sent them with a signature instead.
  app.addHook("onRequest", async (request, reply) => {
    const url = request.routeOptions.url;
    if (url === "/health" || url === "/webhooks/partner") return;
    if (request.headers["x-api-key"] !== API_KEY) {
      return reply
        .code(401)
        .send({ error: "unauthorized", message: "Missing or invalid API key" });
    }
  });

  app.get("/health", async (request, reply) => {
    try {
      await pool.query("SELECT 1");
      return { status: "ok", database: "up" };
    } catch (error) {
      request.log.error({ err: error }, "database health check failed");
      return reply.code(503).send({ status: "degraded", database: "down" });
    }
  });

  app.register(accountRoutes);
  app.register(transferRoutes);
  app.register(externalTransferRoutes);
  app.register(webhookRoutes);

  // Every error leaves the API in the same shape: { error, message }.
  app.setErrorHandler<FastifyError>((error, request, reply) => {
    if (error instanceof AppError) {
      return reply
        .code(error.statusCode)
        .send({ error: error.code, message: error.message });
    }
    if (error.validation) {
      return reply
        .code(400)
        .send({ error: "validation_error", message: error.message });
    }
    if (error.statusCode && error.statusCode < 500) {
      // Things like malformed JSON, which Fastify rejects before our code runs.
      return reply
        .code(error.statusCode)
        .send({ error: "bad_request", message: error.message });
    }
    request.log.error({ err: error }, "unhandled error");
    return reply
      .code(500)
      .send({ error: "internal_error", message: "Something went wrong" });
  });

  app.setNotFoundHandler((request, reply) => {
    reply.code(404).send({
      error: "route_not_found",
      message: `No route for ${request.method} ${request.url}`,
    });
  });

  return app;
}

openapi: 3.1.0
info:

          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/WebhookResult"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"

components:
  securitySchemes:
    apiKey:
      type: apiKey
      in: header
      name: x-api-key

  parameters:
    Id:
      name: id
      in: path
      required: true
      schema:
        type: string
        format: uuid
    IdempotencyKey:
      name: Idempotency-Key
      in: header
      required: false
      description: >
        Send the same key again and you get the first response back, instead
        of a second transfer. Keys are kept for 24 hours.
      schema:
        type: string
        minLength: 1
        maxLength: 255

  responses:
    Error:
      description: The request failed. `error` says why in a stable code.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"

  schemas:
    AmountCents:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100000000

    HealthStatus:
      type: object
      required: [status, database]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [ok, degraded]
        database:
          type: string
          enum: [up, down]

    Account:
      type: object
      required: [id, name, type, balanceCents, createdAt]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        name:
          type: string
        type:
          type: string
          enum: [customer, system]
        balanceCents:
          type: integer
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time

    Transfer:
      type: object
      required:
        [id, kind, fromAccountId, toAccountId, amountCents, status, createdAt]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        kind:
          type: string
          enum: [deposit, internal, external, reversal, settlement]
        fromAccountId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        toAccountId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        amountCents:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/AmountCents"
        status:
          type: string
          enum:
            [completed, pending, submitted, rejected, failed, settled, returned]
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        counterparty:
          type: object
          description: Only on external transfers. Never the full account number.
          required: [name, routingNumber, accountLast4]
          additionalProperties: false
          properties:
            name:
              type: string
            routingNumber:
              type: string
              pattern: "^[0-9]{9}$"
            accountLast4:
              type: string
              pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
        partnerReference:
          type: string
          description: The partner bank's id for a submitted payment
        statusReason:
          type: string
          description: Why a payment was rejected or failed
        reversesTransferId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
          description: On a reversal, the payment it sends money back for

    CounterpartyDetails:
      type: object
      required: [name, routingNumber, accountNumber]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 100
        routingNumber:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{9}$"
        accountNumber:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4,17}$"

    TransferRequestedMessage:
      description: What the API puts on the transfers queue. Not an HTTP response.
      type: object
      required:
        [version, type, transferId, correlationId, amountCents, counterparty]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        version:
          const: 1
        type:
          const: transfer.requested
        transferId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        correlationId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        amountCents:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/AmountCents"
        counterparty:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/CounterpartyDetails"

    PartnerEvent:
      description: What the partner bank sends to /webhooks/partner.
      type: object
      required: [id, type, transferId]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 100
        type:
          enum: [transfer.settled, transfer.returned]
        transferId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        returnCode:
          type: string
          pattern: "^R[0-9]{2}$"
      if:
        properties:
          type:
            const: transfer.returned
      then:
        required: [returnCode]

    WebhookResult:
      type: object
      required: [result]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        result:
          type: string
          enum: [processed, duplicate, ignored]

    Error:
      type: object
      required: [error, message]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        error:
          type: string
          description: Stable code such as insufficient_funds
        message:
          type: string
          description: Human-readable explanation

npm run lint

What the code does

  • The content type parser in webhooks.ts keeps the body exactly as it arrived, in request.rawBody, as well as parsing it. The signature covers the original bytes, and re-serialising parsed JSON can change them. Because it's registered inside the webhook plugin, it only affects this one route.
  • The preValidation hook checks the timestamp and signature before anything else reads the event. Forged requests get a 401 and learn nothing more.
  • The schema then checks the event's shape. if and then say a returned event must include a return code.
  • applyPartnerEvent runs everything in one transaction. It records the event id first, with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a resent event is spotted and reported as a duplicate. Then it locks the payment, checks ALLOWED_FROM, updates the status, and moves the money.
  • Ignored events are still recorded and answered with 200, so the bank stops resending them, and the reason is logged for a person to look at.

Try it by hand

Sign and send an event yourself, using openssl to compute the HMAC. With npm run dev running, and a transfer id from any earlier curl: 

TS=$(date +%s)
BODY='{"id":"evt_manual_1","type":"transfer.settled","transferId":"PASTE-A-TRANSFER-ID"}'
SIG=$(printf '%s.%s' "$TS" "$BODY" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac whsec_local_test | sed 's/^.* //')
curl -s -X POST localhost:3000/webhooks/partner -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "x-partner-timestamp: $TS" -H "x-partner-signature: sha256=$SIG" -d "$BODY"

You'll get a result of processed, or ignored if that transfer can't be settled from its current status. Send the exact same command again and the result is duplicate. Change one character of BODY without re-signing, and you get a 401.

Commit with git add -A && git commit -m "Step 31: Webhooks and returns".

Step 32: Test duplicates, webhooks and returns

About two hours.

The framework gets three additions. The client can send an idempotency key and returns response headers. A PartnerWebhooks helper signs events the way the bank does. And the database helper can list the money movements that followed a payment.

tests/framework/contract.ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import Ajv2020 from "ajv/dist/2020";
import addFormats from "ajv-formats";
import { parse } from "yaml";

// Load openapi.yaml once and teach Ajv (a JSON Schema validator) about it.
const specPath = path.join(__dirname, "..", "..", "openapi.yaml");
const spec = parse(readFileSync(specPath, "utf8"));

// strict: false lets Ajv ignore OpenAPI-only keys like "paths" and "info".
const ajv = new Ajv2020({ allErrors: true, strict: false });
addFormats(ajv);
ajv.addSchema(spec, "openapi");

export type SchemaName =
  | "Account"
  | "Transfer"
  | "Error"
  | "HealthStatus"
  | "TransferRequestedMessage"
  | "WebhookResult";

/** Throws a readable error if body doesn't match the named schema. */
export function assertMatchesContract(
  schemaName: SchemaName,
  body: unknown,
  context: string,
): void {
  const validate = ajv.getSchema(`openapi#/components/schemas/${schemaName}`);
  if (!validate) {
    throw new Error(`openapi.yaml has no schema called ${schemaName}`);
  }
  if (!validate(body)) {
    throw new Error(
      [
        `Contract violation: ${context}`,
        `Expected ${schemaName}: ${ajv.errorsText(validate.errors)}`,
        `Body: ${JSON.stringify(body, null, 2)}`,
      ].join("\n"),
    );
  }
}

tests/framework/ledgerline-client.ts
import type { APIRequestContext, APIResponse } from "@playwright/test";
import { assertMatchesContract, type SchemaName } from "./contract";
import type { Account, HealthStatus, Transfer, WebhookResult } from "./types";

export interface ApiResult<T> {
  status: number;
  body: T;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
}

export interface RequestOptions {
  idempotencyKey?: string;
}

function headersFor(options: RequestOptions): Record<string, string> {
  return options.idempotencyKey
    ? { "idempotency-key": options.idempotencyKey }
    : {};
}

// One method per endpoint. Tests talk to this class, never to raw URLs, so
// when an endpoint changes you fix it here once instead of in every test.
export class LedgerlineClient {
  constructor(private readonly request: APIRequestContext) {}

  health() {
    return this.send<HealthStatus>(
      this.request.get("/health"),
      "HealthStatus",
      "HealthStatus",
    );
  }

  createAccount(name: string) {
    return this.send<Account>(
      this.request.post("/accounts", { data: { name } }),
      "Account",
    );
  }

  getAccount(id: string) {
    return this.send<Account>(this.request.get(`/accounts/${id}`), "Account");
  }

  deposit(accountId: string, amountCents: unknown) {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.post(`/accounts/${accountId}/deposits`, {
        data: { amountCents },
      }),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  // Takes a loose object on purpose, so negative tests can send bad input.
  createTransfer(data: Record<string, unknown>, options: RequestOptions = {}) {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.post("/transfers", { data, headers: headersFor(options) }),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  // Pays a business at another bank. Answers 202: accepted, not finished.
  createExternalTransfer(
    data: Record<string, unknown>,
    options: RequestOptions = {},
  ) {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.post("/transfers/external", {
        data,
        headers: headersFor(options),
      }),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  // Sends a webhook body exactly as given. It's a Buffer so Playwright doesn't
  // re-encode it: the signature covers these exact bytes.
  postPartnerEvent(rawBody: string, headers: Record<string, string>) {
    return this.send<WebhookResult>(
      this.request.post("/webhooks/partner", {
        data: Buffer.from(rawBody),
        headers: { "content-type": "application/json", ...headers },
      }),
      "WebhookResult",
    );
  }

  getTransfer(id: string) {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.get(`/transfers/${id}`),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  async balanceOf(accountId: string): Promise<number> {
    const { status, body } = await this.getAccount(accountId);
    if (status !== 200) {
      throw new Error(`Couldn't read balance of ${accountId}: HTTP ${status}`);
    }
    return body.balanceCents;
  }

  // Every response is checked against openapi.yaml before a test sees it:
  // successes against their resource schema, failures against Error.
  private async send<T>(
    pending: Promise<APIResponse>,
    successSchema: SchemaName,
    errorSchema: SchemaName = "Error",
  ): Promise<ApiResult<T>> {
    const response = await pending;
    const status = response.status();
    const body = await response.json();
    const context = `${response.url()} returned ${status}`;
    assertMatchesContract(
      response.ok() ? successSchema : errorSchema,
      body,
      context,
    );
    return { status, body, headers: response.headers() };
  }
}

tests/framework/db-helper.ts
import { Pool } from "pg";

// Read-only questions tests ask the database directly. One instance per
// Playwright worker (see fixtures.ts), closed when the worker finishes.
export class DbHelper {
  private readonly pool = new Pool({
    connectionString:
      process.env.DATABASE_URL ??
      "postgres://ledgerline:ledgerline@localhost:5432/ledgerline",
    max: 2,
  });

  /** Transfers that don't have exactly two ledger entries summing to zero. */
  async unbalancedTransfers() {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(`
      SELECT t.id, COUNT(e.id) AS entries, COALESCE(SUM(e.amount_cents), 0) AS total
      FROM transfers t
      LEFT JOIN ledger_entries e ON e.transfer_id = t.id
      GROUP BY t.id
      HAVING COUNT(e.id) <> 2 OR COALESCE(SUM(e.amount_cents), 0) <> 0
    `);
    return rows;
  }

  /** Sum of every ledger entry ever written. Should always be "0". */
  async ledgerTotal(): Promise<string> {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(
      "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents), 0)::text AS total FROM ledger_entries",
    );
    return rows[0].total;
  }

  /** Customer accounts whose balance has gone below zero. */
  async negativeCustomerBalances() {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(`
      SELECT a.id, SUM(e.amount_cents) AS balance
      FROM accounts a
      JOIN ledger_entries e ON e.account_id = a.id
      WHERE a.type = 'customer'
      GROUP BY a.id
      HAVING SUM(e.amount_cents) < 0
    `);
    return rows;
  }

  async countAccountsNamed(name: string): Promise<number> {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(
      "SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS count FROM accounts WHERE name = $1",
      [name],
    );
    return rows[0].count;
  }

  async countTransfersFrom(accountId: string): Promise<number> {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(
      "SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS count FROM transfers WHERE from_account_id = $1",
      [accountId],
    );
    return rows[0].count;
  }

  /** The kinds of money movement that followed a payment, oldest first. */
  async followUps(transferId: string): Promise<string[]> {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(
      "SELECT kind FROM transfers WHERE reverses_transfer_id = $1 OR settles_transfer_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at",
      [transferId],
    );
    return rows.map((row) => row.kind);
  }

  async close() {
    await this.pool.end();
  }
}

Create tests/framework/partner-webhooks.ts:

tests/framework/partner-webhooks.ts
import { createHmac, randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import type { LedgerlineClient } from "./ledgerline-client";
import { WEBHOOK_SECRET } from "./test-data";

export interface SendOptions {
  secret?: string;
  timestamp?: number;
  // Changes the body after it's signed, the way an attacker would.
  tamper?: (body: string) => string;
}

// Plays the partner bank's side of webhooks: builds events and signs them
// exactly the way the real partner would.
export class PartnerWebhooks {
  constructor(private readonly api: LedgerlineClient) {}

  settled(transferId: string) {
    return { id: `evt_${randomUUID()}`, type: "transfer.settled", transferId };
  }

  returned(transferId: string, returnCode = "R01") {
    return {
      id: `evt_${randomUUID()}`,
      type: "transfer.returned",
      transferId,
      returnCode,
    };
  }

  async send(event: Record<string, unknown>, options: SendOptions = {}) {
    const body = JSON.stringify(event);
    const timestamp = String(
      options.timestamp ?? Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
    );
    const signature = createHmac("sha256", options.secret ?? WEBHOOK_SECRET)
      .update(`${timestamp}.${body}`)
      .digest("hex");
    return this.api.postPartnerEvent(
      options.tamper ? options.tamper(body) : body,
      {
        "x-partner-timestamp": timestamp,
        "x-partner-signature": `sha256=${signature}`,
      },
    );
  }
}

Create tests/api/idempotency.spec.ts:

tests/api/idempotency.spec.ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { expectApiError } from "../framework/assertions";
import { expect, test } from "../framework/fixtures";

test.describe("idempotency keys", () => {
  test("the same key twice makes one transfer and replays the response", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    db,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();
    const body = {
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
    };
    const key = randomUUID();

    const first = await api.createTransfer(body, { idempotencyKey: key });
    const retry = await api.createTransfer(body, { idempotencyKey: key });

    expect(first.status).toBe(201);
    expect(retry.status).toBe(201);
    expect(retry.body).toEqual(first.body);
    expect(retry.headers["idempotent-replayed"]).toBe("true");
    expect(await db.countTransfersFrom(from.id)).toBe(1);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(7_500);
  });

  test("without a key, a retry moves the money twice", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    db,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();
    const body = {
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
    };

    await api.createTransfer(body);
    await api.createTransfer(body);

    // This is the problem idempotency keys solve.
    expect(await db.countTransfersFrom(from.id)).toBe(2);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(5_000);
  });

  test("the same key with a different body is refused", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    db,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();
    const key = randomUUID();

    await api.createTransfer(
      { fromAccountId: from.id, toAccountId: to.id, amountCents: 2_500 },
      { idempotencyKey: key },
    );
    const reused = await api.createTransfer(
      { fromAccountId: from.id, toAccountId: to.id, amountCents: 3_000 },
      { idempotencyKey: key },
    );

    expectApiError(reused, 422, "idempotency_key_reused");
    expect(await db.countTransfersFrom(from.id)).toBe(1);
  });

  test("ten parallel requests with one key make exactly one transfer", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    db,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();
    const body = {
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
    };
    const key = randomUUID();

    const results = await Promise.all(
      Array.from({ length: 10 }, () =>
        api.createTransfer(body, { idempotencyKey: key }),
      ),
    );

    // One wins. The rest are either still waiting on it (409) or get its
    // response replayed (201).
    for (const result of results) expect([201, 409]).toContain(result.status);
    expect(results.some((result) => result.status === 201)).toBe(true);
    expect(await db.countTransfersFrom(from.id)).toBe(1);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(7_500);
  });

  test("a refusal is replayed as a refusal, even after the balance changes", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();
    const body = {
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      toAccountId: to.id,
      amountCents: 1_001,
    };
    const key = randomUUID();

    expectApiError(
      await api.createTransfer(body, { idempotencyKey: key }),
      422,
      "insufficient_funds",
    );
    await api.deposit(from.id, 5_000);
    const retry = await api.createTransfer(body, { idempotencyKey: key });

    // Same key, same answer. A new attempt needs a new key.
    expectApiError(retry, 422, "insufficient_funds");
    expect(retry.headers["idempotent-replayed"]).toBe("true");
    const fresh = await api.createTransfer(body, {
      idempotencyKey: randomUUID(),
    });
    expect(fresh.status).toBe(201);
  });

  test("payments to other banks honour keys too", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    db,
  }) => {
    await partner.accepts();
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
    const body = {
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    };
    const key = randomUUID();

    const first = await api.createExternalTransfer(body, {
      idempotencyKey: key,
    });
    const retry = await api.createExternalTransfer(body, {
      idempotencyKey: key,
    });

    expect(first.status).toBe(202);
    expect(retry.status).toBe(202);
    expect(retry.body.id).toBe(first.body.id);
    expect(await db.countTransfersFrom(from.id)).toBe(1);
  });

  test("a key longer than 255 characters is refused", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();
    const to = await newAccount().create();

    const result = await api.createTransfer(
      { fromAccountId: from.id, toAccountId: to.id, amountCents: 100 },
      { idempotencyKey: "k".repeat(256) },
    );

    expectApiError(result, 400, "validation_error");
  });
});

    partner,
    webhooks,
    db,
  }) => {
    const { from, transfer } = await submittedPayment(api, newAccount, partner);

    const { status, body } = await webhooks.send(webhooks.settled(transfer.id));

    expect(status).toBe(200);
    expect(body.result).toBe("processed");
    expect((await api.getTransfer(transfer.id)).body.status).toBe("settled");
    expect(await db.followUps(transfer.id)).toEqual(["settlement"]);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(7_500);
  });

  test("a return after settlement sends the money back", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    webhooks,
    db,
  }) => {
    const { from, transfer } = await submittedPayment(api, newAccount, partner);
    await webhooks.send(webhooks.settled(transfer.id));

    await webhooks.send(webhooks.returned(transfer.id, "R03"));

    const { body } = await api.getTransfer(transfer.id);
    expect(body.status).toBe("returned");
    expect(body.statusReason).toBe("R03");
    expect(await db.followUps(transfer.id)).toEqual(["settlement", "reversal"]);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(10_000);
  });

  test("a return before settlement also sends the money back", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    webhooks,
  }) => {
    const { from, transfer } = await submittedPayment(api, newAccount, partner);

    await webhooks.send(webhooks.returned(transfer.id, "R01"));

    expect((await api.getTransfer(transfer.id)).body.status).toBe("returned");
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(10_000);
  });

  test("a resent event is only applied once", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    webhooks,
    db,
  }) => {
    const { from, transfer } = await submittedPayment(api, newAccount, partner);
    const event = webhooks.returned(transfer.id, "R01");

    const first = await webhooks.send(event);
    const resent = await webhooks.send(event);

    expect(first.body.result).toBe("processed");
    expect(resent.body.result).toBe("duplicate");
    expect(await db.followUps(transfer.id)).toEqual(["reversal"]);
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(10_000);
  });

  test("an event that arrives out of order is ignored", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    webhooks,
  }) => {
    const { transfer } = await submittedPayment(api, newAccount, partner);
    await webhooks.send(webhooks.returned(transfer.id, "R01"));

    const late = await webhooks.send(webhooks.settled(transfer.id));

    expect(late.body.result).toBe("ignored");
    expect((await api.getTransfer(transfer.id)).body.status).toBe("returned");
  });

  test("an event for a payment that doesn't exist is ignored", async ({
    webhooks,
  }) => {
    const { status, body } = await webhooks.send(
      webhooks.settled(randomUUID()),
    );

    expect(status).toBe(200);
    expect(body.result).toBe("ignored");
  });

  test("the wrong secret is refused and changes nothing", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    webhooks,
  }) => {
    const { transfer } = await submittedPayment(api, newAccount, partner);

    const forged = await webhooks.send(webhooks.returned(transfer.id), {
      secret: "not-the-secret",
    });

    expectApiError(forged, 401, "invalid_signature");
    expect((await api.getTransfer(transfer.id)).body.status).toBe("submitted");
  });

  test("a body changed after signing is refused", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    webhooks,
  }) => {
    const { transfer } = await submittedPayment(api, newAccount, partner);

    const tampered = await webhooks.send(
      webhooks.returned(transfer.id, "R01"),
      {
        tamper: (body) => body.replace("R01", "R02"),
      },
    );

    expectApiError(tampered, 401, "invalid_signature");
  });

  test("an old event is refused, so it can't be replayed later", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    webhooks,
  }) => {
    const { transfer } = await submittedPayment(api, newAccount, partner);
    const tenMinutesAgo = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - 600;

    const stale = await webhooks.send(webhooks.settled(transfer.id), {
      timestamp: tenMinutesAgo,
    });

    expectApiError(stale, 401, "invalid_signature");
  });

  test("a return without a return code is rejected as invalid", async ({
    webhooks,
  }) => {
    const result = await webhooks.send({
      id: `evt_${randomUUID()}`,
      type: "transfer.returned",
      transferId: randomUUID(),
    });

    expectApiError(result, 400, "validation_error");
  });
});

67 passed: 50 from before, 7 idempotency tests and 10 webhook tests.

What the tests prove

  • The control test shows the problem first: without a key, a retry really does move the money twice. A test that demonstrates the bug makes the fix convincing.
  • Ten parallel requests with one key make exactly one transfer. The others get 409 or a replayed 201, and the test accepts either, because which one each request gets depends on timing.
  • A refusal is replayed as a refusal, even after the account is topped up. Same key, same answer; a new attempt needs a new key. That's the rule Stripe uses, and interviewers like it because it surprises people.
  • Every webhook failure mode is covered: the wrong secret, a body changed after signing, an event ten minutes old, an event resent, an event out of order, an event for a payment that doesn't exist, and an invalid event.
  • db.followUps checks the money movements, not just the status: one settlement, then one reversal, and never two.
  • postPartnerEvent sends a Buffer. You met this in Step 13: a plain string would be re-encoded by Playwright, and the signature would never match.

Try this

Remove the protection and watch the race. In src/idempotency.ts, delete the line ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(pk)", and run: 

npx playwright test -g "ten parallel requests"

It fails, with 422s among the statuses. Without the condition, every request claimed the key and tried to move $25, so the account ran dry after four transfers and the rest were refused for insufficient funds. Put the line back.

README.md
# Ledgerline

A small business-banking backend, and the automated test framework around it.
Built to practise how fintech teams test money movement: ledgers, contracts,
concurrency and CI.

## Run it

You need Docker Desktop and Node 24.

```bash
npm install
npm run db:up        # start Postgres, MiniStack and WireMock in Docker
npm run db:migrate   # create the tables
npm run aws:setup    # create the queues in MiniStack
npm test             # unit tests, then API tests (the API starts automatically)
```

Run the API on its own with `npm run dev`, then try `curl localhost:3000/health`.

## How the tests are organised

```
tests/
  unit/        Vitest. Pure functions, no network or database.
  api/         Playwright specs. Each file covers one feature.
  framework/   The plumbing specs are built on:
    fixtures.ts           api, newAccount, apiWithKey, db
    ledgerline-client.ts  one method per endpoint
    contract.ts           checks every response against openapi.yaml
    account-builder.ts    newAccount().withBalance(5000).create()
    db-helper.ts          ledger integrity queries
    queue-helper.ts       reads and writes queues in MiniStack
    fake-partner.ts       programs WireMock to act as the partner bank
    partner-webhooks.ts   sends signed webhooks, as the partner bank would
    assertions.ts         expectApiError(result, 422, "insufficient_funds")
bruno/         Bruno collection for exploring the API by hand
infra/wiremock/  the fake partner bank's default stubs
src/processor/   the Lambda that sends payments to the partner bank
openapi.yaml   The API contract
```

## Add a test

1. Pick the spec file for the feature, or create `tests/api/<feature>.spec.ts`.
2. Import `{ test, expect }` from `../framework/fixtures`.
3. Set up data with `newAccount()`, act with `api`, assert on the result.

```ts
test("rejects a transfer over the balance", async ({ api, newAccount }) => {
  const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();
  const to = await newAccount().create();

  const result = await api.createTransfer({
    fromAccountId: from.id,
    toAccountId: to.id,
    amountCents: 1_001,
  });

  expectApiError(result, 422, "insufficient_funds");
});
```

Every test creates its own accounts, so tests run in parallel and in any order.
