Phase 3 starts with Week 7: risk rules, like daily limits, using Redis.

Week 7: Risk rules and Redis

Phase 3 starts with the rules that decide whether money may leave at all. Payments over a limit won't be refused: they'll be held for a person to review, the way real risk teams work. You'll write the rules as pure logic tested with a decision table, keep a fast daily counter in Redis, and prove the whole thing holds up under parallel payments and a Redis outage. Chapter 19 of the field guide covers the ideas.

Step 34: The rules as pure logic

About an hour.

What, why and how: Risk rules and decision tables

What it is. Risk rules decide whether a payment goes ahead on its own or waits for a person to look at it. A decision table lists combinations of inputs, like the amount, what's already been sent today and the account's age, next to the outcome each combination must get.

Why we use it. Rules interact in ways that are easy to get wrong. A $10,000.01 payment breaks two limits at once, so which reason should it get? Writing every combination down forces those questions into the open, and each row becomes a test. Relay's QA role sits with its Risk Engineering team.

How we use it. The rules live in src/domain/risk.ts as a pure function: numbers in, a decision out, with no database, Redis or clock involved. A unit test runs every row of the decision table in milliseconds. API tests then check the wiring around it: the counter, the statuses and the review endpoint.

How it works inside. The rules are checked in a fixed order, and the first one that fails decides the reason. Because assessPayment takes plain numbers, never a database or a clock, every rule can be tested exhaustively and instantly. The slower parts, reading the counter and the account's age, are tested separately, in the API tests.

Ledgerline's rules, for payments to other banks:

Rule Limit Otherwise
One payment up to $10,000.00 held: over_payment_limit
Per day, accounts under 30 days old up to $1,000.00 held: over_daily_limit
Per day, older accounts up to $5,000.00 held: over_daily_limit

Create src/domain/risk.ts:

src/domain/risk.ts
// Limits on money leaving Ledgerline, in cents. A payment over a limit isn't
// refused outright: it's held for a person to review.
export const RISK_LIMITS = {
  perPaymentCents: 1_000_000, // $10,000.00 in one payment
  dailyCents: 500_000, // $5,000.00 a day
  newAccountDailyCents: 100_000, // $1,000.00 a day, for new accounts
  newAccountDays: 30, // how long an account counts as new
};

export type RiskDecision =
  | { decision: "allow" }
  | { decision: "review"; reason: "over_payment_limit" | "over_daily_limit" };

// Pure logic: no Redis, no database, no clock. That's what makes every rule
// easy to test exhaustively with unit tests.
export function assessPayment(input: {
  amountCents: number;
  sentTodayCents: number;
  accountAgeDays: number;
}): RiskDecision {
  if (input.amountCents > RISK_LIMITS.perPaymentCents) {
    return { decision: "review", reason: "over_payment_limit" };
  }
  const dailyLimit =
    input.accountAgeDays < RISK_LIMITS.newAccountDays
      ? RISK_LIMITS.newAccountDailyCents
      : RISK_LIMITS.dailyCents;
  if (input.sentTodayCents + input.amountCents > dailyLimit) {
    return { decision: "review", reason: "over_daily_limit" };
  }
  return { decision: "allow" };
}

Create tests/unit/risk.test.ts:

tests/unit/risk.test.ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { assessPayment } from "../../src/domain/risk";

// A decision table: every row is one combination of inputs, with the outcome
// the rules say it must get. Each limit is tested on and just past its edge.
describe("assessPayment", () => {
  it.each([
    // amount     sent today  age   expected
    [100_000, 0, 0, "allow"], // a new account's whole daily limit
    [100_001, 0, 0, "over_daily_limit"], // one cent over it
    [50_000, 50_000, 29, "allow"], // exactly $1,000 in total, day 29
    [50_000, 50_001, 29, "over_daily_limit"],
    [100_001, 0, 30, "allow"], // day 30: the established limit applies
    [500_000, 0, 365, "allow"], // an established account's daily limit
    [500_001, 0, 365, "over_daily_limit"],
    [250_000, 250_000, 365, "allow"],
    [250_000, 250_001, 365, "over_daily_limit"],
    [1_000_000, 0, 365, "over_daily_limit"], // $10,000 is also over $5,000
    [1_000_001, 0, 365, "over_payment_limit"], // the payment limit wins
  ])(
    "%i cents with %i sent today, account %i days old: %s",
    (amountCents, sentTodayCents, accountAgeDays, expected) => {
      const result = assessPayment({
        amountCents,
        sentTodayCents,
        accountAgeDays,
      });
      const outcome = result.decision === "allow" ? "allow" : result.reason;
      expect(outcome).toBe(expected);
    },
  );
});

33 passed: the 22 money tests and 11 rows of the decision table.

What the code does

  • assessPayment knows nothing about Redis, the database, or the clock. It takes three numbers and returns a decision. That's what lets eleven cases run in milliseconds, and it's the pattern to use for any business rule: keep the decision pure and test it exhaustively, then test the wiring separately.
  • The payment limit is checked first, so a $10,000.01 payment is reported as over_payment_limit even though it's also over the daily limit. The last two rows of the table pin that down. Which reason wins is exactly the kind of thing a decision table forces someone to decide.
  • Every limit is tested on its edge and one cent past it, and the account age on day 29 and day 30.

Step 35: Redis and holding payments

About two hours.

What, why and how: Redis

What it is. Redis is an in-memory data store: it keeps keys and values, like counters, in memory, so reading and writing them is extremely fast. Keys can be set to delete themselves after a while.

Why we use it. The daily limit needs a counter per account that's updated on every payment, read instantly, shared by every copy of the API, and reset each day. Redis's INCRBY adds to a counter and returns the new total in one atomic step, and EXPIRE cleans old counters up. Redis is in Relay's stack.

How we use it. Redis runs as a container, and the API talks to it through the ioredis library. Each account gets one key per day, like velocity:<account id>:2026-10-12. To look inside while you work, run docker compose exec redis redis-cli, then KEYS velocity:* to list the counters and GET followed by a key to read one. (KEYS is fine locally, but too slow to use on a busy production Redis.) Chapter 19 of the field guide has a daily-limit demo.

How it works inside. Redis keeps all its data in memory and runs commands on a single thread, one command at a time. That's why INCRBY is atomic without any locking: no other command can run between reading the old total and writing the new one. Keys with an expiry are removed in two ways: when someone tries to read an expired key, and by a background task that regularly samples keys and deletes the expired ones. Redis can also save snapshots to disk, but in this project, losing the counters would only reset a day's limits early. Try the daily limit:

The API now runs the risk check before it moves any money. Allowed payments carry on as before. Held payments still reserve the money in clearing, but they're saved as in_review and never published, so they can't reach the bank. A new endpoint, POST /transfers/:id/review, lets a person approve one, which publishes it, or decline it, which sends the money back.

Create src/risk-check.ts:

src/risk-check.ts
import Redis from "ioredis";
import { assessPayment, type RiskDecision } from "./domain/risk";

export const redis = new Redis(
  process.env.REDIS_URL ?? "redis://localhost:6379",
  {
    // Fail fast instead of queueing commands while Redis is unreachable.
    enableOfflineQueue: false,
    maxRetriesPerRequest: 1,
    connectTimeout: 1000,
  },
);
// Like the pg pool in Step 4: without a listener, a lost connection would
// crash the whole API. Failures are handled per request below instead.
redis.on("error", () => undefined);

export type RiskOutcome =
  RiskDecision | { decision: "review"; reason: "risk_check_unavailable" };

// One counter per account per day, in UTC. Real banks count in their own
// business day and time zone; UTC keeps this project simple.
function velocityKey(accountId: string) {
  return `velocity:${accountId}:${new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)}`;
}

// Adds the payment to today's total first, in one atomic step, and only then
// decides. Two payments at the same moment can't both see the old total.
export async function checkPayment(
  accountId: string,
  amountCents: number,
  accountAgeDays: number,
): Promise<RiskOutcome> {
  const key = velocityKey(accountId);
  try {
    const total = await redis.incrby(key, amountCents);
    await redis.expire(key, 2 * 24 * 60 * 60);
    const decision = assessPayment({
      amountCents,
      sentTodayCents: total - amountCents,
      accountAgeDays,
    });
    // A held payment isn't sent today, so it doesn't count towards the total.
    if (decision.decision === "review") await redis.decrby(key, amountCents);
    return decision;
  } catch {
    // Fail closed: if the check can't run, a person decides instead.
    return { decision: "review", reason: "risk_check_unavailable" };
  }
}

// Takes a payment back off today's total, when it didn't go ahead after all.
export async function releasePayment(accountId: string, amountCents: number) {
  await redis
    .decrby(velocityKey(accountId), amountCents)
    .catch(() => undefined);
}

src/ledger.ts
import type { PoolClient } from "pg";
import { pool } from "./db";
import { formatCents } from "./domain/money";
import { AppError, notFound } from "./errors";

export const FUNDING_ACCOUNT_ID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001";
export const CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002";
export const SETTLED_ACCOUNT_ID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003";

export type TransferKind =
  "deposit" | "internal" | "external" | "reversal" | "settlement";
export type TransferStatus =
  | "completed"
  | "pending"
  | "submitted"
  | "rejected"
  | "failed"
  | "settled"
  | "returned"
  | "in_review"
  | "declined";

// Where a payment to another bank is going.
export interface Counterparty {
  name: string;
  routingNumber: string;
  accountNumber: string;
}

// What a transfers row looks like coming out of Postgres.
interface TransferRow {
  id: string;
  kind: TransferKind;
  from_account_id: string;
  to_account_id: string;
  amount_cents: string; // bigint arrives as a string, see toCents()
  status: TransferStatus;
  counterparty_name: string | null;
  counterparty_routing: string | null;
  counterparty_account: string | null;
  reverses_transfer_id: string | null;
  settles_transfer_id: string | null;
  partner_reference: string | null;
  status_reason: string | null;
  created_at: Date;
}

// What we send back to API clients.
export interface Transfer {
  id: string;
  kind: TransferKind;
  fromAccountId: string;
  toAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  status: TransferStatus;
  createdAt: string;
  // Only the last four digits ever leave the API.
  counterparty?: { name: string; routingNumber: string; accountLast4: string };
  partnerReference?: string;
  statusReason?: string;
  reversesTransferId?: string;
}

// Postgres bigint can hold numbers JavaScript can't represent exactly, so pg
// returns them as strings. Our amounts are far below that limit, so we convert,
// but refuse loudly if a value ever isn't a safe whole number.
export function toCents(value: string | number): number {
  const cents = Number(value);
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(cents)) {
    throw new Error(`Not a safe whole number of cents: ${value}`);
  }
  return cents;
}

export function toTransfer(row: TransferRow): Transfer {
  const transfer: Transfer = {
    id: row.id,
    kind: row.kind,
    fromAccountId: row.from_account_id,
    toAccountId: row.to_account_id,
    amountCents: toCents(row.amount_cents),
    status: row.status,
    createdAt: row.created_at.toISOString(),
  };
  if (row.counterparty_account) {
    transfer.counterparty = {
      name: row.counterparty_name ?? "",
      routingNumber: row.counterparty_routing ?? "",
      accountLast4: row.counterparty_account.slice(-4),
    };
  }
  if (row.partner_reference) transfer.partnerReference = row.partner_reference;
  if (row.status_reason) transfer.statusReason = row.status_reason;
  if (row.reverses_transfer_id) {
    transfer.reversesTransferId = row.reverses_transfer_id;
  }
  return transfer;
}

type Queryable = Pick<PoolClient, "query">;

export async function getBalance(db: Queryable, accountId: string) {
  const { rows } = await db.query<{ balance: string }>(
    "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents), 0) AS balance FROM ledger_entries WHERE account_id = $1",
    [accountId],
  );
  return toCents(rows[0].balance);
}

export async function getTransfer(id: string): Promise<Transfer> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<TransferRow>(
    "SELECT * FROM transfers WHERE id = $1",
    [id],
  );
  if (rows.length === 0) throw notFound("transfer", id);
  return toTransfer(rows[0]);
}

interface MoveMoneyInput {
  kind: TransferKind;
  fromAccountId: string;
  toAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  status?: TransferStatus;
  statusReason?: string;
  counterparty?: Counterparty;
  // Runs inside the transaction, after everything is written but before
  // COMMIT. If it throws, the whole transfer is rolled back.
  beforeCommit?: (transfer: Transfer) => Promise<void>;
}

// The one place money moves. Everything happens inside a database transaction:
// either the transfer and both ledger entries are saved, or nothing is.
export async function moveMoney(input: MoveMoneyInput): Promise<Transfer> {
  if (input.fromAccountId === input.toAccountId) {
    throw new AppError(
      422,
      "same_account",
      "Can't transfer to the same account",
    );
  }

  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query("BEGIN");

    // Lock both account rows until COMMIT, always in the same order (by id).
    // Two transfers touching the same account now take turns instead of both
    // reading the old balance, and opposite transfers can't deadlock.
    const { rows: accounts } = await client.query<{ id: string; type: string }>(
      "SELECT id, type FROM accounts WHERE id = ANY($1::uuid[]) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE",
      [[input.fromAccountId, input.toAccountId]],
    );
    const from = accounts.find((account) => account.id === input.fromAccountId);
    const to = accounts.find((account) => account.id === input.toAccountId);
    if (!from) throw notFound("account", input.fromAccountId);
    if (!to) throw notFound("account", input.toAccountId);

    // Only deposits may draw on a system account.
    if (
      input.kind === "internal" &&
      (from.type !== "customer" || to.type !== "customer")
    ) {
      throw new AppError(
        422,
        "account_not_allowed",
        "Transfers must be between customer accounts",
      );
    }
    if (input.kind === "external" && from.type !== "customer") {
      throw new AppError(
        422,
        "account_not_allowed",
        "Only customer accounts can pay other banks",
      );
    }

    if (from.type === "customer") {
      const balance = await getBalance(client, from.id);
      if (balance < input.amountCents) {
        throw new AppError(
          422,
          "insufficient_funds",
          `Balance is ${formatCents(balance)} but the transfer needs ${formatCents(input.amountCents)}`,
        );
      }
    }

    const { rows } = await client.query<TransferRow>(
      `INSERT INTO transfers (kind, from_account_id, to_account_id, amount_cents, status,
         counterparty_name, counterparty_routing, counterparty_account, status_reason)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9)
       RETURNING *`,
      [
        input.kind,
        input.fromAccountId,
        input.toAccountId,
        input.amountCents,
        input.status ?? "completed",
        input.counterparty?.name ?? null,
        input.counterparty?.routingNumber ?? null,
        input.counterparty?.accountNumber ?? null,
        input.statusReason ?? null,
      ],
    );
    const transfer = toTransfer(rows[0]);

    // Double entry: money leaves one account and arrives in the other.
    await client.query(
      "INSERT INTO ledger_entries (account_id, transfer_id, amount_cents) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)",
      [input.fromAccountId, transfer.id, -input.amountCents],
    );
    await client.query(
      "INSERT INTO ledger_entries (account_id, transfer_id, amount_cents) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)",
      [input.toAccountId, transfer.id, input.amountCents],
    );

    if (input.beforeCommit) await input.beforeCommit(transfer);

    await client.query("COMMIT");
    return transfer;
  } catch (error) {
    await client.query("ROLLBACK");
    throw error;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

export type PartnerOutcome =
  | { status: "submitted"; partnerReference: string }
  | { status: "rejected" | "failed"; reason: string };

/** The transfer's current status, or null if it doesn't exist. */
export async function findTransferStatus(
  id: string,
): Promise<TransferStatus | null> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<{ status: TransferStatus }>(
    "SELECT status FROM transfers WHERE id = $1",
    [id],
  );
  return rows[0]?.status ?? null;
}

// Records what the partner bank said about a pending payment. Safe to call
// twice: only a pending transfer can change, so a duplicate message changes
// nothing. A rejected or failed payment sends the money back with a reversal.
export async function recordPartnerOutcome(
  transferId: string,
  outcome: PartnerOutcome,
): Promise<"updated" | "unchanged"> {
  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query("BEGIN");
    const { rows } = await client.query<TransferRow>(
      "SELECT * FROM transfers WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE",
      [transferId],
    );
    const transfer = rows[0];
    if (!transfer || transfer.status !== "pending") {
      await client.query("ROLLBACK");
      return "unchanged";
    }

    if (outcome.status === "submitted") {
      await client.query(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = 'submitted', partner_reference = $2 WHERE id = $1",
        [transferId, outcome.partnerReference],
      );
    } else {
      await client.query(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = $2, status_reason = $3 WHERE id = $1",
        [transferId, outcome.status, outcome.reason],
      );
      // Money goes back from clearing to the customer: a new transfer.
      await insertMovement(client, {
        kind: "reversal",
        fromAccountId: transfer.to_account_id,
        toAccountId: transfer.from_account_id,
        amountCents: toCents(transfer.amount_cents),
        reversesTransferId: transfer.id,
      });
    }

    await client.query("COMMIT");
    return "updated";
  } catch (error) {
    await client.query("ROLLBACK");
    throw error;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

// Writes a completed transfer and its two ledger entries, inside a
// transaction the caller has already started.
async function insertMovement(
  client: PoolClient,
  movement: {
    kind: "reversal" | "settlement";
    fromAccountId: string;
    toAccountId: string;
    amountCents: number;
    reversesTransferId?: string;
    settlesTransferId?: string;
  },
): Promise<void> {
  const { rows } = await client.query<{ id: string }>(
    `INSERT INTO transfers (kind, from_account_id, to_account_id, amount_cents, status,
       reverses_transfer_id, settles_transfer_id)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, 'completed', $5, $6)
     RETURNING id`,
    [
      movement.kind,
      movement.fromAccountId,
      movement.toAccountId,
      movement.amountCents,
      movement.reversesTransferId ?? null,
      movement.settlesTransferId ?? null,
    ],
  );
  await client.query(
    "INSERT INTO ledger_entries (account_id, transfer_id, amount_cents) VALUES ($1, $2, $3), ($4, $2, $5)",
    [
      movement.fromAccountId,
      rows[0].id,
      -movement.amountCents,
      movement.toAccountId,
      movement.amountCents,
    ],
  );
}

export type PartnerEvent =
  | { id: string; type: "transfer.settled"; transferId: string }
  | {
      id: string;
      type: "transfer.returned";
      transferId: string;
      returnCode: string;
    };

export type EventResult = "processed" | "duplicate" | "ignored";

// Which statuses each event may move a payment out of. Anything else is an
// event arriving out of order, and it's ignored.
const ALLOWED_FROM: Record<PartnerEvent["type"], TransferStatus[]> = {
  "transfer.settled": ["submitted"],
  "transfer.returned": ["submitted", "settled"],
};

// Applies one webhook event from the partner bank, exactly once.
export async function applyPartnerEvent(
  event: PartnerEvent,
): Promise<{ result: EventResult; reason?: string }> {
  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query("BEGIN");

    // Record the event first. A resent event hits the primary key, inserts
    // nothing, and is reported as a duplicate.
    const inserted = await client.query(
      "INSERT INTO webhook_events (id, type, transfer_id) VALUES ($1, $2, $3) ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING",
      [event.id, event.type, event.transferId],
    );
    if (inserted.rowCount === 0) {
      await client.query("ROLLBACK");
      return { result: "duplicate" };
    }

    const { rows } = await client.query<TransferRow>(
      "SELECT * FROM transfers WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE",
      [event.transferId],
    );
    const transfer = rows[0];
    if (!transfer || transfer.kind !== "external") {
      await client.query("COMMIT");
      return { result: "ignored", reason: "no such payment" };
    }
    if (!ALLOWED_FROM[event.type].includes(transfer.status)) {
      await client.query("COMMIT");
      return {
        result: "ignored",
        reason: `${event.type} can't follow ${transfer.status}`,
      };
    }

    const amountCents = toCents(transfer.amount_cents);
    if (event.type === "transfer.settled") {
      await client.query(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = 'settled' WHERE id = $1",
        [transfer.id],
      );
      await insertMovement(client, {
        kind: "settlement",
        fromAccountId: CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID,
        toAccountId: SETTLED_ACCOUNT_ID,
        amountCents,
        settlesTransferId: transfer.id,
      });
    } else {
      await client.query(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = 'returned', status_reason = $2 WHERE id = $1",
        [transfer.id, event.returnCode],
      );
      // The money comes back from wherever it is now.
      await insertMovement(client, {
        kind: "reversal",
        fromAccountId:
          transfer.status === "settled"
            ? SETTLED_ACCOUNT_ID
            : CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID,
        toAccountId: transfer.from_account_id,
        amountCents,
        reversesTransferId: transfer.id,
      });
    }

    await client.query("COMMIT");
    return { result: "processed" };
  } catch (error) {
    await client.query("ROLLBACK");
    throw error;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

/** How many whole days ago the account was opened, or null if it doesn't exist. */
export async function accountAgeDays(
  accountId: string,
): Promise<number | null> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<{ days: number }>(
    "SELECT FLOOR(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - created_at) / 86400)::int AS days FROM accounts WHERE id = $1",
    [accountId],
  );
  return rows[0]?.days ?? null;
}

// A person's decision on a payment held for review. Approving it sends it on
// its way, through the beforeApprove callback, inside the transaction.
// Declining it sends the money back.
export async function reviewPayment(
  transferId: string,
  decision: "approve" | "decline",
  beforeApprove: (
    transfer: Transfer,
    counterparty: Counterparty,
  ) => Promise<void>,
): Promise<Transfer> {
  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query("BEGIN");
    const { rows } = await client.query<TransferRow>(
      "SELECT * FROM transfers WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE",
      [transferId],
    );
    const held = rows[0];
    if (!held) throw notFound("transfer", transferId);
    if (held.status !== "in_review") {
      throw new AppError(
        409,
        "not_in_review",
        `Only held payments can be reviewed; this one is ${held.status}`,
      );
    }

    let updated: TransferRow;
    if (decision === "approve") {
      ({
        rows: [updated],
      } = await client.query<TransferRow>(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = 'pending', status_reason = NULL WHERE id = $1 RETURNING *",
        [transferId],
      ));
      await beforeApprove(toTransfer(updated), {
        name: held.counterparty_name ?? "",
        routingNumber: held.counterparty_routing ?? "",
        accountNumber: held.counterparty_account ?? "",
      });
    } else {
      ({
        rows: [updated],
      } = await client.query<TransferRow>(
        "UPDATE transfers SET status = 'declined', status_reason = 'declined_by_reviewer' WHERE id = $1 RETURNING *",
        [transferId],
      ));
      await insertMovement(client, {
        kind: "reversal",
        fromAccountId: held.to_account_id,
        toAccountId: held.from_account_id,
        amountCents: toCents(held.amount_cents),
        reversesTransferId: held.id,
      });
    }

    await client.query("COMMIT");
    return toTransfer(updated);
  } catch (error) {
    await client.query("ROLLBACK");
    throw error;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

Replace src/routes/external-transfers.ts, which runs the check and adds the review route:

src/routes/external-transfers.ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import type { FastifyInstance, FastifyRequest } from "fastify";
import { AppError } from "../errors";
import { idempotent } from "../idempotency";
import {
  accountAgeDays,
  CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID,
  moveMoney,
  reviewPayment,
  type Counterparty,
  type Transfer,
} from "../ledger";
import { publishTransferRequested } from "../queue";
import { checkPayment, releasePayment } from "../risk-check";
import { amountCents, idParams } from "./schemas";

interface ExternalTransferBody {
  fromAccountId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  counterparty: Counterparty;
}

export async function externalTransferRoutes(app: FastifyInstance) {
  app.post<{ Body: ExternalTransferBody }>(
    "/transfers/external",
    {
      schema: {
        body: {
          type: "object",
          required: ["fromAccountId", "amountCents", "counterparty"],
          additionalProperties: false,
          properties: {
            fromAccountId: { type: "string", format: "uuid" },
            amountCents,
            counterparty: {
              type: "object",
              required: ["name", "routingNumber", "accountNumber"],
              additionalProperties: false,
              properties: {
                name: { type: "string", minLength: 1, maxLength: 100 },
                routingNumber: { type: "string", pattern: "^[0-9]{9}$" },
                accountNumber: { type: "string", pattern: "^[0-9]{4,17}$" },
              },
            },
          },
        },
      },
    },
    async (request, reply) =>
      idempotent(request, reply, async () => {
        // One id that follows this payment through every log and message.
        const correlationId = randomUUID();
        const { fromAccountId, counterparty } = request.body;

        // Risk first. A held payment still reserves the money, but isn't
        // published, so it can't reach the bank until a person approves it.
        const amount = request.body.amountCents;
        const risk = await checkPayment(
          fromAccountId,
          amount,
          (await accountAgeDays(fromAccountId)) ?? 0,
        );
        const held = risk.decision === "review";

        let transfer;
        try {
          transfer = await moveMoney({
            kind: "external",
            fromAccountId,
            toAccountId: CLEARING_ACCOUNT_ID,
            amountCents: amount,
            status: held ? "in_review" : "pending",
            statusReason: held ? risk.reason : undefined,
            counterparty,
            // Publish before COMMIT. If the queue is down, the transfer rolls
            // back, so there's never a pending payment nobody will process.
            beforeCommit: held
              ? undefined
              : (saved) => publish(saved, counterparty, correlationId, request),
          });
        } catch (error) {
          // It didn't go ahead, so it mustn't count towards today's limit.
          if (!held) await releasePayment(fromAccountId, amount);
          throw error;
        }

        request.log.info(
          { transferId: transfer.id, correlationId },
          "external transfer accepted",
        );
        reply.header("x-correlation-id", correlationId);
        return { statusCode: 202, body: transfer };
      }),
  );
}

// Puts the payment on the queue for the processor. Used when a payment is
// accepted, and again when a reviewer approves a held one.
async function publish(
  transfer: Transfer,
  counterparty: Counterparty,
  correlationId: string,
  request: FastifyRequest,
) {
  try {
    await publishTransferRequested({
      version: 1,
      type: "transfer.requested",
      transferId: transfer.id,
      correlationId,
      amountCents: transfer.amountCents,
      counterparty,
    });
  } catch (error) {
    request.log.error(
      { err: error, correlationId },
      "could not publish the transfer message",
    );
    throw new AppError(
      503,
      "queue_unavailable",
      "Payments to other banks are unavailable right now. Nothing was sent.",
    );
  }
}

export async function reviewRoutes(app: FastifyInstance) {
  app.post<{
    Params: { id: string };
    Body: { decision: "approve" | "decline" };
  }>(
    "/transfers/:id/review",
    {
      schema: {
        params: idParams,
        body: {
          type: "object",
          required: ["decision"],
          additionalProperties: false,
          properties: { decision: { enum: ["approve", "decline"] } },
        },
      },
    },
    async (request) =>
      reviewPayment(
        request.params.id,
        request.body.decision,
        (transfer, counterparty) =>
          publish(transfer, counterparty, randomUUID(), request),
      ),
  );
}

Replace src/app.ts to register the review route:

src/app.ts
import Fastify, { type FastifyError } from "fastify";
import { pool } from "./db";
import { AppError } from "./errors";
import { accountRoutes } from "./routes/accounts";
import {
  externalTransferRoutes,
  reviewRoutes,
} from "./routes/external-transfers";
import { transferRoutes } from "./routes/transfers";
import { webhookRoutes } from "./routes/webhooks";

const API_KEY = process.env.API_KEY ?? "local-dev-key";

export function buildApp() {
  const app = Fastify({
    logger: true,
    ajv: {
      customOptions: {
        // Fastify's defaults quietly turn "2500" into 2500 and drop unknown
        // fields. For money we want strict: wrong types and extra fields fail.
        coerceTypes: false,
        removeAdditional: false,
      },
    },
  });

  // Every route needs the right x-api-key header, except the health check and
  // the partner's webhooks, which prove who sent them with a signature instead.
  app.addHook("onRequest", async (request, reply) => {
    const url = request.routeOptions.url;
    if (url === "/health" || url === "/webhooks/partner") return;
    if (request.headers["x-api-key"] !== API_KEY) {
      return reply
        .code(401)
        .send({ error: "unauthorized", message: "Missing or invalid API key" });
    }
  });

  app.get("/health", async (request, reply) => {
    try {
      await pool.query("SELECT 1");
      return { status: "ok", database: "up" };
    } catch (error) {
      request.log.error({ err: error }, "database health check failed");
      return reply.code(503).send({ status: "degraded", database: "down" });
    }
  });

  app.register(accountRoutes);
  app.register(transferRoutes);
  app.register(externalTransferRoutes);
  app.register(webhookRoutes);
  app.register(reviewRoutes);

  // Every error leaves the API in the same shape: { error, message }.
  app.setErrorHandler<FastifyError>((error, request, reply) => {
    if (error instanceof AppError) {
      return reply
        .code(error.statusCode)
        .send({ error: error.code, message: error.message });
    }
    if (error.validation) {
      return reply
        .code(400)
        .send({ error: "validation_error", message: error.message });
    }
    if (error.statusCode && error.statusCode < 500) {
      // Things like malformed JSON, which Fastify rejects before our code runs.
      return reply
        .code(error.statusCode)
        .send({ error: "bad_request", message: error.message });
    }
    request.log.error({ err: error }, "unhandled error");
    return reply
      .code(500)
      .send({ error: "internal_error", message: "Something went wrong" });
  });

  app.setNotFoundHandler((request, reply) => {
    reply.code(404).send({
      error: "route_not_found",
      message: `No route for ${request.method} ${request.url}`,
    });
  });

  return app;
}

      summary: Receive an event from the partner bank
      description: >
        Signed by the partner instead of using an API key. x-partner-signature
        is "sha256=" followed by the HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>",
        using the shared secret, and the timestamp must be under 5 minutes old.
      security: []
      parameters:
        - name: x-partner-timestamp
          in: header
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
        - name: x-partner-signature
          in: header
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/PartnerEvent"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Received. The result says what happened to it.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/WebhookResult"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"

components:
  securitySchemes:
    apiKey:
      type: apiKey
      in: header
      name: x-api-key

  parameters:
    Id:
      name: id
      in: path
      required: true
      schema:
        type: string
        format: uuid
    IdempotencyKey:
      name: Idempotency-Key
      in: header
      required: false
      description: >
        Send the same key again and you get the first response back, instead
        of a second transfer. Keys are kept for 24 hours.
      schema:
        type: string
        minLength: 1
        maxLength: 255

  responses:
    Error:
      description: The request failed. `error` says why in a stable code.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"

  schemas:
    AmountCents:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100000000

    HealthStatus:
      type: object
      required: [status, database]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [ok, degraded]

    Account:
      type: object

        id:

        name:

          type: string

        balanceCents:
          type: integer
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time

    Transfer:
      type: object

      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        id:

        kind:

          enum: [deposit, internal, external, reversal, settlement]
        fromAccountId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        toAccountId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        amountCents:

        status:

            [

              in_review,

            ]
        createdAt:

        counterparty:

    CounterpartyDetails:
      type: object

      properties:
        name:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 100
        routingNumber:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{9}$"

          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4,17}$"

    TransferRequestedMessage:
      description: What the API puts on the transfers queue. Not an HTTP response.

      additionalProperties: false

What the code does

  • checkPayment counts first, then decides. INCRBY adds the amount and returns the new total in one atomic step, so the rule sees the total before this payment (the new total minus the amount). Two payments arriving together each see a different total, and can't both slip under the limit.
  • A held payment is taken back off the total with DECRBY, because it isn't being sent today.
  • A payment that fails after the check, for example for insufficient funds, is also taken off the total, by releasePayment in the route.
  • Fail closed. If Redis can't be reached, checkPayment returns a hold with the reason risk_check_unavailable. enableOfflineQueue: false makes that happen at once, instead of the request hanging while ioredis waits to reconnect.
  • redis.on("error", ...) is the same lesson as the Postgres pool in Step 4: a client with no error listener can crash the whole API when a connection drops.
  • reviewPayment locks the payment, refuses anything that isn't in_review with a 409, and either publishes it (approve) or reverses it (decline), inside one transaction.

Commit with git add -A && git commit -m "Step 35: Redis and review".

In a company

Redis is a managed service, such as Amazon ElastiCache, on the private network, usually with a standby copy that takes over if the main one fails.

Step 36: Test the risk rules

About two hours.

What, why and how: Test data shortcuts

What it is. A test data shortcut sets up a test's starting state directly in the database, instead of through the API.

Why we use it. Some states can't be reached through the API. The rules treat accounts under 30 days old differently, but the API only opens accounts today, and waiting 30 days isn't an option.

How we use it. newAccount().openedDaysAgo(60) opens the account through the API as usual, then db.backdateAccount moves its created_at 60 days into the past. The rule of thumb: use the API for everything it can do, go to the database only for what it can't, and keep those shortcuts in the framework, in one place, rather than scattered through tests.

The unit tests proved the rules. These API tests prove the wiring: that the counter is shared and atomic, that held payments really stay away from the bank, that review works both ways, and that a Redis outage holds payments instead of letting them through. Playwright now starts a fifth server: an API whose Redis doesn't exist.

Replace tests/framework/ledgerline-client.ts:

tests/framework/ledgerline-client.ts
import type { APIRequestContext, APIResponse } from "@playwright/test";
import { assertMatchesContract, type SchemaName } from "./contract";
import type { Account, HealthStatus, Transfer, WebhookResult } from "./types";

export interface ApiResult<T> {
  status: number;
  body: T;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
}

export interface RequestOptions {
  idempotencyKey?: string;
}

function headersFor(options: RequestOptions): Record<string, string> {
  return options.idempotencyKey
    ? { "idempotency-key": options.idempotencyKey }
    : {};
}

// One method per endpoint. Tests talk to this class, never to raw URLs, so
// when an endpoint changes you fix it here once instead of in every test.
export class LedgerlineClient {
  constructor(private readonly request: APIRequestContext) {}

  health() {
    return this.send<HealthStatus>(
      this.request.get("/health"),
      "HealthStatus",
      "HealthStatus",
    );
  }

  createAccount(name: string) {
    return this.send<Account>(
      this.request.post("/accounts", { data: { name } }),
      "Account",
    );
  }

  getAccount(id: string) {
    return this.send<Account>(this.request.get(`/accounts/${id}`), "Account");
  }

  deposit(accountId: string, amountCents: unknown) {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.post(`/accounts/${accountId}/deposits`, {
        data: { amountCents },
      }),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  // Takes a loose object on purpose, so negative tests can send bad input.
  createTransfer(data: Record<string, unknown>, options: RequestOptions = {}) {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.post("/transfers", { data, headers: headersFor(options) }),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  // Pays a business at another bank. Answers 202: accepted, not finished.
  createExternalTransfer(
    data: Record<string, unknown>,
    options: RequestOptions = {},
  ) {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.post("/transfers/external", {
        data,
        headers: headersFor(options),
      }),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  // Sends a webhook body exactly as given. It's a Buffer so Playwright doesn't
  // re-encode it: the signature covers these exact bytes.
  postPartnerEvent(rawBody: string, headers: Record<string, string>) {
    return this.send<WebhookResult>(
      this.request.post("/webhooks/partner", {
        data: Buffer.from(rawBody),
        headers: { "content-type": "application/json", ...headers },
      }),
      "WebhookResult",
    );
  }

  reviewTransfer(id: string, decision: "approve" | "decline") {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.post(`/transfers/${id}/review`, { data: { decision } }),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  getTransfer(id: string) {
    return this.send<Transfer>(
      this.request.get(`/transfers/${id}`),
      "Transfer",
    );
  }

  async balanceOf(accountId: string): Promise<number> {
    const { status, body } = await this.getAccount(accountId);
    if (status !== 200) {
      throw new Error(`Couldn't read balance of ${accountId}: HTTP ${status}`);
    }
    return body.balanceCents;
  }

  // Every response is checked against openapi.yaml before a test sees it:
  // successes against their resource schema, failures against Error.
  private async send<T>(
    pending: Promise<APIResponse>,
    successSchema: SchemaName,
    errorSchema: SchemaName = "Error",
  ): Promise<ApiResult<T>> {
    const response = await pending;
    const status = response.status();
    const body = await response.json();
    const context = `${response.url()} returned ${status}`;
    assertMatchesContract(
      response.ok() ? successSchema : errorSchema,
      body,
      context,
    );
    return { status, body, headers: response.headers() };
  }
}

Replace tests/framework/db-helper.ts:

tests/framework/db-helper.ts
import { Pool } from "pg";

// Read-only questions tests ask the database directly. One instance per
// Playwright worker (see fixtures.ts), closed when the worker finishes.
export class DbHelper {
  private readonly pool = new Pool({
    connectionString:
      process.env.DATABASE_URL ??
      "postgres://ledgerline:ledgerline@localhost:5432/ledgerline",
    max: 2,
  });

  /** Transfers that don't have exactly two ledger entries summing to zero. */
  async unbalancedTransfers() {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(`
      SELECT t.id, COUNT(e.id) AS entries, COALESCE(SUM(e.amount_cents), 0) AS total
      FROM transfers t
      LEFT JOIN ledger_entries e ON e.transfer_id = t.id
      GROUP BY t.id
      HAVING COUNT(e.id) <> 2 OR COALESCE(SUM(e.amount_cents), 0) <> 0
    `);
    return rows;
  }

  /** Sum of every ledger entry ever written. Should always be "0". */
  async ledgerTotal(): Promise<string> {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(
      "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents), 0)::text AS total FROM ledger_entries",
    );
    return rows[0].total;
  }

  /** Customer accounts whose balance has gone below zero. */
  async negativeCustomerBalances() {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(`
      SELECT a.id, SUM(e.amount_cents) AS balance
      FROM accounts a
      JOIN ledger_entries e ON e.account_id = a.id
      WHERE a.type = 'customer'
      GROUP BY a.id
      HAVING SUM(e.amount_cents) < 0
    `);
    return rows;
  }

  async countAccountsNamed(name: string): Promise<number> {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(
      "SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS count FROM accounts WHERE name = $1",
      [name],
    );
    return rows[0].count;
  }

  async countTransfersFrom(accountId: string): Promise<number> {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(
      "SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS count FROM transfers WHERE from_account_id = $1",
      [accountId],
    );
    return rows[0].count;
  }

  /** The kinds of money movement that followed a payment, oldest first. */
  async followUps(transferId: string): Promise<string[]> {
    const { rows } = await this.pool.query(
      "SELECT kind FROM transfers WHERE reverses_transfer_id = $1 OR settles_transfer_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at",
      [transferId],
    );
    return rows.map((row) => row.kind);
  }

  /** Makes an account look as if it was opened some days ago. */
  async backdateAccount(accountId: string, days: number): Promise<void> {
    await this.pool.query(
      "UPDATE accounts SET created_at = now() - make_interval(days => $2) WHERE id = $1",
      [accountId, days],
    );
  }

  async close() {
    await this.pool.end();
  }
}

Replace tests/framework/account-builder.ts:

tests/framework/account-builder.ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import type { DbHelper } from "./db-helper";
import type { LedgerlineClient } from "./ledgerline-client";
import type { Account } from "./types";

// Reads like a sentence in tests:
//   const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
// Defaults (a unique name, zero balance) cover everything you don't mention.
export class AccountBuilder {
  private name = `Test business ${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`;
  private balanceCents = 0;
  private ageDays = 0;

  constructor(
    private readonly api: LedgerlineClient,
    private readonly db?: DbHelper,
  ) {}

  named(name: string): this {
    this.name = name;
    return this;
  }

  withBalance(cents: number): this {
    this.balanceCents = cents;
    return this;
  }

  // The API can't open an account in the past, so this one reaches into the
  // database. A deliberate shortcut, for a state tests can't reach otherwise.
  openedDaysAgo(days: number): this {
    this.ageDays = days;
    return this;
  }

  async create(): Promise<Account> {
    const created = await this.api.createAccount(this.name);
    if (created.status !== 201) {
      throw new Error(
        `Test setup failed creating an account: ${created.status}`,
      );
    }
    if (this.balanceCents > 0) {
      const deposit = await this.api.deposit(
        created.body.id,
        this.balanceCents,
      );
      if (deposit.status !== 201) {
        throw new Error(
          `Test setup failed funding an account: ${deposit.status}`,
        );
      }
    }
    if (this.ageDays > 0) {
      if (!this.db) throw new Error("openedDaysAgo needs the db fixture");
      await this.db.backdateAccount(created.body.id, this.ageDays);
    }
    return (await this.api.getAccount(created.body.id)).body;
  }
}

  INSPECT_API_URL,
  INSPECT_QUEUE,
  TRANSFERS_QUEUE,
} from "./test-data";

interface TestFixtures {
  api: LedgerlineClient;
  newAccount: () => AccountBuilder;
  apiWithKey: (apiKey?: string) => Promise<LedgerlineClient>;
  brokenQueueApi: LedgerlineClient;
  brokenRiskApi: LedgerlineClient;
  inspectApi: LedgerlineClient;
  partner: FakePartner;
  webhooks: PartnerWebhooks;
}

interface WorkerFixtures {
  db: DbHelper;
  inspectQueue: QueueHelper;
  transfersQueue: QueueHelper;
  deadLetterQueue: QueueHelper;
}

// Specs import { test, expect } from here instead of @playwright/test, and
// get these fixtures handed to them, already set up and cleaned up.
export const test = base.extend<TestFixtures, WorkerFixtures>({
  // A client that sends the normal API key (from playwright.config.ts).
  api: async ({ request }, use) => {
    await use(new LedgerlineClient(request));
  },

  // Call newAccount() for a fresh builder: newAccount().withBalance(500).create()
  newAccount: async ({ api, db }, use) => {
    await use(() => new AccountBuilder(api, db));
  },

  // A client with a different API key, or none, for authentication tests.
  apiWithKey: async ({ playwright, baseURL }, use) => {
    const contexts: APIRequestContext[] = [];
    await use(async (apiKey) => {
      const context = await playwright.request.newContext({
        baseURL,
        extraHTTPHeaders: apiKey ? { "x-api-key": apiKey } : {},
      });
      contexts.push(context);
      return new LedgerlineClient(context);
    });
    // Everything after use() runs when the test finishes: clean up.
    for (const context of contexts) await context.dispose();
  },

  // A client for the second API, the one whose queue doesn't exist.
  brokenQueueApi: async ({ playwright }, use) => {
    const context = await playwright.request.newContext({
      baseURL: BROKEN_QUEUE_API_URL,
      extraHTTPHeaders: { "x-api-key": API_KEY },
    });
    await use(new LedgerlineClient(context));
    await context.dispose();
  },

  // A client for the fourth API, the one whose Redis doesn't exist.
  brokenRiskApi: async ({ playwright }, use) => {
    const context = await playwright.request.newContext({
      baseURL: BROKEN_RISK_API_URL,
      extraHTTPHeaders: { "x-api-key": API_KEY },
    });
    await use(new LedgerlineClient(context));
    await context.dispose();
  },

  // A client for the third API, which publishes to the inspect queue.
  inspectApi: async ({ playwright }, use) => {
    const context = await playwright.request.newContext({
      baseURL: INSPECT_API_URL,
      extraHTTPHeaders: { "x-api-key": API_KEY },
    });
    await use(new LedgerlineClient(context));
    await context.dispose();
  },

  // A fake partner bank with its own counterparty, so its stubs only match
  // this test's payments. Its stubs are removed when the test ends.
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
  partner: async ({}, use) => {
    const partner = new FakePartner();
    await use(partner);
    await partner.cleanup();
  },

  // Sends signed webhooks, the way the partner bank does.
  webhooks: async ({ api }, use) => {
    await use(new PartnerWebhooks(api));
  },

  // The queues in MiniStack, one helper each per worker.
  inspectQueue: [
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
    async ({}, use) => {
      await use(new QueueHelper(INSPECT_QUEUE));
    },
    { scope: "worker" },

  transfersQueue: [
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
    async ({}, use) => {
      await use(new QueueHelper(TRANSFERS_QUEUE));
    },

  deadLetterQueue: [

      await use(new QueueHelper(DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE));
    },
    { scope: "worker" },
  ],

  db: [
    // Playwright requires the {} here even though this fixture needs nothing.
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
    async ({}, use) => {
      const db = new DbHelper();
      await use(db);
      await db.close();
    },
    { scope: "worker" },
  ],
});

      // A second API whose queue doesn't exist: fault injection by config.
      command: "npm run start",
      url: "http://localhost:3001/health",
      reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
      timeout: 30_000,
      env: {
        PORT: "3001",
        TRANSFERS_QUEUE_NAME: "ledgerline-queue-that-does-not-exist",
      },
    },
    {

import { expectApiError } from "../framework/assertions";
import { expect, test } from "../framework/fixtures";

test.describe("risk limits on payments to other banks", () => {
  test("a new account can send $1,000 a day, then payments are held", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
  }) => {
    await partner.accepts();
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(200_000).create();
    const pay = (amountCents: number) =>
      api.createExternalTransfer({
        fromAccountId: from.id,
        amountCents,
        counterparty: partner.counterparty,
      });

    expect((await pay(60_000)).body.status).toBe("pending");
    expect((await pay(40_000)).body.status).toBe("pending"); // exactly $1,000
    const oneCentOver = await pay(1);

    expect(oneCentOver.status).toBe(202);
    expect(oneCentOver.body).toMatchObject({
      status: "in_review",
      statusReason: "over_daily_limit",
    });
  });

  test("an established account can send $5,000 a day", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
  }) => {
    await partner.accepts();
    const from = await newAccount()
      .withBalance(1_000_000)
      .openedDaysAgo(60)
      .create();
    const pay = (amountCents: number) =>
      api.createExternalTransfer({
        fromAccountId: from.id,
        amountCents,
        counterparty: partner.counterparty,
      });

    expect((await pay(400_000)).body.status).toBe("pending");
    expect((await pay(100_000)).body.status).toBe("pending"); // exactly $5,000
    expect((await pay(1)).body).toMatchObject({
      status: "in_review",
      statusReason: "over_daily_limit",
    });
  });

  test("a single payment over $10,000 is held", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount()
      .withBalance(2_000_000)
      .openedDaysAgo(365)
      .create();

    const { body } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 1_000_001,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });

    expect(body).toMatchObject({
      status: "in_review",
      statusReason: "over_payment_limit",
    });
  });

  test("a held payment keeps the money aside and never reaches the bank", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    transfersQueue,
  }) => {
    await partner.accepts();
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(200_000).create();

    const { body: held } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 150_000,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });

    expect(held.status).toBe("in_review");
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(50_000);
    await expect
      .poll(() => transfersQueue.isIdle(), { timeout: 15_000 })
      .toBe(true);
    expect(await partner.requests()).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test("five payments at once can't sneak past the daily limit together", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
  }) => {
    await partner.accepts();
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(200_000).create();

    // Five $300 payments against a $1,000 limit, all at the same moment.
    const results = await Promise.all(
      Array.from({ length: 5 }, () =>
        api.createExternalTransfer({
          fromAccountId: from.id,
          amountCents: 30_000,
          counterparty: partner.counterparty,
        }),
      ),
    );

    const statuses = results.map((result) => result.body.status).sort();
    expect(statuses).toEqual([
      "in_review",
      "in_review",
      "pending",
      "pending",
      "pending",
    ]);
  });

  test("an approved payment goes on to the bank", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
  }) => {
    await partner.accepts();
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(200_000).create();
    const { body: held } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 150_000,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });

    const { status, body } = await api.reviewTransfer(held.id, "approve");

    expect(status).toBe(200);
    expect(body.status).toBe("pending");
    await expect
      .poll(async () => (await api.getTransfer(held.id)).body.status)
      .toBe("submitted");
    expect(await partner.requests()).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test("a declined payment sends the money back", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
    db,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(200_000).create();
    const { body: held } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 150_000,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });

    const { body } = await api.reviewTransfer(held.id, "decline");

    expect(body.status).toBe("declined");
    expect(await api.balanceOf(from.id)).toBe(200_000);
    expect(await db.followUps(held.id)).toEqual(["reversal"]);
  });

  test("only held payments can be reviewed", async ({
    api,
    newAccount,
    partner,
  }) => {
    await partner.accepts();
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();
    const { body: normal } = await api.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });

    expectApiError(
      await api.reviewTransfer(normal.id, "approve"),
      409,
      "not_in_review",
    );
  });

  test("when Redis is down, payments are held rather than sent unchecked", async ({
    brokenRiskApi,
    newAccount,
    partner,
  }) => {
    const from = await newAccount().withBalance(10_000).create();

    const { status, body } = await brokenRiskApi.createExternalTransfer({
      fromAccountId: from.id,
      amountCents: 2_500,
      counterparty: partner.counterparty,
    });

    expect(status).toBe(202);
    expect(body).toMatchObject({
      status: "in_review",
      statusReason: "risk_check_unavailable",
    });
  });
});

What the tests prove

  • Both daily limits, on their edges: exactly $1,000 goes through for a new account and one more cent is held; exactly $5,000 goes through for an established one.
  • Five parallel $300 payments against a $1,000 limit: exactly three go through and two are held. That's the atomic counter doing its job, the same kind of race you saw with the row lock in Week 2.
  • A held payment keeps the money aside and never reaches the bank. The test waits until the queue is idle, then checks WireMock received nothing.
  • Approve and decline both work, and anything not held can't be reviewed.
  • A Redis outage holds the payment instead of letting it through unchecked.

README.md
# Ledgerline

A small business-banking backend, and the automated test framework around it.
Built to practise how fintech teams test money movement: ledgers, contracts,
concurrency and CI.

## Run it

You need Docker Desktop and Node 24.

```bash
npm install
npm run db:up        # start Postgres, MiniStack, WireMock and Redis in Docker
npm run db:migrate   # create the tables
npm run aws:setup    # create the queues in MiniStack
npm test             # unit tests, then API tests (the API starts automatically)
```

Run the API on its own with `npm run dev`, then try `curl localhost:3000/health`.

## How the tests are organised

```
tests/
  unit/        Vitest. Pure functions, no network or database.
  api/         Playwright specs. Each file covers one feature.
  framework/   The plumbing specs are built on:
    fixtures.ts           api, newAccount, apiWithKey, db
    ledgerline-client.ts  one method per endpoint
    contract.ts           checks every response against openapi.yaml
    account-builder.ts    newAccount().withBalance(5000).create()
    db-helper.ts          ledger integrity queries
    queue-helper.ts       reads and writes queues in MiniStack
    fake-partner.ts       programs WireMock to act as the partner bank
    partner-webhooks.ts   sends signed webhooks, as the partner bank would
    assertions.ts         expectApiError(result, 422, "insufficient_funds")
bruno/         Bruno collection for exploring the API by hand
infra/wiremock/  the fake partner bank's default stubs
src/processor/   the Lambda that sends payments to the partner bank
openapi.yaml   The API contract
```

## Add a test

1. Pick the spec file for the feature, or create `tests/api/<feature>.spec.ts`.
2. Import `{ test, expect }` from `../framework/fixtures`.
3. Set up data with `newAccount()`, act with `api`, assert on the result.

```ts
test("rejects a transfer over the balance", async ({ api, newAccount }) => {
  const from = await newAccount().withBalance(1_000).create();
  const to = await newAccount().create();

  const result = await api.createTransfer({
    fromAccountId: from.id,
    toAccountId: to.id,
    amountCents: 1_001,
  });

  expectApiError(result, 422, "insufficient_funds");
});
```

Every test creates its own accounts, so tests run in parallel and in any order.

Week 8 is reconciliation: matching the ledger against the bank's settlement files.

Week 8: Reconciliation

The ledger balances, the tests pass, and it can still disagree with the bank. This week you'll check it against reality: the bank drops a settlement file into S3 every day, and Ledgerline compares it line by line with what it thinks happened. This is where your ETL background pays off. Chapter 20 of the field guide covers the idea.

Step 38: Reconciliation as pure logic

About an hour.

What, why and how: Reconciliation

What it is. Reconciliation compares your records with someone else's, line by line, and flags every difference. Each difference is called a break. Ledgerline looks for four kinds: a payment missing from the bank's file, one in the file that the ledger doesn't know, one with a different amount, and one the bank listed twice.

Why we use it. The ledger can balance perfectly and still disagree with reality: a payment the bank never received, one it recorded for the wrong amount, or money that moved without Ledgerline knowing. Finance teams reconcile every day to catch these. It's the same work as ETL validation: two data sets, a key to join them on, and rules for what counts as a match.

How we use it. The matching is a pure function, reconcile, tested with unit tests up to 100,000 rows. An endpoint runs it for one day: it reads the bank's CSV file from S3, gets the payments Ledgerline settled that day from Postgres, compares the two, and writes a report back to S3. Chapter 20 of the field guide lets you run a reconciliation by hand.

How it works inside. The matching is a hash join. reconcile puts the bank's lines into a Map keyed by transfer id, then walks through the ledger once, finding each payment's line instantly. That's one pass over each list, so 100,000 payments take milliseconds. Comparing every payment with every line instead would mean ten billion comparisons. Real reconciliations also allow for tolerances, like fees or currency rounding, and for timing: a payment settled late in the day can show up in the next day's file. Run one by hand:

The bank's settlement file is CSV, with amounts in dollars, the way banks send them: 

transfer_id,amount,settled_on
9f1c2b7e-4a1d-4e0b-8c3f-5a6d7e8f9a0b,25.00,2031-05-01

Create src/domain/reconcile.ts:

src/domain/reconcile.ts
import { parseAmountToCents } from "./money";

export interface LedgerPayment {
  transferId: string;
  amountCents: number;
}

export interface BankLine {
  transferId: string;
  amountCents: number;
  line: number;
}

export type BreakType =
  | "missing_at_bank"
  | "unknown_to_ledger"
  | "amount_mismatch"
  | "duplicate_at_bank";

export interface Break {
  type: BreakType;
  transferId: string;
  ledgerAmountCents?: number;
  bankAmountCents?: number;
  line?: number;
}

export const SETTLEMENT_HEADER = "transfer_id,amount,settled_on";

// The bank's file is CSV with amounts in dollars, like "25.10". The Week 1
// function turns them into cents, so nothing here ever touches a float.
export function parseSettlementFile(csv: string): BankLine[] {
  const [header, ...rows] = csv.trim().split(/\r?\n/);
  if (header?.trim() !== SETTLEMENT_HEADER) {
    throw new Error(`Expected the header "${SETTLEMENT_HEADER}"`);
  }
  return rows
    .map((row, index) => ({ row, line: index + 2 }))
    .filter(({ row }) => row.trim() !== "")
    .map(({ row, line }) => {
      const [transferId, amount] = row.split(",");
      return {
        transferId: (transferId ?? "").trim(),
        amountCents: parseAmountToCents(amount ?? ""),
        line,
      };
    });
}

// Pure logic: two lists in, matches and breaks out. No S3, no database.
export function reconcile(
  ledger: LedgerPayment[],
  bank: BankLine[],
): { matched: number; breaks: Break[] } {
  const breaks: Break[] = [];

  // The first time the bank lists a payment counts; any repeat is a break.
  const bankById = new Map<string, BankLine>();
  for (const line of bank) {
    if (bankById.has(line.transferId)) {
      breaks.push({
        type: "duplicate_at_bank",
        transferId: line.transferId,
        bankAmountCents: line.amountCents,
        line: line.line,
      });
    } else {
      bankById.set(line.transferId, line);
    }
  }

  let matched = 0;
  const ledgerIds = new Set<string>();
  for (const payment of ledger) {
    ledgerIds.add(payment.transferId);
    const line = bankById.get(payment.transferId);
    if (!line) {
      breaks.push({
        type: "missing_at_bank",
        transferId: payment.transferId,
        ledgerAmountCents: payment.amountCents,
      });
    } else if (line.amountCents !== payment.amountCents) {
      breaks.push({
        type: "amount_mismatch",
        transferId: payment.transferId,
        ledgerAmountCents: payment.amountCents,
        bankAmountCents: line.amountCents,
        line: line.line,
      });
    } else {
      matched++;
    }
  }

  for (const line of bankById.values()) {
    if (!ledgerIds.has(line.transferId)) {
      breaks.push({
        type: "unknown_to_ledger",
        transferId: line.transferId,
        bankAmountCents: line.amountCents,
        line: line.line,
      });
    }
  }

  return { matched, breaks };
}

Create tests/unit/reconcile.test.ts:

tests/unit/reconcile.test.ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import {
  parseSettlementFile,
  reconcile,
  SETTLEMENT_HEADER,
} from "../../src/domain/reconcile";

const line = (transferId: string, amountCents: number, n = 2) => ({
  transferId,
  amountCents,
  line: n,
});

describe("reconcile", () => {
  it("matches a clean file with no breaks", () => {
    const result = reconcile(
      [
        { transferId: "a", amountCents: 2_500 },
        { transferId: "b", amountCents: 100 },
      ],
      [line("a", 2_500), line("b", 100, 3)],
    );
    expect(result).toEqual({ matched: 2, breaks: [] });
  });

  it("finds every kind of break at once", () => {
    const result = reconcile(
      [
        { transferId: "ok", amountCents: 100 },
        { transferId: "wrong", amountCents: 7_550 },
        { transferId: "twice", amountCents: 1_999 },
        { transferId: "missing", amountCents: 300_000 },
      ],
      [
        line("ok", 100, 2),
        line("wrong", 7_505, 3),
        line("twice", 1_999, 4),
        line("twice", 1_999, 5),
        line("stranger", 50_000, 6),
      ],
    );

    expect(result.matched).toBe(2);
    expect(result.breaks).toEqual(
      expect.arrayContaining([
        {
          type: "duplicate_at_bank",
          transferId: "twice",
          bankAmountCents: 1_999,
          line: 5,
        },
        {
          type: "amount_mismatch",
          transferId: "wrong",
          ledgerAmountCents: 7_550,
          bankAmountCents: 7_505,
          line: 3,
        },
        {
          type: "missing_at_bank",
          transferId: "missing",
          ledgerAmountCents: 300_000,
        },
        {
          type: "unknown_to_ledger",
          transferId: "stranger",
          bankAmountCents: 50_000,
          line: 6,
        },
      ]),
    );
    expect(result.breaks).toHaveLength(4);
  });

  it("handles 100,000 payments in well under a second", () => {
    const ledger = Array.from({ length: 100_000 }, (_, i) => ({
      transferId: `t${i}`,
      amountCents: i,
    }));
    const bank = ledger.map((p, i) => line(p.transferId, p.amountCents, i + 2));

    const started = performance.now();
    const result = reconcile(ledger, bank);

    expect(result.matched).toBe(100_000);
    expect(performance.now() - started).toBeLessThan(1_000);
  });
});

describe("parseSettlementFile", () => {
  it("turns dollar amounts into cents and skips blank lines", () => {
    const csv = `${SETTLEMENT_HEADER}\nabc,25.10,2031-05-01\n\ndef,0.99,2031-05-01\n`;
    expect(parseSettlementFile(csv)).toEqual([
      { transferId: "abc", amountCents: 2_510, line: 2 },
      { transferId: "def", amountCents: 99, line: 4 },
    ]);
  });

  it("refuses a file with the wrong header", () => {
    expect(() => parseSettlementFile("id,amount\nabc,1.00")).toThrow(
      "Expected the header",
    );
  });

  it("refuses an amount it can't read", () => {
    expect(() =>
      parseSettlementFile(`${SETTLEMENT_HEADER}\nabc,1.234,2031-05-01`),
    ).toThrow("Invalid amount");
  });
});

npm run test:unit

39 passed.

What the code does

  • parseSettlementFile checks the header, skips blank lines, and turns each dollar amount into cents with parseAmountToCents, the function you wrote in Week 1. Bank files are exactly why it exists.
  • reconcile indexes the bank's lines by transfer id with a Map, so each lookup is instant. Repeats in the bank file are duplicates. Then it walks the ledger's payments, and finally reports bank lines the ledger never mentioned.
  • The 100,000-row test proves the approach scales. A version that searched the whole bank list for every payment would take minutes on a real day's file.
  • Each break records the line number in the bank's file, so a person can find it.

Step 39: S3 and the reconciliation endpoint

About 90 minutes.

What, why and how: Amazon S3

What it is. S3, the Simple Storage Service, stores files, called objects, inside containers called buckets. Each object has a key, which is its full name, like settlements/2031-05-01.csv. The slashes look like folders, but they're just part of the name.

Why we use it. Banks and partners exchange files: settlement reports, statements, lists of returns. In most AWS systems, S3 is where those files land, and it can start code, such as a Lambda, the moment a file arrives. S3 is in Relay's stack.

How we use it. The bucket ledgerline-settlements lives in MiniStack, and npm run aws:setup creates it. src/storage.ts reads files with GetObjectCommand and writes them with PutObjectCommand. In the tests, the SettlementFiles helper plays the bank uploading its files. forcePathStyle: true makes the SDK use addresses like localhost:4566/bucket/key, which emulators expect.

How it works inside. S3 stores each object whole, under its key, in one flat list per bucket. There are no real folders, only keys that share a prefix like settlements/. A write replaces the whole object, and S3 guarantees that a read straight after a write sees the new version. A bucket can also send an event, for example to a Lambda, whenever an object is created, which is how the bank's file arriving could start a reconciliation by itself.

POST /reconciliations with a date reads settlements/<date>.csv from the bucket, finds the payments Ledgerline settled that day, runs reconcile, and writes the report to reports/<date>.json. 

npm install @aws-sdk/client-s3@3

Create src/storage.ts:

src/storage.ts
import {
  GetObjectCommand,
  PutObjectCommand,
  S3Client,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-s3";
import { awsConfig } from "./aws";

// Path-style addresses (localhost:4566/bucket/key) are what emulators expect.
export const s3 = new S3Client({ ...awsConfig, forcePathStyle: true });

export const SETTLEMENT_BUCKET =
  process.env.SETTLEMENT_BUCKET ?? "ledgerline-settlements";

/** Reads a file from the bucket as text, or null if it isn't there. */
export async function readText(key: string): Promise<string | null> {
  try {
    const result = await s3.send(
      new GetObjectCommand({ Bucket: SETTLEMENT_BUCKET, Key: key }),
    );
    return (await result.Body?.transformToString()) ?? "";
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as Error).name === "NoSuchKey") return null;
    throw error;
  }
}

export async function writeJson(key: string, value: unknown): Promise<void> {
  await s3.send(
    new PutObjectCommand({
      Bucket: SETTLEMENT_BUCKET,
      Key: key,
      Body: JSON.stringify(value, null, 2),
      ContentType: "application/json",
    }),
  );
}

Replace scripts/aws-setup.ts, which now creates the bucket too:

scripts/aws-setup.ts
import {
  CreateQueueCommand,
  GetQueueAttributesCommand,
  ListQueuesCommand,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-sqs";
import {
  CreateTableCommand,
  DynamoDBClient,
  UpdateTimeToLiveCommand,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb";
import { CreateBucketCommand } from "@aws-sdk/client-s3";
import { awsConfig } from "../src/aws";
import { IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE } from "../src/idempotency";
import { sqs, TRANSFERS_QUEUE } from "../src/queue";
import { s3, SETTLEMENT_BUCKET } from "../src/storage";

const dynamo = new DynamoDBClient(awsConfig);

const DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE = `${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}-dlq`;
const INSPECT_QUEUE = `${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}-inspect`;

// MiniStack can take a few seconds to start, especially in CI.
async function waitForMiniStack() {
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 30; attempt++) {
    try {
      await sqs.send(new ListQueuesCommand({}));
      return;
    } catch {
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
    }
  }
  throw new Error("MiniStack didn't answer on port 4566. Is it running?");
}

async function setup() {
  await waitForMiniStack();

  // The dead-letter queue first, because the main queue points at it.
  const dlq = await sqs.send(
    new CreateQueueCommand({ QueueName: DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE }),
  );
  const { Attributes } = await sqs.send(
    new GetQueueAttributesCommand({
      QueueUrl: dlq.QueueUrl,
      AttributeNames: ["QueueArn"],
    }),
  );

  // After 3 failed receives, SQS moves a message to the dead-letter queue.
  await sqs.send(
    new CreateQueueCommand({
      QueueName: TRANSFERS_QUEUE,
      Attributes: {
        VisibilityTimeout: "30",
        RedrivePolicy: JSON.stringify({
          deadLetterTargetArn: Attributes?.QueueArn,
          maxReceiveCount: 3,
        }),
      },
    }),
  );

  // A queue nobody reads from. Tests point a copy of the API at it, so they
  // can inspect messages before the processor takes them.
  await sqs.send(new CreateQueueCommand({ QueueName: INSPECT_QUEUE }));

  console.log(
    `Queues ready: ${TRANSFERS_QUEUE}, ${DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE} and ${INSPECT_QUEUE}`,
  );

  // The idempotency table: one item per key, found by its "pk" attribute.
  try {
    await dynamo.send(
      new CreateTableCommand({
        TableName: IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE,
        AttributeDefinitions: [{ AttributeName: "pk", AttributeType: "S" }],
        KeySchema: [{ AttributeName: "pk", KeyType: "HASH" }],
        BillingMode: "PAY_PER_REQUEST",
      }),
    );
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as Error).name !== "ResourceInUseException") throw error;
  }
  // Items delete themselves once their expiresAt time has passed.
  try {
    await dynamo.send(
      new UpdateTimeToLiveCommand({
        TableName: IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE,
        TimeToLiveSpecification: { Enabled: true, AttributeName: "expiresAt" },
      }),
    );
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as Error).name !== "ValidationException") throw error;
  }
  console.log(`Table ready: ${IDEMPOTENCY_TABLE}`);

  // Where the bank drops settlement files, and reports are written back.
  try {
    await s3.send(new CreateBucketCommand({ Bucket: SETTLEMENT_BUCKET }));
  } catch (error) {
    const name = (error as Error).name;
    if (name !== "BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou" && name !== "BucketAlreadyExists") {
      throw error;
    }
  }
  console.log(`Bucket ready: ${SETTLEMENT_BUCKET}`);
}

setup().catch((error) => {
  console.error("AWS setup failed:", error);
  process.exitCode = 1;
});

Create src/reconciliation.ts:

src/reconciliation.ts
import { pool } from "./db";
import {
  parseSettlementFile,
  reconcile,
  type BankLine,
  type LedgerPayment,
} from "./domain/reconcile";
import { AppError } from "./errors";
import { toCents } from "./ledger";
import { readText, writeJson } from "./storage";

// Payments whose settlement Ledgerline recorded on a given day, in UTC.
async function settledPaymentsOn(date: string): Promise<LedgerPayment[]> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<{ id: string; amount_cents: string }>(
    `SELECT payment.id, payment.amount_cents
     FROM transfers payment
     JOIN transfers settlement ON settlement.settles_transfer_id = payment.id
     WHERE settlement.kind = 'settlement' AND settlement.created_at::date = $1::date`,
    [date],
  );
  return rows.map((row) => ({
    transferId: row.id,
    amountCents: toCents(row.amount_cents),
  }));
}

// Reads the bank's file for a day, compares it with the ledger, and writes
// the result back to the bucket as a report.
export async function runReconciliation(date: string) {
  const csv = await readText(`settlements/${date}.csv`);
  if (csv === null) {
    throw new AppError(404, "file_not_found", `No settlement file for ${date}`);
  }

  let bank: BankLine[];
  try {
    bank = parseSettlementFile(csv);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new AppError(
      422,
      "invalid_settlement_file",
      (error as Error).message,
    );
  }

  const result = reconcile(await settledPaymentsOn(date), bank);
  const report = { date, ...result, createdAt: new Date().toISOString() };
  await writeJson(`reports/${date}.json`, report);
  return report;
}
